cues.zh: 我觉得从伦理角度讲，你有义务告诉我们那到底是谁。

cues.en: It's one of the Frontier Labs CEOs, and it's not Dario.
cues.zh: 他是前沿实验室的几位CEO之一，不是达里奥。

cues.en: The Dario CEO.
cues.zh: 那就是 Frontier Labs 的CEO，不是达里奥。

cues.en: But I don't know.
cues.zh: 但我不知道。

cues.en: These things are Chinese whispers, so I don't know.
cues.zh: 这些消息都是零散流传的，所以我也不清楚。

cues.en: I think that you can actually get this info firsthand.
cues.zh: 我觉得你其实可以直接获得这些信息。

cues.en: Elon Musk is clear about this.
cues.zh: 埃隆·马斯克对此态度很明确。

cues.en: He did an interview last year where he was like, I didn't want to get into this AI stuff because I thought I was too dangerous.
cues.zh: 他去年接受采访时说过，他原本不想涉足人工智能领域，因为觉得自己太危险了。

cues.en: But then I realized it was going to happen with or without me.
cues.zh: 但后来他意识到，不管自己愿不愿意，这件事都会发生。

cues.en: And I decided I would rather be a participant than a spectator.
cues.zh: 于是他决定要做参与者，而不是旁观者。

cues.en: Because Google said that they were going to pursue it and he didn't trust Google.
cues.zh: 因为谷歌表示要继续推进这项技术，而他并不信任谷歌。

cues.en: That's right.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: You know, you can see in the leaked, sorry, not leaked, the open AI emails that came out during the discovery and court cases.
cues.zh: 你知道的，在调查和诉讼期间公开的那些人工智能相关邮件里，就能看到这些内容。

cues.en: You can see these guys discussing.
cues.zh: 可以看到这些人正在讨论相关事宜。

cues.en: in the threads.
cues.zh: 在这些讨论中。

cues.en: Like, we need to make sure that we and our nonprofit at OpenAI control this instead of, you know, the people at Google controlling this.
cues.zh: 我们得确保由我们以及OpenAI旗下的非营利组织来掌控这一切，而不是让谷歌那边的人来掌控。

cues.en: And then, of course, you know, OpenAI was founded as a nonprofit and then it was sort of changed into a for-profit and there's much debate about how much of that nonprofit money was in
cues.zh: 当然，OpenAI最初是作为非营利组织成立的，后来某种程度上变成了营利性机构，关于有多少非营利资金被

cues.en: some sense stolen.
cues.zh: 在某种意义上被挪用了，存在着很多争论。

cues.en: And so, you know, Elon also left because he thought they weren't going to be good stewards.
cues.zh: 因此，埃隆也离开了，因为他觉得他们不会做好管理。

cues.en: Dario also left to create Anthropic because, so, you know, in some sense, all of these AI labs except The Google one that came out of Demis Hassabis' original
cues.zh: 达里奥也离开去创建Anthropic了，因为从某种意义上说，除了源自德米斯·哈萨比斯最初

cues.en: startup.
cues.zh: 创办的那家公司之外的所有AI实验室，

cues.en: All of the other AI labs exist because none of the CEOs trust the other guys.
cues.zh: 其他所有的AI实验室存在都是因为这些CEO们互不信任。

cues.en: None of the CEOs think the other guy should be the one holding the leash on the superintelligence.
cues.zh: 没有一位CEO认为应该由其他人来掌控超级智能的发展。

cues.en: None of them trust each other.
cues.zh: 他们彼此之间都不信任。

cues.en: I just trust one fewer.
cues.zh: 我就少信任一个人而已。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: What are your closing thoughts, Andy?
cues.zh: 安迪，你最后想说什么？

cues.en: We're living in really interesting times.
cues.zh: 我们正生活在一个极其有趣的时代。

cues.en: And I think you guys have made a very good argument that these systems are demonstrating new
cues.zh: 而且我认为你们已经提出了非常有力的论据，说明这些系统正在展现出新的

cues.en: capabilities, which are very powerful and which demand a response.
cues.zh: 能力，这些能力极为强大，因此需要我们做出回应。

cues.en: I'm much more confident in our ability to rise to that challenge than you are.
cues.zh: 相比你，我对我们有能力应对这一挑战要有信心得多。

cues.en: But you accept the existential risk.
cues.zh: 但你承认其中存在生存风险。

cues.en: Let me try to say it again.
cues.zh: 让我再试着说一遍。

cues.en: I appreciate that there are new harms we haven't seen before that come along with a technology that's this dogged,
cues.zh: 我明白，随着这种顽强、

cues.en: tenacious, agentic, you know, deceptive.
cues.zh: 坚韧、具有自主性且还会欺骗人的技术出现，确实会出现我们以前从未见过的新的危害。

cues.en: I think that's the right word for it.
cues.zh: 我觉得用‘欺骗性’来形容它再合适不过了。

cues.en: I agree with that.
cues.zh: 我同意这一点。

cues.en: I am much more optimistic about our ability to respond effectively to that new challenge out there in the world than I think my
cues.zh: 相比你，我对我们有能力有效应对世界上出现的这一新挑战要乐观得多。

cues.en: two colleagues are.
cues.zh: 有两位同事在场。

cues.en: And would you still be at 0%?
cues.zh: 那你的比例还是0%吗？

cues.en: My prior has not shifted during this meeting.
cues.zh: 在这次会议期间我的立场没有改变。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: I think we've spent an alarming amount of time not talking about the actual harms of AI as it is today.
cues.zh: 我觉得我们花了太多时间，却不去讨论当前人工智能所带来的实际危害。

cues.en: I think these are necessary conversations to have.
cues.zh: 我认为这些是必须进行的对话。

cues.en: I think we should talk about the fact that Amazon, Microsoft, Google, Oracle are helping power these hacks, that Sam Altman and Dario Amadei have overseen companies
cues.zh: 我觉得我们应该谈谈亚马逊、微软、谷歌、甲骨文都在为这些黑客行为提供支持，萨姆·奥尔特曼和达里奥·阿马德伊曾监管过那些

cues.en: that have done what is tantamount to felony hacking, that we are not having discussions about how to stop this today, but what we might stop tomorrow.
cues.zh: 实施了近乎重罪级别黑客行为的公司，而我们现在没有讨论如何立即制止这一切，只是在考虑明天能阻止什么。

cues.en: And I think in general, we also need to worry about the financials, which have not come up at all.
cues.zh: 总体而言，我们还需要关注财务问题，不过这个问题至今完全未被提及。

cues.en: But if there is an industry slowdown, how do you deal
cues.zh: 但如果行业出现放缓，要如何应对

cues.en: deal with the $1.3 trillion of compute commitments.
cues.zh: 如何处理那1.3万亿美元的算力投入？

cues.en: All of these are very real things that will have very real consequences very, very soon.
cues.zh: 所有这些都是非常现实的问题，很快就会带来极其严重的后果。

cues.en: But, and I understand why, and it's necessary to discuss what we do around AI.
cues.zh: 但是，我明白原因，我们确实有必要探讨在人工智能领域该采取哪些措施。

cues.en: The actual regulatory thing we need to do today is cut off the compute, slow down these labs fully.
cues.zh: 我们今天真正需要做的监管措施，就是切断计算资源，彻底放缓这些实验室的运作速度。

cues.en: And I don't care about China here.
cues.zh: 我这里并不关心中国的问题。

cues.en: What are they going to do?
cues.zh: 他们打算做什么？

cues.en: Distill a model like they have the whole time?
cues.zh: 像一直以来那样继续训练模型吗？

cues.en: They are capped on our progress.
cues.zh: 他们在限制我们的进展。

cues.en: So the biggest thing to do is to slow down.
cues.zh: 所以最要紧的就是放慢速度。

cues.en: And also, It's time to start arresting people.
cues.zh: 另外，现在也是该开始逮捕相关人员的时机了。

cues.en: They did felony hacking.
cues.zh: 他们犯了严重的黑客罪。

cues.en: Someone's got to go to prison.
cues.zh: 总得有人进监狱。

cues.en: We need responsibility and accountability for these companies.
cues.zh: 这些公司必须承担相应的责任与义务。

cues.en: And as long as we don't have it, we may as well not have had any discussion about safety because we're not doing anything.
cues.zh: 只要没有这些，那我们谈论安全问题也就毫无意义，因为根本没有任何实际行动。

cues.en: Do you accept that there's an existential risk?
cues.zh: 你承认存在生存风险吗？

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Absolutely.
cues.zh: 当然。

cues.en: We have the largest companies in the world doing what I think we can all agree are extremely reckless experiments using hundreds of billions of dollars of infrastructure.
cues.zh: 世界上规模最大的企业正在开展我认为大家都会认同的极其鲁莽的实验，它们动用了数千亿美元的基础设施。

cues.en: And they are building more infrastructure around the world very slowly to do more of these chaotic experiments.
cues.zh: 而且它们还在全球极其缓慢地建设更多基础设施，以便继续进行这些混乱的实验。

cues.en: We must rein them in.
cues.zh: 我们必须对它们加以约束。

cues.en: This does not mean that large language models are conscious or able to do things that people have been promising.
cues.zh: 这并不意味着大型语言模型具有意识，或者能够做到人们所宣称的那些事。

cues.en: Indeed, they may.
cues.zh: 事实上，它们或许可以做到。

cues.en: I don't think they will lead to what you're talking about.
cues.zh: 我不认为它们会带来你所说的那种情况。

cues.en: That doesn't mean there aren't real harms, but these are real harms caused.
cues.zh: 但这并不代表不存在真正的危害，这些危害确实存在。

cues.en: by very specific parties allowed to run rampant in the scourge of neoliberalism.
cues.zh: 它们是由在新自由主义浪潮中肆意妄为的某些特定势力造成的。

cues.en: What's your percentage?
cues.zh: 你的比例是多少？

cues.en: I mean, what are we talking about here?
cues.zh: 我的意思是，我们这里到底在讨论什么？

cues.en: Do you think there's a more than 10% chance of existential harm?
cues.zh: 你认为出现存在性危害的概率会超过10%吗？

cues.en: Wasn't it within 10 years or something?
cues.zh: 不是说在10年之内之类的事情吗？

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Not 10%.
I mean, 1%.
cues.zh: 我是说，1%。

cues.en: But let me just be clear about what that means.
cues.zh: 不过让我先把这到底意味着什么说清楚。

cues.en: Do I think that unrestrained LLM use connected to massive amounts of infrastructure could lead to actually a power system going down?
cues.zh: 我是否认为，如果无节制地使用大型语言模型并且依赖大量基础设施，真的可能会导致电力系统瘫痪？

cues.en: Absolutely.
cues.zh: 当然会。

cues.en: We had Knight Capital, what, like 13, 14 years ago.
cues.zh: 13、14年前不是有过Knight Capital的那次事件吗？

cues.en: I could see someone being dumb enough to connect that to financial accounts.
cues.zh: 我能想象会有人蠢到把那和金融账户联系起来。

cues.en: Human error led with this chaotic software we use is a danger.
cues.zh: 我们使用的这种混乱的软件，再加上人为失误，确实很危险。

cues.en: I will directionally agree with arresting everyone.
cues.zh: 在逮捕所有相关人员这一点上，我基本同意。

cues.en: But don't build general superintelligence.
cues.zh: 但不要去研发通用的超级智能。

cues.en: If you're working at one of those labs, quit today.
cues.zh: 如果你在那些实验室工作，今天就辞职吧。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。

cues.en: The people at these labs really do believe this poses an extinction threat.
cues.zh: 这些实验室里的人真的认为这会带来物种灭绝的威胁。

cues.en: I think our response as a society cannot be, please continue, we hope you'll fail.
cues.zh: 我认为我们社会应有的反应不应该是‘请继续，希望你们失败’。

cues.en: And our response as a society cannot be...
cues.zh: 我们社会应有的反应也不可能是……

cues.en: let it rip in a giant competitive race that you yourselves are saying you don't want to be in, we are forcing you to go ahead because
cues.zh: 任由它在一场你们自己也说不想参与的激烈竞争中被放任发展，而我们却强迫你们继续前进，只因为

cues.en: of the boogeyman of China.
cues.zh: 害怕中国的威胁。

cues.en: We have seen the people at these companies say that we need to develop the tools to pace the frontier, which is corporate speak for
cues.zh: 我们看到这些公司的人声称我们需要开发工具来引领技术前沿，用企业术语来说就是

cues.en: this is going too fast for us to get a handle on things.
cues.zh: 发展速度太快，我们根本来不及掌控局面。

cues.en: We need, like, these people believe it.
cues.zh: 我们需要……这些人就是这么认为的。

cues.en: They believe they're gambling with your lives.
cues.zh: 他们觉得自己在拿你们的生命冒险。

cues.en: What has changed is that the rest of the world is starting to notice.
cues.zh: 变化在于，全世界其他地方也开始注意到这个问题了。

cues.en: And that's what gives us a moment of hope.
cues.zh: 而这正是给我们带来希望的时刻。

cues.en: Trump this week was asked about the threat of AI, and this was his response.
cues.zh: 本周特朗普被问及人工智能带来的威胁，他的回答就是如此。

cues.en: The case scenario with AI is that the robots, the machinery learns to, obviously it thinks for itself, that's what it does, and that could
cues.zh: 关于人工智能的设想是，那些机器人、机器会学会独立思考，而这正是它们的功能，而这种情况就有可能

cues.en: turn against humanity.
cues.zh: 反过来威胁人类。

cues.en: Do we have the guardrails?
cues.zh: 我们有相应的约束措施吗？

cues.en: It's going to be fine.
cues.zh: 一切都会没事的。

cues.en: We'll always have something to stop them, right?
cues.zh: 我们总会有办法阻止它们，对吧？

cues.en: We'll have a little gear.
cues.zh: 我们会设置一些限制机制。

cues.en: I really don't like that robot.
cues.zh: 我真的很讨厌那个机器人。

cues.en: We'll stop it.
cues.zh: 我们会阻止它的。

cues.en: You're laughing, but this is a state of the art in AI safety right now.
cues.zh: 你在笑，但这可是目前人工智能安全领域的最先进技术。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: This is the device we have.
cues.zh: 这就是我们现有的设备。

cues.en: That's the best we got.
cues.zh: 这是我们能做到的最好成果了。

cues.en: For anyone that couldn't hear that, Trump went, we'll always be fine.
cues.zh: 给没听清的人说明一下，特朗普说我们会一直没事的。

cues.en: We'll have something to control it.
cues.zh: 我们会找到办法来控制它。

cues.en: And then he did a little gun finger and he went, boom, I don't like that robot.
cues.zh: 然后他还比了个开枪的手势，接着说‘砰’，我不喜欢那个机器人。

cues.en: I don't like Sammy.
cues.zh: 我不喜欢萨米。

cues.en: If you don't laugh.
cues.zh: 如果你不笑的话。

cues.en: I would say that the reason humanity...
cues.zh: 我想说人类……

cues.en: always has something to stop a problem is because people notice a problem and build what it takes to have something to stop a problem, which I think you'd agree with.
cues.zh: 总能找到办法解决问题的原因，是人们察觉到问题后就会打造出相应的工具来解决问题，我想这一点你应该也认同。

cues.en: I am not here saying we're going to die.
cues.zh: 我并不是说我们就要完蛋了。

cues.en: I'm here saying, if you look at the technology, if you look at what it's doing now, if you look at what the experts who
cues.zh: 我来这里是想说，只要看看这项技术，看看它目前的运作情况，再听听开发它的专家们对自己所担忧问题的看法，就会明白我们必须挺身应对这一挑战。

cues.en: are building it are saying about their own fears, you see that we need to rise to this occasion.
cues.zh: 那些正在开发这项技术的人也谈到了他们自身的恐惧，由此可见我们确实需要迎接这一挑战。

cues.en: You said you trust humanity to rise to the occasion.
cues.zh: 您说过您相信人类有能力挺身应对这一挑战。

cues.en: I sure hope we can.
cues.zh: 我真心希望我们真的能做到。

cues.en: I think that rising to this occasion is going to mean that nobody races towards superintelligence because we have no idea how
cues.zh: 我认为要应对这一挑战，就意味着不能有人急于追求超级智能，因为我们根本不知道该

cues.en: to get that right.
cues.zh: 如何正确实现它。

cues.en: And, you know, finally, the world is starting to notice that it's an extinction threat.
cues.zh: 而且，您也知道，如今全世界终于开始意识到它是一种可能导致物种灭绝的威胁。

cues.en: Thank you, Nate, Roman, Ed, Andy.
cues.zh: 谢谢，Nate、Roman、Ed、Andy。

cues.en: Super appreciate you.
cues.zh: 非常感谢你们。

cues.en: All of your books will be linked below in the description and on screen.
cues.zh: 所有相关的书籍链接都会放在下方的描述中以及屏幕上。

cues.en: Let's see what happens.
cues.zh: 让我们看看接下来会发生什么。

cues.en: We'll convene again.
cues.zh: 我们以后还会再聚在一起。

cues.en: Thank you so much.
cues.zh: 非常感谢您。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢您。

cues.en: YouTube have this new crazy algorithm where they know exactly what video you would like to watch next based on AI and all of your viewing behavior.
cues.zh: YouTube现在用了一种全新的疯狂算法，它能通过人工智能以及您所有的观看行为，精准判断出您接下来想看哪个视频。

cues.en: And the algorithm says that this video is the perfect video for you.
cues.zh: 而这个算法会判定，这个视频正是适合您的最佳选择。

cues.en: It's different for everybody looking right now.
cues.zh: 目前对不同的人来说，推荐的内容各不相同。

cues.en: Check this video out.
cues.zh: 去看看这个视频吧。

cues.en: I bet you, you might love it.
cues.zh: 我敢打赌，您一定会喜欢它。

material.title: CEO 日记 · 安迪·加尔平谈减脂
material.subtitle: The Diary of a CEO · Fat Loss Scientist： It’s Easy To Lose Weight, But Here’s Why You WON’T Do It! ｜ Dr Andy Galpin · 英文自动字幕

cues.en: Everything you see on this table has strong scientific evidence that it will help us sleep.
cues.zh: 这张表格里列出的所有物品，都有充分的科学依据表明它们有助于我们入睡。

cues.en: So we're going to dig into all of those in great detail.
cues.zh: 因此我们会对这些物品进行极其详细的探讨。

cues.en: So the first one is a really good one.
cues.zh: 第一个就是非常不错的选择。

cues.en: Kiwis.
cues.zh: 猕猴桃。

cues.en: Kiwis?
cues.zh: 猕猴桃？

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: So there's been good studies on them.
cues.zh: 关于猕猴桃已经有不少不错的研究结果。

cues.en: So if you have two to three kiwis before bed, you'll see people sleeping better.
cues.zh: 如果你在睡前吃两到三个猕猴桃，就会发现人们的睡眠质量会更好。

cues.en: Next on our list is sleep divorce.
cues.zh: 接下来我们要讲的是睡眠分离现象。

cues.en: People generally don't sleep as well when you're in the same bed as others.
cues.zh: 当与他人同床共枕时，人们的睡眠质量通常会下降。

cues.en: Next.
cues.zh: 下一个。

cues.en: What about this?
cues.zh: 这个怎么样？

cues.en: This has more evidence than the rest of these things combined.
cues.zh: 相比其他所有因素加起来，这一项的证据更为充分。

cues.en: And it is effective.
cues.zh: 而且它的效果也很显著。

cues.en: Another one to think about is sound.
cues.zh: 另一个需要考虑的因素是声音。

cues.zh: 所以在接下来的几个小时里，我对即将说出的每一句话都会格外谨慎。

cues.zh: 我不想引发健康焦虑。

cues.en: I don't want you to be so terrified to touch a receipt that it sends you into a three-day tailspin.
cues.zh: 我也不想让你因为看到一张收据就惊恐万分，进而陷入三天的情绪低谷。

cues.en: Anytime we're talking about health or performance, we want to run the spectrum of disease, to optimization.
cues.zh: 每当我们谈论健康或表现时，都需要把讨论范围从疾病到最佳状态全面涵盖。

cues.en: We should not be playing around with optimization performance if we're in the presence of a medical disease.
cues.zh: 如果已经患有疾病，我们就绝不该再去追求性能优化了。

cues.en: And why I say that is sleep is probably the biggest place of clinical disease that exists that no one knows about.
cues.zh: 我之所以这么说，是因为睡眠问题很可能是目前存在却无人知晓的最大临床疾病隐患。

cues.en: Somewhere in the neighborhood of 70 to 80% of people who have clinical sleep apnea will go undiagnosed.
cues.zh: 大约70%到80%的临床睡眠呼吸暂停患者都得不到诊断。

cues.en: Wow.
cues.zh: 哇。

cues.en: If that existed for a broken bone, right?
cues.zh: 要是骨折也会这样吧？

cues.en: If that existed for diabetes, you'd be like insane.
cues.zh: 要是糖尿病也是这种情况，那可就太离谱了。

cues.en: It gets worse.
cues.zh: 情况更糟糕。

cues.en: 50%, depending on which study you look at, of athletes have a clinical sleep disorder.
cues.zh: 根据不同的研究，有50%的运动员存在临床睡眠障碍。

cues.en: For women, it's somewhere in the neighborhood of 90% to 95% of women that have clinical sleep apnea will go
cues.zh: 对于女性而言，大约90%到95%的临床睡眠呼吸暂停女性都

cues.en: undiagnosed.
cues.zh: 无法得到诊断。

cues.en: Why?
cues.zh: 为什么？

cues.en: If you were to look at me and you would say, if I said, Stephen, you think I have apnea?
cues.zh: 如果你看着我问，斯蒂芬，你觉得我有睡眠呼吸暂停吗？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不会。

cues.en: No, right?
cues.zh: 不会吧？

cues.en: If I were to bring in a whole table of 10 people and I said, pick the person in here least likely to have sleep apnea, you'd find the smallest girl.
cues.zh: 如果我请来一整桌10个人，然后问谁最不可能患有睡眠呼吸暂停，你们会选那个最瘦的小女孩。

cues.en: True.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: You don't think about apnea as something that can happen unless you're big and fat.
cues.zh: 除非人又胖又大，否则人们不会想到自己会患上睡眠呼吸暂停。

cues.en: Women also are less likely than men to complain.
cues.zh: 女性比男性更少抱怨这个问题。

cues.en: They're less likely to think about it as an anatomical issue.
cues.zh: 她们不太可能将其视为解剖结构上的问题。

cues.en: They're going to charge it to hormones, to their menstrual cycle, to their cognitive load, to the demands that it is to be mom.
cues.zh: 她们会把原因归咎于激素、月经周期、认知负担，或是作为母亲所承受的压力。

cues.en: All these are true, by the way.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这些说法都是对的。

cues.en: It is also, in the same point, true.
cues.zh: 从同一个角度来说，这也是事实。

cues.en: You could have apnea that has nothing to do with body composition.
cues.zh: 存在与体脂率毫无关系的睡眠呼吸暂停。

cues.en: And let's define apnea for a second.
cues.zh: 那我们先来简单定义一下睡眠呼吸暂停。

cues.en: you stop breathing at night.
cues.zh: 你在夜间会停止呼吸。

cues.en: And that wakes you up?
cues.zh: 这会把你吵醒吗？

cues.en: Sometimes it doesn't.
cues.zh: 有时候不会。

cues.en: That's the problem, is it won't necessarily wake you up, but it is deleterious to your health.
cues.zh: 问题就在这里，它不一定会把你吵醒，但会对健康造成危害。

cues.en: It's highly associated with consequences from long-term death risk to short-term cognitive function, emotion, mood regulation,
cues.zh: 它与诸多不良后果密切相关，从长期的生命风险到短期的认知功能、情绪与情绪调节能力，

cues.en: performance, recovery, metabolic health.
cues.zh: 还有运动表现、恢复能力以及代谢健康都会受到影响。

cues.en: It's really, really nasty.
cues.zh: 这真的非常糟糕。

cues.en: In fact, one of the larger things that can go wrong in your health is not breathing at night.
cues.zh: 事实上，健康方面可能出现的最严重问题之一就是夜间呼吸停止。

cues.en: This might be a silly question, but does sleep apnea disrupt your...
cues.zh: 这可能是个愚蠢的问题，但睡眠呼吸暂停会干扰你的……

cues.en: Sleep.
cues.zh: 睡眠吗？

cues.en: It can.
cues.zh: 会的。

cues.en: So it doesn't always?
cues.zh: 所以并不总是这样？

cues.en: Doesn't always.
cues.zh: 并不总是这样。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: This is why do you think it's so poorly diagnosed?
cues.zh: 这就是为什么你觉得这种病很难被诊断出来的原因吗？

cues.en: So the classic giveaways, if you were that person who wakes up four counties because you snore so loud, snoring doesn't necessarily mean you have sleep apnea,
cues.zh: 所以那些典型的迹象是，如果你因为打鼾声音太大而不得不在凌晨四点醒来，打鼾并不一定意味着你患有睡眠呼吸暂停症，

cues.en: but it's a really strong indicator.
cues.zh: 但它确实是一个很强的提示信号。

cues.en: That's one form of it.
cues.zh: 那是其中一种表现形式。

cues.en: So apnea happens for a bunch of different reasons.
cues.zh: 睡眠呼吸暂停症是由很多不同原因引起的。

cues.en: More evidence recently has suggested like neck size was this kind of original thing that we say like a big neck is just a problem.
cues.zh: 最近有更多证据表明，颈部尺寸原本并不是我们所说的‘大脖子就是问题’的那种唯一因素。

cues.en: Doesn't look like that's as true, but certainly it is true.
cues.zh: 看起来情况并非完全如此，但这一点确实是事实。

cues.en: As you increase obesity rates, you'll see an increase in apnea as well.
cues.zh: 随着肥胖率的上升，睡眠呼吸暂停症的发病率也会随之上升。

cues.en: So what's happening here is now you're talking about, I'll call it anatomical or physical, like something physically is landing on your neck and your tongue and your throat,
cues.zh: 现在的情况是，我们可以从解剖学或生理学的角度来解释，比如有某些物理性因素压在你的颈部、舌头和喉咙上，

cues.en: your larynx and esophagus, and it's stopping your breathing.
cues.zh: 还有喉部和食道，从而阻碍你的呼吸。

cues.en: And why this matters is when you're standing here or sitting here in this chair, you're in this vertical position.
cues.zh: 之所以这很重要，是因为当你站在这里或坐在这把椅子上时，你是处于垂直状态的。

cues.en: And as you go and lay down, anatomy shifts.
cues.zh: 而当你躺下时，身体的解剖结构就会发生变化。

cues.en: You also have a lot of research showing that the larger the human being, the more fluid they have, which is pretty normal, right?
cues.zh: 还有大量研究表明，人的体型越大，体内所含的体液就越多，这很正常，对吧？

cues.en: So a person who's twice your size will have...
cues.zh: 所以一个体型是你的两倍的人，其体内...

cues.en: Twice the amount of water in their body that you do.
cues.zh: 所含的水量也会是你的两倍。

cues.en: Imagine if you had, I mean, we'll take this beverage right here.
cues.zh: 想象一下，我们就拿这里的这种饮料来举例。

cues.en: Why do you have red wine?
cues.zh: 为什么要放红酒？

cues.en: Well, anyways, we'll come back in case you get thirsty.
cues.zh: 不管怎样，我们先放回去，免得你口渴。

cues.en: So you see the water is sitting vertically, right?
cues.zh: 可以看到水是垂直放置的，对吧？

cues.en: If I were to shift this cup horizontally, the water would shift and it would balance horizontally to where the gap in the air would be on the top, right?
cues.zh: 如果我把这个杯子水平移动，水也会随之移动，并在水平方向上找到平衡，让空气间隙位于顶部，对吧？

cues.en: That happens in your body.
cues.zh: 你的身体里也会出现这种情况。

cues.en: So imagine this top piece start up here.
cues.zh: 现在想象一下，最上面的那部分从这里开始上升。

cues.en: That's your neck.
cues.zh: 那是你的脖子。

cues.en: Now when you lay down, your neck is over here, and I would tip this over, but it would spill everywhere.
cues.zh: 当你躺下时，脖子会在这个位置，我本想把这个倒过来，但液体就会流得到处都是。

cues.en: That fluid then shifts up into your neck.
cues.zh: 然后那些液体就会向上流到你的脖子里。

cues.en: So it's not even necessarily a physical size thing, but it's the fluid associated with being a larger human being that the fluid shift can happen.
cues.zh: 所以这并不一定与身体尺寸有关，而是与体型较大所伴随的体液流动有关。

cues.en: What we're now finding is a whole series of other types of apnea.
cues.zh: 我们现在发现还有许多其他类型的呼吸暂停现象。

cues.en: Now there are neural causes to it.
cues.zh: 这类问题有神经方面的原因。

cues.en: There are environmental causes.
cues.zh: 也有环境方面的原因。

cues.en: There are positional causes.
cues.zh: 还有体位方面的原因。

cues.en: And so as a classic example to round the story out, Traditionally, if you're told you have apnea, you're going to be given one of about three choices.
cues.zh: 作为总结的一个典型例子，传统上，如果被告知患有呼吸暂停，通常只有三种选择。

cues.en: Medication, what's called a CPAP device, right?
cues.zh: 药物治疗，也就是所谓的CPAP呼吸机，对吧？

cues.en: So that's the big like Darth Vader breathing machine, or potentially what's called an oral appliance.
cues.zh: 那就是那种像达斯·维达用的那种大型呼吸机，或者也可能是所谓的口腔矫治器。

cues.en: It's a mouthpiece that kind of repositions your jaw and neck.
cues.zh: 那是一种能够调整下颌和颈部位置的牙套。

cues.en: I'm for all of those treatments.
cues.zh: 我支持所有这些治疗方法。

cues.en: Why they all have such low success rates is because they're given out generically.
cues.zh: 它们的成功率之所以如此之低，是因为它们被随意地开给患者。

cues.en: You come in, you have apnea, you get the same stuff.
cues.zh: 患者前来就诊时患有睡眠呼吸暂停，得到的却还是同样的治疗。

cues.en: now what the field is moving towards is precision.
cues.zh: 目前这个领域正在朝着精准化方向发展。

cues.en: And saying you have this specific type of apnea, an oral appliance won't help here.
cues.zh: 如果明确是某种特定类型的睡眠呼吸暂停，口腔矫治器是不起作用的。

cues.en: You actually need this surgical intervention.
cues.zh: 这种情况下实际上需要手术干预。

cues.en: I was looking at some of the data here and it says that sleep apnea is very common globally, much more common than I expected.
cues.zh: 我看了这里的一些数据，显示睡眠呼吸暂停在全球范围内非常普遍，比我预想的还要常见得多。

cues.en: It says men who are middle-aged have a 24 to 34% prevalence of apnea.
cues.zh: 数据显示，中年男性的睡眠呼吸暂停患病率为24%到34%。

cues.en: Women, 9 to 17%.
cues.zh: 女性则为9%到17%。

cues.en: At seniors, 30 to 60%.
cues.zh: 老年人则达到30%到60%。

cues.en: That's right.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: Postmenopausal women, 25%.
cues.zh: 绝经后的女性患病率为25%。

cues.en: So yeah, rough numbers.
cues.zh: 大致就是这些数字吧。

cues.en: That means that listening now, if you're a middle-aged man listening, if there's three of you listening right now, one of you statistically might have apnea.
cues.zh: 也就是说，正在听讲的各位如果是中年男性，而且此刻有三人一起听，从统计上看其中一人可能患有睡眠呼吸暂停症。

cues.en: Now that's clinical sleep apnea.
cues.zh: 那指的是临床型的睡眠呼吸暂停症。

cues.en: That doesn't even count subclinical.
cues.zh: 还没算上亚临床型的。

cues.en: And if you're a senior listening now, which is 65 years older.
cues.zh: 而如果是65岁及以上的老年人正在听讲，

cues.en: There's a 30% to 60% chance.
cues.zh: 患病几率在30%到60%之间。

cues.en: Wow.
cues.zh: 哇。

cues.en: Depending on some numbers you see, Stephen, you'll see a billion people across the globe.
cues.zh: 根据某些数据，斯蒂芬，全球会有十亿人受到影响。

cues.en: Yeah, that's what it says.
cues.zh: 没错，资料上是这么写的。

cues.en: It says a billion people.
cues.zh: 上面确实写着十亿人。

cues.en: Now, that's only apnea.
cues.zh: 那只是指睡眠呼吸暂停症。

cues.en: That's not insomnia.
cues.zh: 这还不包括失眠症。

cues.en: That's not all the other sleep disorders.
cues.zh: 那还不是其他所有的睡眠障碍。

cues.en: That's simply the one variant of it.
cues.zh: 那只是其中的一种表现形式而已。

cues.en: Why is this happening?
cues.zh: 为什么会这样呢？

cues.en: Because, again, from an evolutionary perspective, sleep apnea couldn't have been great for survival.
cues.zh: 因为从进化的角度来看，睡眠呼吸暂停对生存并没有好处。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: Three primary reasons why.
cues.zh: 出现这种情况有三个主要原因。

cues.en: this is happening.
cues.zh: 第一个原因是我们的环境正在发生物理变化。

cues.en: The first is the fact that our environment is physically changing.
cues.zh: 我们的祖先从来不需要面对这个问题。

cues.en: Our ancestors never had to deal with this.
cues.zh: 第二个原因是，目前用于检测的方法要么极其过时，要么极难获取。

cues.en: Two, our current solutions for testing are either insanely outdated or incredibly difficult to get to.
cues.zh: 第三个主要问题是，我们在公共宣传中提供的解决方案过于笼统，因此

cues.en: The third major one is our solutions that we provide people in public communication are wildly generic, thus
cues.zh: 毫无帮助。

cues.en: not helpful.
cues.zh: 起不到任何作用。

cues.en: In fact, if you were to poll everyone listening right now, sleep comes up and you go, oh, great.
cues.zh: 事实上，要是现在去询问在场的所有人，提到睡眠时大家都会觉得，哦，太好了。

cues.en: They're going to tell me to sleep in a quiet room that's cold and dark.
cues.zh: 他们打算让我待在又冷又暗的安静房间里睡觉。

cues.en: And they're like, I've heard it all.
cues.zh: 他们就会说，这些我都听过了。

cues.en: And you have.
cues.zh: 你确实做到了。

cues.en: Where we need to get to next is how do we help people find these precision solutions based on their type of sleep issues?
cues.zh: 接下来我们需要探讨的是，如何帮助人们根据自身的睡眠问题类型找到精准的解决方案？

cues.en: But that's the three-part reason why this stuff is happening.
cues.zh: 但这就是导致这类事情发生的三个原因。

cues.en: Oh, I'd like to go into all three of them.
cues.zh: 哦，我想详细谈谈这三点。

cues.en: I also would like to just pause on the diagnosis part because there'll be people listening here that might have a suspicion that they need help.
cues.zh: 关于诊断这部分，我也想稍作停顿，因为在场可能有部分人正怀疑自己需要帮助。

cues.en: But again, they're going off their feelings.
cues.zh: 不过他们这又是凭感觉在做决定。

cues.en: How can they know for sure?
cues.zh: 他们怎么才能确定呢？

cues.en: what help they need and what their problem is.
cues.zh: 他们需要什么帮助，又存在什么问题。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: I always start with subjective.
cues.zh: 我总是从主观感受入手。

cues.en: How do you feel?
cues.zh: 你感觉怎么样？

cues.en: If you feel good, let's now like immediately take a breath.
cues.zh: 如果你感觉良好，那我们现在就立刻深呼吸一次吧。

cues.en: You have good energy.
cues.zh: 你的精力很充沛。

cues.en: You wake up, you feel good.
cues.zh: 你醒来时感觉状态不错。

cues.en: Like everyone's going to be a little bit tired.
cues.zh: 不过每个人都会有一点疲惫感。

cues.en: We also don't, we've actually had a, I've been working with for several years, a very close friend of you and I.
cues.zh: 我们也有这样的经历，实际上我有一位与你我关系非常亲密的朋友，我已经和他共事好几年了。

cues.en: We constantly have to battle because he'll just get like really honestly terrified because he gets sleepy at the end of the day.
cues.zh: 我们常常需要与之斗争，因为他到一天结束时真的会变得非常害怕，因为他会感到困倦。

cues.en: And I'm like, bro, that's the point.
cues.zh: 而我会说，兄弟，这正是关键所在。

cues.en: People that are hard chargers, high performers are actually afraid of being tired.
cues.zh: 那些精力充沛、表现优异的人其实很害怕感到疲惫。

cues.en: We have to recognize and realize that is natural and needed.
cues.zh: 我们必须认识到，这种感觉是自然的，也是必要的。

cues.en: You need to feel a little bit sleepy in the early afternoon and you should feel tired, unmotivated, lack of focus at the end of the day.
cues.zh: 你在下午早些时候应该会感到有点困倦，到一天结束时也应当感到疲惫、缺乏动力、注意力不集中。

cues.en: What if I didn't used to?
cues.zh: 要是我以前不是这样的呢？

cues.en: Because that's what people will, they compare it to an old version of themselves.
cues.zh: 因为人们就会这么做，他们会把自己和过去的自己作比较。

cues.en: Sure.
cues.zh: 当然。

cues.en: Again, we can say natural.
cues.zh: 再说一次，我们可以称之为自然现象。

cues.en: When you are sub 25, like you're just a powerhouse, right?
cues.zh: 在25岁以下的时候，人就像个能量无穷的引擎，对吧？

cues.en: When you're...
cues.zh: 当你……

cues.en: past 25, we shouldn't just accept frailty.
cues.zh: 过了25岁，我们就不能一味接受身体机能的衰退。

cues.en: We shouldn't accept a permanent decline, but we do have to start to realize we're not going to have the energy of a 20 year old.
cues.zh: 我们不应接受永久性的机能下降，但必须开始意识到自己不会再拥有20岁时的精力了。

cues.en: Like it's just not typically super realistic.
cues.zh: 因为这通常并不太现实。

cues.en: And if you do, you're probably getting there exogenously, right?
cues.zh: 如果你真的出现了这种情况，那很可能是通过外部因素导致的，对吧？

cues.en: Stimulants and other things, which have a place, but we just want to be a little bit careful of those things.
cues.zh: 比如兴奋剂之类的东西，虽然它们也有其用途，但我们还是需要对这类物质保持谨慎。

cues.en: We'll talk about stimulants, melatonin and all these things, but going back to this point of diagnosis.
cues.zh: 我们会谈到兴奋剂、褪黑素以及所有这些相关物质，但还是要回到诊断这个话题上来。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: So Jenny, who doesn't have much money.
cues.zh: 那么珍妮，她没什么钱。

cues.en: How does she get?
cues.zh: 她要怎么弄到呢？

cues.en: Okay, great.
cues.zh: 好的，太棒了。

cues.en: So one thing we can do, and we can put these in your show notes for you for free.
cues.zh: 有一件事我们可以做，我们可以免费把这些内容放进您的节目笔记里。

cues.en: There are a ton of completely free short questionnaires that are scientifically validated.
cues.zh: 有很多经过科学验证的完全免费的简短问卷。

cues.zh: 他们的骨骼、肌肉等等状况。

cues.en: And she basically proved to me, I'll put up the scan on the screen.
cues.zh: 她基本上向我证明了这一点，我会把扫描结果显示在屏幕上。

cues.en: It really is a mind-blowing scan.
cues.zh: 这真是一次令人惊叹的扫描。

cues.en: I've actually sent it to my best friends because it really did.
cues.zh: 我确实已经把结果发给了我最好的朋友们，因为它实在太出色了。

cues.en: I couldn't get this idea out of my head that I actually don't accept everything as an aging problem because the minute you do, you go on this downward cycle.
cues.zh: 我一直无法摆脱这样一个想法：我不能把所有问题都归咎于衰老，因为一旦那样想，就会陷入不断恶化的循环。

cues.en: And it blew my mind.
cues.zh: 这真的让我大为震惊。

cues.en: And that was such an important idea to get in my head at my age, at 30 years old.
cues.zh: 在我30岁的年纪能明白这个道理，实在非常重要。

cues.en: So when I feel like a pain in my back, my solution isn't...
cues.zh: 所以当我觉得背痛时，我的解决办法并不是……

cues.en: okay, Steven, you're getting older.
cues.zh: 好了，史蒂文，你年纪越来越大啦。

cues.en: Stop bending down and protect the pain.
cues.zh: 别再弯腰了，避免加重疼痛。

cues.en: It is go to the gym and start squatting and bending, et cetera.
cues.zh: 应该去健身房，开始做深蹲、弯腰之类的运动。

cues.en: There are some things that will go down with age.
cues.zh: 有些状况会随着年龄增长而出现。

cues.en: Sleep is actually one of them.
cues.zh: 睡眠其实就是其中之一。

cues.en: We typically just see you will sleep a little bit less as you age.
cues.zh: 通常我们认为人年纪越大睡眠时间就会越短。

cues.en: Fine.
cues.zh: 好吧。

cues.en: There are some aspects of that, but I think you can resist and fight as much of that as possible.
cues.zh: 虽然确实有这样的趋势，但我认为可以尽可能地抵抗和避免它。

cues.en: This is actually, you're seeing a turning of the tide right now that's just starting to emerge.
cues.zh: 实际上，现在正出现一种刚刚开始显现的转折趋势。

cues.en: With longevity.
cues.zh: 在长寿方面。

cues.en: Longevity is currently being positioned as this anti-aging phenomenon.
cues.zh: 目前长寿被视作一种抗衰老的现象。

cues.en: And people are already bored.
cues.zh: 而人们已经对此感到厌倦了。

cues.en: Like, is your goal to just not age?
cues.zh: 也就是说，你的目标只是不衰老吗？

cues.en: Or is your goal to dunk a basketball at 70?
cues.zh: 还是说你的目标是在70岁的时候还能扣篮？

cues.en: Do you want to have the 4x4 truck that has the best off-road package ever and it stays in your garage?
cues.zh: 你想拥有一辆配备最顶级越野配置的4x4卡车，但它却一直停在车库里吗？

cues.en: Probably not, right?
cues.zh: 大概不会吧？

cues.en: Like, you want to be able to be like, no, you want to live.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，你希望自己能够活下去，对吧？

cues.en: because you want to experience life.
cues.zh: 因为你想体验生活。

cues.en: And so then you want to be able to take advantage of those capacities and functionality.
cues.zh: 所以你才想充分利用这些能力和功能。

cues.en: Yeah, someone said to me, you want to extend your health span, not necessarily your lifespan.
cues.zh: 没错，有人跟我说，你是想延长健康寿命，而不一定是总寿命。

cues.en: It's not health span though.
cues.zh: 不过那并不是健康寿命。

cues.en: Oh, really?
cues.zh: 哦，真的吗？

cues.en: No, that's what I'm pushing back on.
cues.zh: 不，这正是我反对的观点。

cues.en: Health span, cool.
cues.zh: 健康寿命，挺不错的。

cues.en: I mean, lifespan, fine, great.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，总寿命也挺好，很棒。

cues.en: We're all past that.
cues.zh: 我们都已经超越那个阶段了。

cues.en: Health span though is still like, I don't want to be in pain.
cues.zh: 不过健康寿命还是意味着，我不想一直处于痛苦之中。

cues.en: I don't want to be, I'm saying performance span.
cues.zh: 我指的并不是表现时长，而是健康寿命。

cues.en: I'm saying I want you to be focused on having the most.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，我希望你们把重点放在获得尽可能长的健康寿命上。

cues.en: I want you to just be crushing cognitively.
cues.zh: 我希望你们的认知能力能够始终保持巅峰状态。

cues.en: I want you to be able to do anything you want physically for as long as we possibly can.
cues.zh: 我希望只要有可能，你们就能在身体方面做任何想做的事情。

cues.en: And not just being like, well, that's going to go away.
cues.zh: 而不是觉得那些问题以后自然就会消失。

cues.en: Let's just stay alive and be out of pain.
cues.zh: 我们就努力活下去，远离痛苦吧。

cues.en: I want you to be thinking about, no, I'm going to be doing awesome stuff in whatever venue you like to do it in for as long as you possibly can.
cues.zh: 我希望你们能想着，只要有可能，我就会在任何自己喜欢的场合做很棒的事情。

cues.en: I think people want both.
cues.zh: 我觉得人们两者都想要。

cues.en: Yeah, of course.
cues.zh: 没错，当然。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: But let's just not leave that into the table and assume the performance has to go away.
cues.zh: 但我们不要直接忽略这一点，就认定表现能力必须消失。

cues.en: So on this point of energy then, I think we've covered a lot of it and given me some sort of like really actionable principles there for how to have more energy.
cues.zh: 至于精力方面，我觉得我们已经讨论了很多，也给出了一些真正可行的原则，帮助人们提升精力。

cues.en: I do notice, I have to say, because I travel quite a lot.
cues.zh: 我必须说，我确实注意到了这一点，因为我经常出差。

cues.en: And so on occasion, my gym routine will be impacted.
cues.zh: 因此偶尔我的健身计划就会受到影响。

cues.en: And there's quite a clear correlation for me between the amount of times I've gone to the gym in previous weeks and how I feel in terms of energy today.
cues.zh: 对我来说，过去几周我去健身房的次数与今天我的精力状况之间有着非常明显的关联。

cues.en: I was thinking about this this morning.
cues.zh: 今天早上我就在思考这个问题。

cues.en: We're in New York here.
cues.zh: 我们现在在纽约。

cues.en: And over the last couple of weeks, I've probably been going to the gym like three times a week, if I'm being honest.
cues.zh: 说实话，过去几周我大概每周只去健身房三次左右。

cues.en: Whereas usually I'd go almost every day.
cues.zh: 而通常情况下我几乎每天都会去。

cues.en: And I have felt a difference in my energy.
cues.zh: 我的精力状态确实有了变化。

cues.en: And I wasn't sure if that was just like psychological or if that was supported by science.
cues.zh: 我不确定这是心理作用还是真的有科学依据。

cues.en: Both.
cues.zh: 两者都有。

cues.en: If you go and do a moderate to light, lower intensity exercise session, those are generally going to provide energy.
cues.zh: 如果你进行强度适中或较低的锻炼，通常会提升精力。

cues.en: If you're like, no, I did a like to the death training, I pegged it, I went all the way, whatever that is, whether you're lifting weights, intensity, whether you're getting heart rate all the way
cues.zh: 但如果你进行高强度的训练，比如竭尽全力地锻炼，不管是通过举重还是让心率达到极限，情况就不一样了。

cues.en: up, then you might walk out of those and be like, whoa, I'm exhausted.
cues.zh: 等体力恢复后，你走出训练场时可能会感叹，哇，我累坏了。

cues.en: but on aggregate, those will provide more daily energy.
cues.zh: 但总体而言，这些活动能为你提供更多日常能量。

cues.en: If you're traveling, sick, super busy, do the former.
cues.zh: 如果你正在出差、生病或非常忙碌，那就选择前者。

cues.en: Like just get in some motion, you'll feel better, you'll get a sweat in, you'll be there.
cues.zh: 只要动起来，你就会感觉好些，还能出点汗，状态也会提升。

cues.en: If you're healthy and looking for long-term adaptation, then that's when you can start to push the pace on the training.
cues.zh: 如果你身体健康且希望实现长期的身体适应，那时就可以开始加大训练强度。

cues.en: I want to speak to the business owners listening and watching right now.
cues.zh: 我想对正在聆听和观看的各位企业主说几句话。

cues.en: I know what it's like to be personally responsible for every decision.
cues.zh: 我深知亲自为每一个决策负责是怎样的感受。

cues.en: I founded my first company at 21 years old, and honestly, the pressure can be immense.
cues.zh: 我在21岁时创立了第一家公司，说实话，那种压力大到难以承受。

cues.en: It's the kind of mental load that takes its toll below the surface.
cues.zh: 这是一种会在潜意识里造成影响的心理负担。

cues.en: I recently did some tests through our sponsor, Function, which got me thinking about that invisible impact.
cues.zh: 最近我通过我们的赞助商Function做了一些检测，这让我开始思考那种无形的影响。

cues.en: I found that I had low levels of omega-3s.
cues.zh: 我发现我的欧米伽-3含量偏低。

cues.en: I had...
cues.zh: 我的……

cues.en: deficient levels of vitamin D, probably because I sit inside this dark room all day.
cues.zh: 维生素D水平偏低，很可能是因为我一整天都待在昏暗的房间里。

cues.en: And that has totally changed how I construct my day going forward.
cues.zh: 这彻底改变了我今后安排一天的方式。

cues.en: I get up in the morning and the first thing I now do is I go for a walk outside in the sunshine, in part to help my vitamin D levels increase, but also because it helps to reset
cues.zh: 我早上起床后做的第一件事就是到户外晒太阳，一方面是为了提升维生素D水平，另一方面也有助于重置

cues.en: my circadian rhythm.
cues.zh: 我的生物钟。

cues.en: With Function, you can check your brain health, your aging, your stress, and so much more.
cues.zh: 通过Function，你可以检测大脑健康状况、衰老程度、压力水平以及更多指标。

cues.en: They provide over 160 lab tests for what is equal to a dollar a day and member pricing on advanced imaging.
cues.zh: 他们提供超过160项实验室检测项目，每日费用仅约一美元，高级影像检查还享有会员价。

cues.en: head to functionhealth.com slash DOAC to join and use code DOAC25 for a $25 credit.
cues.zh: 请访问functionhealth.com/DOAC注册，使用代码DOAC25可获得25美元的抵扣额度。

cues.en: There should be a button just down below here.
cues.zh: 就在这里下方应该有个按钮。

cues.en: And if it says subscribe, you're already subscribed.
cues.zh: 如果显示的是subscribe，那就说明你已经订阅了。

cues.en: If it says subscriber, that means you're not yet.
cues.zh: 如果显示的是subscriber，那就意味着你还没有订阅。

cues.en: And if you're not subscribed, please could you do us a favor and hit that button?
cues.zh: 如果你还没有订阅，能否麻烦你点击一下那个按钮？

cues.en: It helps the show more than you know.
cues.zh: 这对我们的节目帮助非常大。

cues.en: And according to the algorithm, you're someone that watches our show, but you haven't yet hit that button.
cues.zh: 根据算法显示，您是观看我们节目的观众，但还没有点击过那个按钮。

cues.en: Thank you so much.
cues.zh: 非常感谢您。

cues.en: Speaking of training.
cues.zh: 说到训练的话。

cues.en: You know what this is, don't you?
cues.zh: 您知道这是什么吧？

cues.en: Sure.
cues.zh: 当然知道。

cues.en: This is a grip strength machine.
cues.zh: 这是一台握力测试仪。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: A lot of people told me that grip strength is the single biggest predictor of, I think they said like longevity and stuff like that.
cues.zh: 很多人告诉我，握力是预测寿命等指标的最重要因素。

cues.en: I wouldn't call it the number one predictor of mortality.
cues.zh: 我倒不认为它是预测死亡率的第一要素。

cues.en: It is a really nice scientific test.
cues.zh: 这确实是一项很不错的科学测试。

cues.en: Late 1980s, Stephen Blair and his team started looking at giant databases and started to realize that cardiovascular fitness,
cues.zh: 20世纪80年代末，斯蒂芬·布莱尔和他的团队开始研究庞大的数据库，逐渐意识到心肺功能，

cues.en: VO2 max, VO2 peak, things like this.
cues.zh: 最大摄氧量、峰值摄氧量这类指标的重要性。

cues.en: were predicting how long people were going to live.
cues.zh: 他们当时正在预测人们的预期寿命会是多少。

cues.en: And in fact, they started to realize it was out predicting what we call traditional clinical markers, blood pressure, your cholesterol levels, things like that.
cues.zh: 事实上，他们逐渐意识到，这些预测结果比我们所说的传统临床指标——比如血压、胆固醇水平之类的——更为准确。

cues.en: And this launched an entire 45-year field that we're in now, which is like, wait a minute, these performance-based markers are
cues.zh: 这就催生出了我们如今所处的这个长达45年的研究领域，人们开始思考：等等，这些基于表现能力的指标

cues.en: actually predicting health more than these indirect markers.
cues.zh: 实际上比那些间接指标更能预示健康状况。

cues.en: The unfortunate problem is that got taken too far.
cues.zh: 不幸的是，这一理念被过度夸大了。

cues.en: And so when you hear things like people, and my colleagues have been on your show and said things like, oh, grip strength is an important predictor of mortality.
cues.zh: 所以当你听到有人，还有我的同事们上过你们的节目，说‘握力是预测死亡风险的重要指标’之类的话时

cues.en: It's good.
cues.zh: 这固然不错。

cues.en: It's great.
cues.zh: 非常棒。

cues.en: It's an important message.
cues.zh: 这确实是一条重要的信息。

cues.en: But we have to be careful in being lost in what that means.
cues.zh: 但我们必须谨慎，不要过度解读其含义。

cues.en: Getting a grip strength device like that, which is probably under $40, is amazing.
cues.zh: 能买到价格大概在40美元以下的握力测试仪，实在令人惊喜。

cues.en: And what you will see consistently is those people that are really, really, really weak are in worse health on average.
cues.zh: 而我们可以一直观察到的现象是，那些握力极其薄弱的人，平均健康状况更差。

cues.en: Where we become false is saying, okay, therefore, you need to alter your lifestyle to maximize grip strength.
cues.zh: 我们常犯的错误就是认为，既然如此，就必须改变生活方式来提升握力。

cues.en: I did do my grip strength results, actually.
cues.zh: 实际上我确实测过自己的握力数据。

cues.en: Do you remember how they were?
cues.zh: 你还记得那些数据是多少吗？

cues.en: It was good.
cues.zh: 还不错。

cues.en: It was high.
cues.zh: 数值很高。

cues.en: You know what that tells me about your health?
cues.zh: 你知道这能说明你的健康状况如何吗？

cues.en: Nothing.
cues.zh: 什么都说明不了。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好吧。

cues.en: Why wouldn't it be high?
cues.zh: 为什么不会高呢？

cues.en: You're young, you're fit.
cues.zh: 你还年轻，身体也很健康。

cues.en: I have all those other markers.
cues.zh: 我还有其他各种健康指标。

cues.en: It's not going to tell you anything.
cues.zh: 这些数据根本无法反映任何问题。

cues.en: You know when these things are really powerful?
cues.zh: 你知道这些指标什么时候才真正有参考价值吗？

cues.en: Somebody who doesn't have blood work.
cues.zh: 那些没有做过血液检测的人。

cues.en: or doesn't have a body composition test or doesn't have anything else, it can give us a crude strength or a crude metric and say this person's probably
cues.zh: 或者没有做过身体成分检测，也没有其他任何检查的人，这些指标也能给我们一个粗略的强度数值或衡量标准，从而说明这个人很可能

cues.en: at a health risk.
cues.zh: 存在健康风险。

cues.en: So I've always been quite confused by this because is grip strength a proxy for my overall strength of my entire body and
cues.zh: 所以我一直对这一点很困惑，因为握力真的能代表我全身的整体力量吗，

cues.en: therefore it's just indicating that my overall strength is low or is it actually like my arm?
cues.zh: 所以它只是表明我的整体力量较低，还是实际上只代表我的手臂力量？

cues.en: It's both.
cues.zh: 两者都是。

cues.en: Oh, okay.
cues.zh: 哦，原来如此。

cues.en: It's both.
cues.zh: 两者都是。

cues.en: Here's why.
cues.zh: 原因就在这里。

cues.en: You know what you're really testing right there?
cues.zh: 你知道你实际上在测试什么吗？

cues.en: What's that?
cues.zh: 是什么？

cues.en: Your nervous system.
cues.zh: 你的神经系统。

cues.en: Oh, really?
cues.zh: 哦，真的吗？

cues.en: You're testing your brain.
cues.zh: 你其实是在测试大脑功能。

cues.en: So you're not testing your strength as much?
cues.zh: 那么说你测试的并不是力量本身？

cues.en: You are.
cues.zh: 其实也是在测试力量。

cues.en: But it's both.
cues.zh: 但两者是相关的。

cues.en: There's an overlap.
cues.zh: 存在重叠部分。

cues.en: That's why your grip strength, does it indicate general poor health?
cues.zh: 所以握力低能说明整体健康状况不佳吗？

cues.en: Yes.
cues.zh: 可以。

cues.en: That's the value.
cues.zh: 这就是它的价值所在。

cues.en: Does it tell you anything directly about your, it can.
cues.zh: 它能直接反映出你的某些状况，确实可以。

cues.en: And so this is when you see two camps here.
cues.zh: 正因如此，这里就会出现两种不同的观点。

cues.en: So camp one is like, great, I'm going to open up a gym down the street and it's going to test your grip strength.
cues.zh: 第一派的观点是，太好了，我打算在街角开一家健身房，通过训练来检测你的握力。

cues.en: And then we're going to focus all of your training on grip strength training.
cues.zh: 然后我们会让你把所有的训练都集中在握力训练上。

cues.en: That is, we've exaggerated the point.
cues.zh: 也就是说，我们把这个问题夸大处理了。

cues.en: The other camp is it doesn't matter.
cues.zh: 另一派则认为这并不重要。

cues.en: It's all indirect.
cues.zh: 因为这都是间接影响的。

cues.en: That's not true either.
cues.zh: 那也不对。

cues.en: It is an actionable, useful thing.
cues.zh: 握力确实是一种可行且实用的指标。

cues.en: What you don't need to worry about is optimizing it, maxing it.
cues.zh: 你不需要操心的是如何让它达到最优或最高水平。

cues.en: Like if you're in the 80th percentile, going to the 90th percentile probably doesn't make you live a day longer.
cues.zh: 比如如果你已经处于第80百分位，再提升到第90百分位大概也不会让你多活一天。

cues.en: Over the last probably three years, I would imagine there's over 20 to 25 studies that have been published on a very specific type of grip strength,
cues.zh: 在过去的三年里，我想已经有20到25项研究针对一种非常特定的握力类型进行了探讨，

cues.en: and that's grip strength asymmetry.
cues.zh: 那就是握力不对称性。

cues.en: Do you know why that matters?
cues.zh: 你知道为什么这很重要吗？

cues.en: I don't, but I know that I'm stronger on my left side than my right.
cues.zh: 我不知道原因，但我知道我的左侧比右侧力量更大。

cues.en: It's not uncommon.
cues.zh: 这种情况并不少见。

cues.en: Typically, your force-dependent limb is not your neural control limb.
cues.zh: 通常来说，力量较强的那条肢体并非由大脑神经直接控制的那一条。

cues.en: It was selfish.
cues.zh: 那是很自私的行为。

cues.en: It wasn't fiduciarily responsible to do that.
cues.zh: 那样做并不符合受托责任的要求。

cues.en: And now I have no more excuse.
cues.zh: 现在我再也没有借口了。

cues.en: Well, looking at this list then, listen, we can't, we're going to pray no one in your family, no one you know gets sick.
cues.zh: 好吧，看看这份清单，听着，我们只能祈祷你的家人、你认识的人都不会生病。

cues.en: So let's stay away from that one.
cues.zh: 所以咱们还是避开那种情况吧。

cues.en: The two of them there that can be quite motivating.
cues.zh: 那两项其实能起到很好的激励作用。

cues.en: And again, we don't want to motivate you if you're completely fine.
cues.zh: 再说一次，如果你已经完全健康，我们也不想再激励你。

cues.en: But this actually answers the question is to go and get your health checked.
cues.zh: 但这也正好回答了问题，那就是去做一次健康检查。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: That's like a simple solution because maybe you're fine and that's great.
cues.zh: 这其实是个简单的解决办法，因为也许你的身体状况已经很好了，那当然很棒。

cues.en: Maybe you're doing everything right.
cues.zh: 也许你做的所有事情都已经很正确了。

cues.en: But also just saying, oh, I want to lose a bit of weight or I want to do this isn't as solid enough as going and finding out how you're doing.
cues.zh: 但仅仅说‘我想减点肥’或者‘我想做这件事’，并不如去了解自己的真实健康状况那么可靠。

cues.en: One thing also I think is important because I will default to performance and optimization and getting the best and excellence.
cues.zh: 我还觉得有一点很重要，那就是我通常会倾向于追求最佳表现、不断优化，力求做到最好、出类拔萃。

cues.en: Like that's just the language and stuff I do.
cues.zh: 那只是我常用的表达方式和做事思路而已。

cues.en: But that's not the opposite of what you just said.
cues.zh: 但这并不与你刚才说的相反。

cues.en: To be really clear on that point, not everyone gravitates the idea of being the best possible ever.
cues.zh: 明确一点，不是每个人都渴望成为最优秀的人。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Totally fine.
cues.zh: 完全没问题。

cues.en: But that still doesn't mean it's okay to just check out on your health.
cues.zh: 但这仍然不意味着可以忽视自己的健康状况。

cues.en: You can have it both ways.
cues.zh: 两者完全可以兼得。

cues.en: You can be like, look, I'm not an optimizer.
cues.zh: 你可以这么说，看，我不是那种追求最优解的人。

cues.en: I'm not a maximizer.
cues.zh: 我也不是那种追求最大化的人。

cues.en: That doesn't live with my ethos and cool.
cues.zh: 那不符合我的理念和风格。

cues.en: We can still, though, say you still want to live that life for as long as possible, right?
cues.zh: 不过我们仍然可以说，你还是希望尽可能长久地过那样的生活，对吧？

cues.en: All right, let's just make sure we're paying enough attention to where nothing catches up and we're not waking up one day and be like, oh my gosh, now I've got to
cues.zh: 好吧，我们得确保足够留意那些不会被追上来的地方，免得有一天醒来后惊呼，天哪，现在我得

cues.en: go invest all these time and resource energy and all those things to go backwards in that.
cues.zh: 投入大量时间、精力以及各种资源去扭转局面。

cues.en: So pay attention enough.
cues.zh: 所以要足够重视这一点。

cues.en: How important is it to get clear on your why?
cues.zh: 明确自己的目标有多重要？

cues.en: You're not going to love the answer because traditionally when people approach me, they already
cues.zh: 你可能不会喜欢答案，因为通常人们来找我的时候，他们已经

cues.en: have that figured out.
cues.zh: 想清楚了。

cues.en: They're getting to me, they figured out why they're here or they're...
cues.zh: 他们来找我时，已经弄清楚自己为何而来，或者他们……

cues.en: If they haven't figured out, they at least have had the motivation to seek outside counsel like that.
cues.zh: 如果他们还没想清楚，至少也有动力去寻求外部的建议。

cues.en: So now they're getting to the what and how part.
cues.zh: 那么现在他们要开始探讨具体该做什么以及如何做了。

cues.en: What about bad goals?
cues.zh: 糟糕的目标又该如何处理呢？

cues.en: I look back at my life and I had some bad goals that set me up for failure.
cues.zh: 回顾我的人生，我曾经设定过一些会让我走向失败的不良目标。

cues.en: That's more realistic to what we all do.
cues.zh: 这其实更符合我们所有人的行事方式。

cues.en: And this is a, you're aiming at the wrong target.
cues.zh: 也就是说，你把目标定错了。

cues.en: I was aiming at, my goal when I was 20, I think it was 27, was to go to the gym every day and I failed.
cues.zh: 我20岁时的目标，记得是27岁的时候，就是每天去健身房，但我失败了。

cues.en: Oh, yeah, yeah.
cues.zh: 哦，对，没错。

cues.en: I failed six months later, but then once I'd failed, it was catastrophic for me.
cues.zh: 六个月后我就失败了，而一旦失败，对我来说后果就非常严重。

cues.en: And how are you not going to fail?
cues.zh: 那怎么可能不会失败呢？

cues.en: Yeah, yeah.
cues.zh: 是啊，没错。

cues.en: Were you going to go every day the rest of your life?
cues.zh: 你打算余生每天都去吗？

cues.en: It was a terrible goal because the day that I missed one day because of some flight.
cues.zh: 那是个糟糕的目标，因为有一次因为航班原因我缺训了一天。

cues.en: It was like my entire motivation was over.
cues.zh: 我感觉自己的全部动力都消失了。

cues.en: Yeah, sure.
cues.zh: 嗯，当然。

cues.en: And I was like, how do I get back on the horse now?
cues.zh: 我就想，现在要怎么重新振作起来呢？

cues.en: Here's an example.
cues.zh: 这里有个例子。

cues.en: You want to lose fat.
cues.zh: 你想减脂。

cues.en: Your goal is fat loss.
cues.zh: 你的目标是减掉脂肪。

cues.en: Cool.
cues.zh: 不错。

cues.en: Why aren't you leaner right now?
cues.zh: 那为什么你现在还没变得更瘦呢？

cues.en: And you automatically think I have to exercise more and diet.
cues.zh: 于是你自然而然就会觉得我得多锻炼、控制饮食。

cues.en: And I'm like, great.
cues.zh: 我就想，很好啊。

cues.en: That's the tactic.
cues.zh: 这就是常用的策略。

cues.en: I want to know why you're not there right now.
cues.zh: 我想知道为什么你现在还没达到那个状态。

cues.en: What is the thing that's actually getting in the way?
cues.zh: 到底是什么在阻碍我们呢？

cues.en: Because like calorie fight, like, yeah, yeah.
cues.zh: 因为就是那种热量控制的斗争，对，就是那样。

cues.en: Like, you know that though, but it's not working.
cues.zh: 你懂我的意思，但那样做根本没用。

cues.en: What is really in the way?
cues.zh: 真正阻碍我们的是什么？

cues.en: Do we actually have some hidden stressor?
cues.zh: 我们身上是不是存在某些隐藏的压力源？

cues.en: A lot of times people will say things like, I gotta lose fat so I can get healthy.
cues.zh: 很多人会说，我得减脂才能保持健康。

cues.en: And we will generally say, you need to get healthy first.
cues.zh: 而我们通常会回答，你得先让身体健康起来。

cues.en: And then the fat loss would be a whole lot easier.
cues.zh: 那样减脂就会容易得多。

cues.en: That's the bad goal.
cues.zh: 那是个错误的目标。

cues.en: And so we'll ask this question, like, what would success look like?
cues.zh: 所以我们会问这样一个问题，成功会是什么样子？

cues.en: What would failure look like?
cues.zh: 失败又会是什么样子？

cues.en: And when we hear things like, oh, success is I lose these 25 pounds.
cues.zh: 当听到有人说，哦，成功就是我减掉这25磅时。

cues.en: All right, great.
cues.zh: 好的，太棒了。

cues.en: Let me ask you this.
cues.zh: 让我问你一个问题。

cues.en: If we lost 12 pounds and then your shoulder pain went away, you have normal bowel movements now for the first time in
cues.zh: 如果我们减掉了12磅，你的肩痛也消失了，而且10年来你第一次有了正常的排便，精力也大幅提升，这难道就全是失败吗？

cues.en: 10 years, your energy is way up, is that all a failure?
cues.zh: 不，这就是成功。

cues.en: No, that's success.
cues.zh: 所以我们并没有真正找到成功的方法。

cues.en: So then we didn't just find success properly.
cues.zh: 因此，如何帮助人们在那些一直困扰他们的领域取得进步，是我们重点关注的课题。

cues.en: So it's a huge focus of how we help people actually make progress in those areas that they've struggled with.
cues.zh: 博士，

cues.en: Dr.
cues.zh: 博士

cues.en: Andy Galpin, we have a closing tradition where the last guest leaves a question for the next, not knowing who they're leaving it for.
cues.zh: 留给你的问题是，如果你确定自己会失败，还有哪些事情是值得去做的？

cues.en: And the question left for you is, if you were sure to fail, what would still be worth doing?
cues.zh: 非常好的问题。

cues.en: A great question.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: Fantastic question.
cues.zh: 问得真好。

cues.en: I am ultra competitive, but I really don't mind losing.
cues.zh: 我极具竞争意识，但其实并不介意失败。

cues.en: So my answer to that question was, it sounds like a cop-out, but it's all of it.
cues.zh: 对于那个问题我的回答是，虽然听起来像是在推脱，但实际上全都是如此。

cues.en: Because I actually don't care about failing that much.
cues.zh: 因为我其实并不太在乎失败这件事。

cues.en: It just doesn't bother me.
cues.zh: 它根本不会困扰我。

cues.en: I just like the competing thing.
cues.zh: 我就是喜欢竞争的感觉。

cues.en: I like the doing thing.
cues.zh: 我喜欢付诸行动的感觉。

cues.en: So my initial reaction to that was like, God, being around my kids, right?
cues.zh: 一开始我对此的反应是，天哪，和孩子们在一起的时候不就是这样吗？

cues.en: You fail anything you want there, and I'm like, we're winning, right?
cues.zh: 在那里无论做什么都会失败，但我会想，我们不是还在赢吗？

cues.en: And then I went to business things, and I'm like, I don't even really care about losing those.
cues.zh: 后来涉及到商业领域时，我甚至也不太在乎会输。

cues.en: Because you get to do it.
cues.zh: 因为至少还有机会去做。

cues.en: You get to be active and whatever.
cues.zh: 至少还能保持活跃，做各种事情。

cues.en: So kind of a cop-out, but my answer would be all of them, man.
cues.zh: 这算是一种推脱吧，但我的答案是全部都是，伙计。

cues.en: The process is dope.
cues.zh: 整个过程非常棒。

cues.en: The podium is the process.
cues.zh: 演讲台本身就是这个过程。

cues.en: Yeah, man.
cues.zh: 没错，伙计。

cues.en: The process over the podium.
cues.zh: 在演讲台上的整个过程。

cues.en: Dr.
cues.zh: 博士。

cues.en: Andy Galpin, thank you so much.
cues.zh: 安迪·加尔平，非常感谢您。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢。

cues.en: You're held in such high regard by everybody.
cues.zh: 大家都对您极为敬重。

cues.en: I think there's two reasons.
cues.zh: 我觉得原因有两个。

cues.en: I think it's so you're so deeply obsessed with this subject matter for reasons that we talked a lot about last time.
cues.zh: 一方面是因为您对我们上次谈过很多次的这个研究主题有着极深的执着。

cues.en: But also, I think the essence of your motivations is so unbelievably pure.
cues.zh: 另一方面，我认为您动机的本质纯得令人难以置信。

cues.en: you know before we started recording you were saying to me how like you're really not that concerned with the business side of things because what you'd love to do is just be focusing on the research
cues.zh: 你知道，在我们开始录制之前，你就跟我说过你其实并不太关心业务方面的问题，因为你真正想做的就是专注于研究工作。

cues.en: the education and the coaching and i think that says a lot about you and it comes through people understand that you're just deeply obsessed about this stuff in a way which allows us to
cues.zh: 还有教育与指导工作，我觉得这很能体现你的特质，大家也能看出你对此事有着极度的热忱，而这正是让我们能够从你所做的所有工作中获得巨大益处的原因。

cues.en: benefit tremendously from all the work that you have done and you're a wonderful synthesizer of very very complex things so please carry on doing what you're doing if people want
cues.zh: 你还是非常擅长把极其复杂的事物整合起来，所以如果大家还想继续听你的节目，或者想进一步了解你的内容，想和你一起继续这段旅程，他们该去哪里呢？

cues.en: to go and listen to your show or if they want to go consume more of your stuff, if they want to continue this journey with you, where do they go?
cues.zh: 把他们引向最好的地方是哪里？

cues.en: Where's the best place to send them?
cues.zh: 首先，非常感谢你的美言，也感谢邀请我再次参与录制。

cues.en: Well, first of all, thank you for those kind words and to be invited back.
cues.zh: 这是个难得的机会，我永远都不会忘记这份恩情。

cues.en: It's a huge opportunity and I will never be ungrateful for it.
cues.zh: 我的播客名叫《与安迪博士一起表现》，在各大平台都能收听。

cues.en: My podcast is called Perform with Dr.
cues.zh: 另外andygalpin.com以及Instagram等社交媒体平台，可能是最方便关注我的方式。

cues.en: Andy Galpin, available everywhere.
cues.zh: 我强烈建议大家去订阅安迪的频道。

cues.en: And then andygalpin.com and social media, Instagram and all that stuff is probably the easiest way to follow along.
cues.zh: 我们马上会在下方附上链接。

cues.en: I highly recommend you go and subscribe to Andy's channel.
cues.zh: 我会继续努力把复杂的内容用简单的方式呈现出来。

cues.en: We're going to link it down below now.
cues.zh: 希望大家都能持续关注我的更新。

cues.en: But you're incredibly rigorous with all the work that you do.
cues.zh: 但你对待所有工作都极其严谨。

cues.en: Having spoken to Andrew, Andrew Huberman, who's a good friend of both of ours, he's also told me just how utterly obsessed you are with truth
cues.zh: 我和我们共同的好友安德鲁·胡伯曼谈过，他也告诉我你对真相有着多么强烈的执着。

cues.en: and also your mission of helping people become who they could be.
cues.zh: 还有你帮助人们成为最佳自我的使命。

cues.en: And that shines through in all of your work.
cues.zh: 这些都体现在你的所有工作中。

cues.en: So please go and subscribe to Andy's podcast as well, Perform.
cues.zh: 所以也请去订阅安迪的播客《Perform》吧。

cues.en: And I shall link all of his other...
cues.zh: 我会在下面附上他所有的其他……

cues.en: resources below, including some of them that we've mentioned today, including the tests and questionnaires that we talked about.
cues.zh: 资源，包括我们今天提到过的一些内容，以及我们讨论过的测试和问卷。

cues.en: Andy, thank you.
cues.zh: 安迪，谢谢你。

cues.en: YouTube have this new crazy algorithm where they know exactly what video you would like to watch next based on AI and all of your viewing behavior.
cues.zh: YouTube现在有个新的奇怪算法，它能通过人工智能和你的所有观看行为，准确判断你想看下一个什么视频。

cues.en: And the algorithm says that this video is the perfect video for you.
cues.zh: 而这个算法会判定这个视频正是为你准备的完美内容。

cues.en: It's different for everybody looking right now.
cues.zh: 目前对每个人来说显示的内容都不一样。

cues.en: Check this video out.
cues.zh: 去看看这个视频吧。

cues.en: I bet you, you might love it.
cues.zh: 我敢说，你一定会喜欢它的。

material.title: CEO 日记 · 里克·鲁宾谈创造力
material.subtitle: The Diary of a CEO · Rick Rubin： The Only Skill That Matters Now Is The One Thing AI Can Never Steal! · 英文自动字幕

cues.en: Jay-Z wrote in a way that no one else wrote.
cues.zh: Jay-Z的写作风格是其他人无法复制的。

cues.en: All the other rappers that I worked with spent a lot of time writing lyrics, and I never saw Jay write lyrics.
cues.zh: 我合作过的其他说唱歌手都花大量时间写歌词，但我从未见过Jay写歌词。

cues.en: And when I played him the beat for 99 Problems, he said, OK, just keep playing it over and over again.
cues.zh: 当我把《99 Problems》的节奏给他听时，他说好的，继续反复播放吧。

cues.en: And he sat in the back of the room.
cues.zh: 他坐在房间的后面。

cues.en: You could hear him mumbling or humming.
cues.zh: 能听到他在低声嘀咕或哼唱。

cues.en: After 20 or 30 minutes, he's like, OK, I got it, and ran into the other room and did the first verse.
cues.zh: 二十到三十分钟后，他说好了，我懂了，然后跑进另一个房间写起了第一段歌词。

cues.en: He did, let's say, three takes, and then he came in and he listened to them.
cues.zh: 他大概试了三遍，之后回来听了那些歌词。

cues.en: He's like, oh, yeah, I think the second one's good.
cues.zh: 他说，哦，对，我觉得第二遍不错。

cues.en: happens in his mind and then this big list of people that you've worked with i mean it's just this unbelievable list jay-z kanye adele justin timberlake and mick
cues.zh: 他的脑海里会浮现出各种想法，还有那一长串他曾合作过的人，那名单简直长得令人难以置信——Jay-Z、Kanye、Adele、Justin Timberlake、Mick Jagger以及Red Hot Chili Peppers。你以为这些人为什么找你？因为我从事创作已经40年了，最初只是把做音乐当作爱好，

cues.en: jagger and the red hot chili peppers why do you think these people call you because i've been making things for 40 years and i started making music as a hobby it
cues.zh: 结果它逐渐发展成了一种独立的事业，而那份名单里的那些人其实并不特别。

cues.en: ended up picking on a life of its own and becoming a business and that list They're not special.
cues.zh: 我认为是普通的人做出了选择而已。

cues.en: I would say they're ordinary people who made a decision.
cues.zh: 他们不过是做出了决定的普通人罢了。

cues.en: I think of Eminem as a good example.
cues.zh: 我觉得埃米纳姆是个很好的例子。

cues.en: Eminem is someone who's always writing because he wants to be the best he could possibly be.
cues.zh: 埃米纳姆是个始终在创作的人，因为他想做到最好。

cues.en: And he's insanely obsessive about that.
cues.zh: 而且他对这一点有着极其强烈的执着。

cues.en: It appears that some people are just like inherently more creative than others.
cues.zh: 显然，有些人天生就比其他人更有创造力。

cues.en: Well, creativity is beaten out of us over the course of our lives.
cues.zh: 其实，我们的创造力会在一生中逐渐被磨灭。

cues.en: We go to school, we're taught to follow rules.
cues.zh: 我们上学时，被教导要遵守规则。

cues.en: The rules are not there to help us.
cues.zh: 那些规则并不是为了帮助我们。

cues.en: The rules are there to control us.
cues.zh: 那些规则是为了控制我们。

cues.en: We're not taught to be free creative thinkers.
cues.zh: 我们并没有被教导如何成为自由且富有创造力的思考者。

cues.en: So I'm suggesting we break free and express ourselves freely.
cues.zh: 所以我建议我们要挣脱束缚，自由地表达自己。

cues.en: How?
cues.zh: 怎么做呢？

cues.en: Well, all of the best things involve risk.
cues.zh: 嗯，所有最出色的事物都离不开风险。

cues.en: It's only through the risk that the greatness is shown.
cues.zh: 唯有通过承担风险，才能展现出真正的伟大。
