cues.en: You worked on that album.
cues.zh: 你参与制作了那张专辑。

cues.en: And that's a good example of like, it was a sort of an anti-hip hop album.
cues.zh: 这是个很好的例子，可以说它算是一种反嘻哈专辑。

cues.en: And that was done intentionally.
cues.zh: 这是有意为之的。

cues.en: And it definitely, we went as far as we could into an
cues.zh: 而且我们确实尽可能深入到了一个

cues.en: indefensible realm.
cues.zh: 难以辩护的领域。

cues.en: But what about the numbers?
cues.zh: 那销售数据怎么样呢？

cues.en: What about the sales?
cues.zh: 那销售情况怎么样？

cues.en: What about the record label?
cues.zh: 唱片公司那边呢？

cues.en: Is it an important album to you now?
cues.zh: 对您来说，这现在还是一张重要的专辑吗？

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: Did its job.
cues.zh: 它完成了任务。

cues.en: Those near-term incentives though.
cues.zh: 不过那些短期的激励措施……

cues.en: Listen, we need, Drake, we need you to make another.
cues.zh: 听着，德雷克，我们需要你再制作一张。

cues.en: We never consider near-term incentive ever at any point in time.
cues.zh: 我们在任何时候都不会考虑短期激励这种事。

cues.en: Never once.
cues.zh: 一次都不会。

cues.en: Never a consideration.
cues.zh: 根本不会考虑。

cues.en: It doesn't exist.
cues.zh: 那东西根本不存在。

cues.en: We're making things forever.
cues.zh: 我们会永远创造新事物。

cues.en: We're making things that are truly personal to us.
cues.zh: 我们创造的是真正属于我们自己的东西。

cues.en: And if it's truly personal to us, if someone doesn't get it, that's, they just don't get it yet.
cues.zh: 如果它是真正属于我们的，就算有人理解不了，那也只是他们还没懂而已。

cues.en: Or maybe they'll never get it.
cues.zh: 或者他们可能永远也理解不了。

cues.en: And it's fine because I know this is my diary entry.
cues.zh: 这没关系，因为我知道这是我的日记内容。

cues.en: Can someone else read your diary entry and tell you it's wrong?
cues.zh: 会有别人读完你的日记后说它有错吗？

cues.en: It's not good enough.
cues.zh: 说它不够好。

cues.en: Or it's not true.
cues.zh: 或者说它不真实。

cues.en: It's not how you see the world.
cues.zh: 说它不符合你对世界的看法。

cues.en: Everything we make is a diary entry.
cues.zh: 我们创造的一切都是一篇日记。

cues.en: Everything we make is our personal
cues.zh: 我们创造的一切都是我们个人的

cues.en: true expression.
cues.zh: 真实表达。

cues.en: The reason we're saying it is to show you see it like that, we see it like this, or I see it like this.
cues.zh: 我们这么说是为了向您展示，您是这么看的，我们是这么看的，或者我是这么看的。

cues.en: This is how I see it.
cues.zh: 这就是我眼中的样子。

cues.en: And with that information, you can see it's like, ah, I never considered that before.
cues.zh: 有了这些信息，您就会发现，啊，我以前从未考虑过这一点。

cues.en: There's more.
cues.zh: 还有更多。

cues.en: The world is bigger than I thought.
cues.zh: 这个世界比我想象的要广阔。

cues.en: It's not just more the same.
cues.zh: 并不只是更多相同的东西。

cues.en: It's not just...
cues.zh: 也不仅仅是...

cues.en: more numbers.
cues.zh: 更多的数字。

cues.en: And it's also the more numbers game is a shorter term game.
cues.zh: 而且，这种靠更多数字的策略其实属于短期策略。

cues.en: I remember I made an album with Lincoln Park, who at the time were probably one of the biggest bands in the
cues.zh: 我记得我和Lincoln Park一起制作过一张专辑，当时他们大概是全

cues.en: world.
cues.zh: 世界范围内最出色的乐队之一。

cues.en: And they'd made three albums that were, I would say, stylistically very similar.
cues.zh: 他们已经出了三张专辑，从风格上来说非常相似。

cues.en: They were rap rock and they were, there was this, there was a rap rock movement.
cues.zh: 那是说唱摇滚风格，当时还出现了一股说唱摇滚音乐潮流。

cues.en: Korn, I guess Rage Against the Machine was first, Korn, Limp Bizkit, all these bands.
cues.zh: 我觉得首先是Rage Against the Machine，还有Korn、Limp Bizkit，这些乐队。

cues.en: And Linkin Park was probably the last of that wave of music.
cues.zh: 而Linkin Park大概是那一波音乐中的最后一批。

cues.en: And they were wildly successful doing that music.
cues.zh: 他们演奏这种音乐时取得了极大的成功。

cues.en: And when we started working together, there was a choice.
cues.zh: 当我们开始一起合作时，面临一个选择。

cues.en: We could continue and do the next in that same style, which the audience would love, and it would be easy to do.
cues.zh: 我们可以继续沿用同样的风格创作，观众会喜欢，而且制作起来也很容易。

cues.en: Or we could be true to where the band was in this moment of time, 10 years after they started about, probably 10 years after they started,
cues.zh: 或者我们可以忠实于乐队在那个阶段的定位，大概是在他们成立10年之后，

cues.en: and be free to find the new sound, the next sound.
cues.zh: 去自由探索新的音乐风格、下一种音乐风格。

cues.en: And when we did that, probably half of the audience didn't like it, and half of the audience loved it, and new people came along,
cues.zh: 当我们这么做的时候，大概有一半的观众不喜欢，另一半则很喜欢，同时也有新听众出现。

cues.en: and they set themselves up.
cues.zh: 他们因此能够

cues.en: to have a much longer career of making the things that they wanted to make.
cues.zh: 长久地创作自己想做的音乐。

cues.en: Whereas they were already on the tail end of a genre that had they made another one, maybe it would have been, it probably would have
cues.zh: 而当时他们已经处于那个音乐流派的末期，如果再创作同一类型的作品，或许情况还会是这样。

cues.en: been, you know, as successful as what they had done.
cues.zh: 要知道，那部作品已经算是该类型作品的末期作品了，要是他们再拍一部，或许也能取得和之前一样的成功。

cues.en: But long term, the genre was dying.
cues.zh: 但从长远来看，这个类型正在走向衰落。

cues.en: Again, none of this was thought about at the time.
cues.zh: 话说回来，当时根本没人考虑过这些问题。

cues.en: Another example I think of is Radiohead's Kid A.
cues.zh: 我记得的另一个例子是Radiohead的《Kid A》。

cues.en: I remember when Kid A came out, I didn't like it at all.
cues.zh: 《Kid A》发行的时候，我完全不喜欢它。

cues.en: I loved the Benz and OK Computer.
cues.zh: 我倒是很喜欢《Benz》和《OK Computer》。

cues.en: They were my favorite band.
cues.zh: 那是我最喜欢的乐队。

cues.en: And then they made this album Kid A.
cues.zh: 后来他们推出了这张《Kid A》专辑。

cues.en: And it was totally different.
cues.zh: 风格完全变了。

cues.en: And it really alienated me.
cues.zh: 这让我感到很疏离。

cues.en: And today, that might be my favorite Radiohead album.
cues.zh: 不过如今，它可能反倒成了我最喜欢的Radiohead专辑。

cues.en: It feels like a risk.
cues.zh: 这感觉就像是一次冒险。

cues.en: Yes, but that's all of the best things involve risk.
cues.zh: 没错，但所有最棒的事物都离不开风险。

cues.en: Because I'm sure you've also got examples where someone followed that thesis of listening to what they wanted to make or doing it for themselves and not thinking too much about the audience and it didn't
cues.zh: 因为我敢肯定，你们肯定也见过这样的例子：有人只听从自己想创作的内容或只为自己做事，而不太考虑受众，结果却并不

cues.en: work.
cues.zh: 成功。

cues.en: Of course.
cues.zh: 当然。

cues.en: And they could have just made, you know, a hit and paid off their mortgage and...
cues.zh: 他们本可以只创作出热门作品，这样就还清了房贷，还能……

cues.en: Yeah, it's not so interesting.
cues.zh: 是啊，那样就没那么有趣了。

cues.en: I know, it's not so interesting to me.
cues.zh: 我知道，对我来说也没那么有趣。

cues.en: I think that's, it's a different game.
cues.zh: 我觉得那是另一回事。

cues.en: That's the, you know, that's the investment commerce game and I'm in the art game.
cues.zh: 那是投资商业领域的游戏，而我从事的是艺术领域的工作。

cues.en: It's just a different thing.
cues.zh: 就是两码事而已。

cues.en: There's nothing wrong with that other game.
cues.zh: 那种游戏本身并没有什么问题。

cues.en: It's just not my game.
cues.zh: 只是不是我擅长的领域罢了。

cues.en: Which one leads to more success over the long term?
cues.zh: 从长远来看，哪一种方式能带来更多成功？

cues.en: Defined by, let's say, if we define success in this context by the subjective opinion of people that that was good and money.
cues.zh: 可以说，如果我们用人们认为某件事很棒以及能带来金钱这样的主观看法来定义成功的话，

cues.en: All I can say is that I've been making things for 40 years.
cues.zh: 我只能说，我从事创作已经40年了。

cues.en: I have never...
cues.zh: 我从来没……

cues.en: done it the way you're suggesting.
cues.zh: 按照你建议的那种方式去做过。

cues.en: I've always taken the risk.
cues.zh: 我一直都在承担风险。

cues.en: I've always made my favorite thing.
cues.zh: 我一直都在做自己最喜欢的事情。

cues.en: I've always supported the artists in making their favorite thing.
cues.zh: 我一直都在支持艺术家们去做他们最喜欢的事情。

cues.en: And luckily, a lot of revolutionary things have happened from that.
cues.zh: 幸运的是，由此诞生了许多具有革命性的作品。

cues.en: And I would say things that probably inspired other artists to be more free and
cues.zh: 我认为这些作品很可能激励了其他艺术家更加自由地

cues.en: more true and more honest and take bigger risks.
cues.zh: 更加真实、更加诚恳，并且敢于承担更大的风险。

cues.en: to make something more interesting, made the world a more interesting place.
cues.zh: 从而创作出更有趣的作品，也让世界变得更加有趣。

cues.en: Why do you think these people call you?
cues.zh: 你认为这些人为什么称呼你呢？

cues.en: I think it's probably different for different artists.
cues.zh: 我觉得不同的艺术家情况可能有所不同。

cues.en: Why did Jay-Z call you?
cues.zh: Jay-Z为什么找你？

cues.en: The time that I first met Jay was when he was making the Black Album, and he wanted to...
cues.zh: 我第一次见到Jay的时候，他正在制作《Black Album》，他想要……

cues.en: He was planning on retiring, and this was going to be his one song, his final album, the Black Album, was Jay-Z's last album.
cues.zh: 他原本打算退休，打算把这首歌作为自己的最后一首作品，把这张专辑《Black Album》当作Jay-Z的最后一张专辑。

cues.en: Turned out not to be, but that was the plan.
cues.zh: 后来并没有变成那样，但那确实是他的计划。

cues.en: He asked his 10 favorite producers to each make one track with him.
cues.zh: 他让10位他最喜欢的制作人各自和他一起创作一首曲子。

cues.en: And ours was called 99 Problems.
cues.zh: 我们创作的那一首就叫《99 Problems》。

cues.en: And it was a really fun experience to make.
cues.zh: 制作那首歌的经历非常有趣。

cues.en: I mean, what an iconic record that is.
cues.zh: 我的天，那可真是一张极具代表性的专辑啊。

cues.en: What was your contribution to that record?
cues.zh: 你对那张专辑做出了什么贡献？

cues.en: Everybody knows that record.
cues.zh: 每个人都知道那张专辑。

cues.en: Everybody.
cues.zh: 大家都知道那首歌。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: We created the track and we played it for Jay and he liked it.
cues.zh: 我们创作了这首曲子，播放给杰伊听，他很喜欢。

cues.en: And then he wrote the words and rapped on top of it.
cues.zh: 然后他写了歌词，并在曲子上进行了说唱。

cues.en: So you produced the music?
cues.zh: 那么是你负责制作音乐吗？

cues.en: Made the music.
cues.zh: 我负责创作音乐。

cues.en: Made the music.
cues.zh: 我负责创作音乐。

cues.en: I read that you gave him direction in terms of the lyrics as well.
cues.zh: 我听说你在歌词方面也给了他指导。

cues.en: Well, my friend Chris Rock had the idea of...
cues.zh: 其实是我的朋友克里斯·洛克提出了这个想法……

cues.en: Ice-T had a song called 99 Problems that was the opposite.
cues.zh: Ice-T有一首叫《99个问题》的歌，内容正好相反。

cues.en: It was, I have 99 problems and a bitch ain't one, and then it's a story about the girls.
cues.zh: 那首歌的歌词是‘我有99个问题，可女人不算一个’，讲的是关于女人的故事。

cues.en: And Chris said, you know, 99 problems would be a great hook and it doesn't have to be about the girls.
cues.zh: 克里斯说，你知道的，‘99个问题’会是个很棒的hook，而且不一定要围绕女人来写。

cues.en: And then I suggested to Jay, make it about the problems.
cues.zh: 然后我建议杰伊，把主题定为那些问题。

cues.en: And then that's what it was.
cues.zh: 后来作品确实就是围绕这些问题创作的。

cues.en: And business people, startups, they seek your advice as well?
cues.zh: 那商界人士和初创企业也会向你寻求建议吗？

cues.en: Entrepreneurs?
cues.zh: 企业家们？

cues.en: All the time.
cues.zh: 一直都有。

cues.en: And what are they seeking?
cues.zh: 他们想要寻求什么建议？

cues.en: Let's talk about 99 problems a little more because it's an interesting story.
cues.zh: 让我们再多聊聊《99 Problems》，因为这是个有趣的故事。

cues.en: Jay-Z was signed to Def Jam Records.
cues.zh: 杰·Z当时签约了Def Jam唱片公司。

cues.en: Def Jam Records was the label that I founded.
cues.zh: Def Jam唱片公司是我创立的厂牌。

cues.en: I was no longer at Def Jam when we made 99 Problems.
cues.zh: 我们在制作《99 Problems》时我已经不在Def Jam了。

cues.en: And I remember giving it to the people at Def Jam and the person who was the president of Def Jam at the time listened to it.
cues.zh: 我记得把这首歌交给了Def Jam的同事，当时担任公司总裁的那位也听了。

cues.en: And he's like, oh, this is great.
cues.zh: 他当时就说，哦，这太棒了。

cues.en: It'll never be a single, but it'll be a great album track.
cues.zh: 它不会成为单曲，但会是一首很棒的专辑曲目。

cues.en: And I remember thinking, okay.
cues.zh: 我记得当时就想，好吧。

cues.en: And again, I don't know.
cues.zh: 再说一次，我也不知道。

cues.en: I couldn't say.
cues.zh: 我无法断言。

cues.en: But the president of the label that I founded was saying this could never be a single because it doesn't sound like everything else on the
cues.zh: 但我创立的唱片公司的总裁说，这绝对不可能成为单曲，因为它听起来和广播里其他的歌曲都不一样。

cues.en: radio.
cues.zh: 那就是那种老式的思维方式。

cues.en: That was the old way of thinking.
cues.zh: 那是一种常规的思维模式，就是制作出和广播里其他歌曲风格相同的作品来播放。

cues.en: That was the normal way of thinking of like, you make things to go on the radio that sound like everything else on the radio.
cues.zh: 但要是那样做，又有谁会在意呢？

cues.en: But if you do that, who cares?
cues.zh: 那不还是老一套罢了。

cues.en: It's just more of the same.
cues.zh: 所以《99 Problems》听起来和广播里的任何歌曲都不一样。

cues.en: So 99 Problems didn't sound like anything on the radio.
cues.zh: 因此当它最终出现在广播中时，产生了巨大的影响。

cues.en: So when it eventually got on the radio, it had a big impact.
cues.zh: 所以当它最终登上广播频道时，确实带来了深远的影响。

cues.en: So another band I work with is called System of a Down.
cues.zh: 我还曾与另一支乐队合作，他们的名字叫System of a Down。

cues.en: And I remember bringing their record to Kevin Weatherly at K-Rock, which is the rock station, alternative rock station
cues.zh: 我记得我把他们的唱片拿给了加利福尼亚那家摇滚电台K-Rock的凯文·韦瑟利。

cues.en: in California.
cues.zh: 如果那家电台播放他们的歌，全美其他所有另类摇滚电台都会跟着播放。

cues.en: And if they play it, all of the other alternative rock stations in the country play it.
cues.zh: K-Rock算是当时最具影响力的电台。

cues.en: They were like the leading station.
cues.zh: 那是支在夜店里逐渐走红的加利福尼亚乐队。

cues.en: And this was a California band that was starting to get popular in the clubs.
cues.zh: 每场演出大概只有200人到场，但夜店的票总是卖光。

cues.en: Maybe 200 people would come, but in a club, the club would sell out.
cues.zh: 这是个好迹象。

cues.en: Good sign.
cues.zh: 我带去的歌好像叫《Sugar》。

cues.en: And I brought, I think the song was called Sugar.
cues.zh: 我把唱片拿给凯文·韦瑟利，然后为他播放了这首歌。

cues.en: And I brought it to Kevin Weatherly and I played it for him.
cues.zh: 他却说，我们不仅不会播放这张唱片，更永远不会在电台介绍这支乐队，因为他们的音乐听起来太疯狂了。

cues.en: And he said, not only will we not play this record, we will never play this band on our station because it sounded insane.
cues.zh: 那音乐和电台里其他任何歌曲都不一样。

cues.en: It didn't sound like anything else on the station.
cues.zh: 这声音和电台里的其他任何内容都不一样。

cues.en: One year later, number one song on the station, most requested.
cues.zh: 一年后，这首歌成了电台播放量第一、听众点播率最高的曲目。

cues.en: And two weeks ago, I saw System of a Down sell out 80,000 seats in a stadium in Paris.
cues.zh: 两周前，我亲眼看到System of a Down在巴黎的体育场把8万个座位全部卖空。

cues.en: They sold it out two nights in a row.
cues.zh: 他们连续两个晚上都把门票卖得一干二净。

cues.en: I can't tell you how or why this works.
cues.zh: 我实在说不清楚这是为何以及是如何做到的。

cues.en: I can't tell you that there's anything to follow.
cues.zh: 我也无法断言这其中有什么规律可循。

cues.en: But I will say, we made the things that we loved.
cues.zh: 但我可以肯定，我们创作的是自己热爱的作品。

cues.en: We never questioned if anyone else was going to like it.
cues.zh: 我们从未考虑过是否会有其他人喜欢它。

cues.en: We never questioned what the audience was going to think.
cues.zh: 我们从未考虑过观众会作何评价。

cues.en: We never questioned where does it fit in the market.
cues.zh: 我们从未考虑过它在市场中的定位如何。

cues.en: None of those normal conversations.
cues.zh: 完全没有进行过那些常规的讨论。

cues.en: We made our favorite thing.
cues.zh: 我们创作了自己最钟爱的作品。

cues.en: We took it to an indefensible level as far as we could go.
cues.zh: 我们竭尽全力，将其提升到无可超越的水平。

cues.en: And luckily, it worked out.
cues.zh: 幸运的是，事情最终有了好结果。

cues.en: Is there a way to get clearer on what you love?
cues.zh: 有没有什么方法能更清楚地知道自己热爱什么？

cues.en: This sounds like a strange question.
cues.zh: 这听起来像是个奇怪的问题。

cues.en: Meditate.
cues.zh: 冥想吧。

cues.en: Meditate.
cues.zh: 冥想吧。

cues.en: I learned to meditate when I was 14.
cues.zh: 我是在14岁的时候学会冥想的。

cues.en: And I think having a TM as a grounding element in
cues.zh: 而且我觉得把超验冥想当作一种

cues.en: my life.
cues.zh: 我生活中的安定力量。

cues.en: TM.
cues.zh: 超验冥想。

cues.en: A transcendental meditation.
cues.zh: 就是那种超验冥想。

cues.en: That was the first type of meditation I learned when I was 14.
cues.zh: 那是我在14岁时学到的第一种冥想方式。

cues.en: It changed me.
cues.zh: 它改变了我。

cues.en: I know this because I stopped meditating when I went to college.
cues.zh: 我知道这一点，是因为我上大学后就不再冥想了。

cues.en: And then when I moved to California, right after college, I started meditating again.
cues.zh: 大学毕业后我搬到加利福尼亚后，又开始冥想。

cues.en: Somewhere I knew it was a big decision, and somewhere I knew there would be a right moment to start.
cues.zh: 一方面我知道这是个重大的决定，另一方面我也知道总会有合适的时机开始。

cues.en: And it took several months before I actually sat for the first meditation after not doing it for several years.
cues.zh: 在停练好几年之后，我过了几个月才真正坐下来进行第一次冥想。

cues.en: And in that first meditation, I realized, oh, this is very familiar to me.
cues.zh: 在那第一次冥想中，我意识到，哦，这对我来说非常熟悉。

cues.en: This is a big part of who I am, even though I haven't done it in five years.
cues.zh: 尽管我已经五年没有冥想了，但它仍是构成我自我的重要部分。

cues.en: It's a big part of how I see the world.
cues.zh: 它也影响着我看待世界的方式。

cues.en: The fact that I got to do that from a young age.
cues.zh: 我很庆幸能从小就开始做这件事。

cues.en: To understand who you are with it, I'm going to ask you who you would be without it.
cues.zh: 为了通过它了解你是谁，我要问你，如果没有它你会是谁。

cues.en: I don't know.
cues.zh: 我不知道。

cues.en: I'm curious.
cues.zh: 我很好奇。

cues.en: I'm happy that I don't know because I like having the practice.
cues.zh: 我很高兴自己不知道，因为我喜欢这种冥想练习。

cues.en: But whether I continue a practice or not, I've done enough of it over the course of my life that I'm
cues.zh: 不过无论我是否继续坚持这种练习，我这辈子已经做了足够多的次数，所以我现在

cues.en: there.
cues.zh: 已经达到了那个境界。

cues.en: When I meditate more, it gets deeper.
cues.zh: 当我冥想得更多时，这种体验会愈发深刻。

cues.en: But even if I don't meditate, it's like Maharishi, teacher of transcendental meditation, Maharishi Mahesh Yogi, says
cues.zh: 但即便我不冥想，正如超觉静坐的导师马哈里希·马赫什·尤吉所说

cues.en: every time you meditate, it's like making a deposit in the bank.
cues.zh: 每次冥想都像是往银行存钱一样。

cues.en: So it builds up.
cues.zh: 这样就能逐渐积累起来。

cues.en: And again, that was rhetoric before, but in my experience, I got to see, oh, it's not rhetoric.
cues.zh: 之前那只是说说而已，但根据我的亲身经历，我发现哦，那并非空话。

cues.en: Like I actually had this experience.
cues.zh: 因为我确实有过这样的体验。

cues.en: And it changed the way I saw the world.
cues.zh: 它改变了我看待世界的方式。

cues.en: And I'll say, you see beyond the surface.
cues.zh: 我想说，你能看到表面之下的东西。

cues.en: You can see the depth underneath.
cues.zh: 你能洞察到其深处的本质。

cues.en: And for me, the things on the surface are not so interesting.
cues.zh: 对我来说，表面上的东西已经没那么有趣了。

cues.en: I'm interested in the depth, the depth behind it.
cues.zh: 我感兴趣的是其背后的深度，那种深层的意义。

cues.en: So my first question would be, what is transcendental meditation?
cues.zh: 那么我的第一个问题就是，什么是超觉静坐？

cues.en: It's a mantra practice that's done silently.
cues.zh: 这是一种以默念方式进行的修行。

cues.en: You do it sitting with your eyes closed.
cues.zh: 练习时需要闭着眼睛坐着。

cues.en: You learn it from a TM teacher.
cues.zh: 你需要向一位超觉静坐导师学习它。

cues.en: I can't teach it to you.
cues.zh: 我无法教你这种方法。

cues.en: We close our eyes, and then the mantra is a sound vibration that gets given to
cues.zh: 我们闭上眼睛，然后那个咒语会以声波的形式传递给

cues.en: you.
cues.zh: 你。

cues.en: I was given mine when I was 14.
cues.zh: 我在14岁的时候得到了属于自己的咒语。

cues.en: I have never uttered it out loud since that time.
cues.zh: 从那以后我就再也没有大声念过它。

cues.en: I've never shared it with anyone, and that's part of the training.
cues.zh: 我也从未向任何人透露过它，这也是训练内容的一部分。

cues.en: It's like a private sound, and you...
cues.zh: 它就像一种私密的音声，而你……

cues.en: engage with this sound in the way that you're taught, 20 minutes, at least once a day, typically twice a
cues.zh: 按照所学的方法去接触这种声音，每天至少一次，每次20分钟，通常是一天两次。

cues.en: day.
cues.zh: 一天两次。

cues.en: I would do it right when I woke up in the morning and then again before dinner.
cues.zh: 我会在早上醒来后立刻做，然后在晚餐前再做一次。

cues.en: Those would be the two windows.
cues.zh: 那就是两个固定的时间段。

cues.en: When I lived in California and I was working in different recording studios, I meditated with Tom Petty
cues.zh: 我住在加利福尼亚时，在不同的录音室工作，我会在录制前和汤姆·佩蒂、

cues.en: and Johnny Cash and different artists before sessions.
cues.zh: 约翰尼·卡什以及其他艺人一起冥想。

cues.en: That would be part of our practice, Red Hot Chili Peppers.
cues.zh: 那也是红热辣椒乐队练习的一部分。

cues.en: We would sit and meditate together before sessions.
cues.zh: 我们会在录制前一起坐下来冥想。

cues.en: So I've had this experience for a while in my life, and it's probably the most profound thing I can mention.
cues.zh: 我一生中已经有过这样的体验，这可能是我能提及的最有意义的事情了。

cues.en: We'll get to others, but that's one that's a learnable, practicable action that really changed who I am.
cues.zh: 我们还会谈到其他方法，但这是其中一种可以通过学习并付诸实践、真正改变我的人生态度的方法。

cues.en: How did you know it was efficacious?
cues.zh: 您是怎么知道它有效的？

cues.en: How did you know it was working?
cues.zh: 您是怎么知道它起作用的？

cues.en: What is the measure that this practice is worth that investment in time, in your view?
cues.zh: 在您看来，这项练习值得投入时间，其价值体现在哪些方面？

cues.en: The only proof that I had was getting away from it and coming back to it.
cues.zh: 我唯一的证明就是暂时远离它，然后再重新回到它面前。

cues.en: That was, I recognized it in that first meditation back, how deep and connected I was to this thing.
cues.zh: 也就是说，在那第一次重新冥想时，我意识到自己与这件事的联结有多深、有多紧密。

cues.en: And I'm guessing this unlocked, you said a deeper level, a deeper level of creativity and ideas.
cues.zh: 我猜这开启了某种更深的层次，也就是更深入的创造力和创意。

cues.en: Everything.
cues.zh: 所有方面。

cues.en: Oh.
cues.zh: 哦。

cues.en: Everything.
cues.zh: 所有方面。

cues.en: Deeper understanding.
cues.zh: 更深入的理解。

cues.en: People often hear that meditation in various forms is beneficial.
cues.zh: 人们常常听说各种形式的冥想都有益处。

cues.en: Very successful people sit here all the time and say it's so central to why I've been able to do what I've done.
cues.zh: 许多非常成功的人总是说，冥想是我能够取得成就的关键所在。

cues.en: And then there'll be people, you know, that think, well, I was sitting there for 10 minutes.
cues.zh: 但也有一些人会想，我就坐了10分钟而已。

cues.en: My brain is very, very busy.
cues.zh: 我的大脑已经非常非常忙碌了。

cues.en: I tried it once.
cues.zh: 我试过一次。

cues.en: It didn't really work.
cues.zh: 那方法并没有真正起作用。

cues.en: And then they move on.
cues.zh: 然后他们就继续前进了。

cues.en: And then I study some of the great creatives in the world, the great visionaries, people that I thought could see round corners in an atypical way, like Steve Jobs.
cues.zh: 接着我研究了世界上一些伟大的创客和远见卓识的人，那些我认为能够以非传统方式预见未来的人，比如史蒂夫·乔布斯。

cues.en: And there's always a practice, a meditation practice, well, so often at the very heart of their brilliance.
cues.zh: 他们的卓越才华背后，往往都有一种练习，也就是冥想练习。

cues.en: So I don't currently have a meditation practice.
cues.zh: 目前我还没有进行冥想练习的习惯。

cues.en: My wonderful fiance does.
cues.zh: 我可爱的未婚妻有这个习惯。

cues.en: She does it every morning for 20 minutes.
cues.zh: 她每天早上都会冥想20分钟。

cues.en: She's a breathwork practitioner.
cues.zh: 她是一名呼吸法练习者。

cues.en: So, I mean, it's her whole world.
cues.zh: 可以说，这完全就是她的世界。

cues.en: And tell me what she says about it.
cues.zh: 告诉我她是怎么说的。

cues.en: She says it unlocks a deeper level of calm.
cues.zh: 她说冥想能让人获得更深层次的平静。

cues.en: And I don't mean calm as in like stress.
cues.zh: 我说的平静并非指没有压力的状态。

cues.en: I mean a deeper level of like groundedness.
cues.zh: 我指的是一种更深层次的安定感。

cues.en: And she says, She feels more connected.
cues.zh: 她说，自己感觉与周围有了更紧密的联系。

cues.en: Now in her context, I think that's more of like a spiritual thing.
cues.zh: 在她的视角里，我觉得这更偏向于一种精神层面的感受。

cues.en: She feels more connected to the universe and others.
cues.zh: 她觉得自己与宇宙以及他人之间的联系更紧密了。

cues.en: As far as the creative experience goes, a spiritual connection is a big part of that.
cues.zh: 就创造过程而言，这种精神上的联结是其中非常重要的一部分。

cues.en: It's just the nature of how it works.
cues.zh: 这就是它运作的本质。

cues.en: It's not an intellectual process.
cues.zh: 这不是一个纯粹的智力过程。

cues.en: It's a spiritual process.
cues.zh: 而是一个精神层面的过程。

cues.en: What is the mechanism?
cues.zh: 那么其机制是什么？

cues.en: that is causing these results that you see?
cues.zh: 就是导致你看到这些结果的那个原因吗？

cues.en: From a biological perspective?
cues.zh: 从生物学角度来讲呢？

cues.en: I couldn't answer that in the way that you would hope, but I will say, I think it allows you to let go
cues.zh: 我无法用你们期望的方式回答这个问题，但我可以这么说，我认为这种做法能让你放下执念。

cues.en: of all of the ordinary concerns.
cues.zh: 放下所有那些平常的忧虑。

cues.en: I also have a question, which is, if you live with a person who says this practice is so impactful
cues.zh: 我也有个问题，那就是，如果你和某个声称这种练习对她的生活影响极大的人住在一起，

cues.en: on her life, I'm questioning why you at least haven't tried it with her for a month to see.
cues.zh: 我就在想，你为什么至少不试着和她一起练习一个月看看呢。

cues.en: No,
cues.zh: 不。

cues.en: it's a good question.
cues.zh: 这是个好问题。

cues.en: I have no good answer for it.
cues.zh: 我也没有合适的答案。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Because it's what it has to do with it.
cues.zh: 因为事情本来就是如此。

cues.en: It's you're not looking for cues from the outside.
cues.zh: 因为你不会向外寻求线索。

cues.en: You're looking for cues on the inside.
cues.zh: 你会向内心寻找线索。

cues.en: What lights you up?
cues.zh: 什么能让你充满热情？

cues.en: What are you excited to play for your friend?
cues.zh: 你愿意为朋友玩什么游戏而感到兴奋？

cues.en: Not what are you excited to play for your friend?
cues.zh: 不是你愿意为朋友玩什么游戏而感到兴奋吗？

cues.en: Like, what do you think this will do?
cues.zh: 比如，你觉得这会带来什么效果？

cues.en: You play it for your friend like, wow, can you believe something like this exists in the world?
cues.zh: 你为朋友玩这个游戏的时候，会感叹：哇，真不敢相信世界上居然有这样的东西存在。

cues.en: How cool is that?
cues.zh: 那有多酷啊？

cues.en: The distinction that I'm trying to make is often if you read business books or entrepreneurship books, when they're talking about innovation, when they're talking about the great companies like Amazon,
cues.zh: 我想要区分的是，如果你阅读商业类或创业类的书籍，当它们谈论创新，谈论亚马逊这样的伟大企业时，

cues.en: or I heard Sebastian, who's the CEO of Klarna say the other day, who's a tech founder, they spend a lot of time.
cues.zh: 或者我前几天听到Klarna的CEO塞巴斯蒂安说过，他也是位科技行业创业者，他们会花大量时间，

cues.en: thinking about the customer, the customer's problem, and they work backwards, they call it, to the answer.
cues.zh: 思考客户的需求以及客户面临的问题，然后从问题出发反向推导出解决方案。

cues.en: So they'll zoom in on Rick's world and say, Rick has these problems, he's da-da-da-da, and they'll work backwards from there to a answer.
cues.zh: 所以他们会聚焦在里克所处的领域，认为里克有这些问题，接着从这些问题反向推导出答案。

cues.en: That's how Amazon say they built the platform.
cues.zh: 亚马逊就是这么宣称自己构建该平台的。

cues.en: And one of the quotes that's quite famous with Jeff Bezos is he bets on things that he knows won't change.
cues.zh: 杰夫·贝索斯有一句非常有名的话，他说自己会投资那些他知道不会改变的事物。

cues.en: He says, no one in 10 years is going to come up to me and say, I wish my package would take longer.
cues.zh: 他说，10年后不会有人来找我，说希望自己的包裹能多花点时间送达。

cues.en: So you can double down on that as solving a customer problem.
cues.zh: 所以你可以把这一点当作解决客户问题的关键策略来加倍投入。

cues.en: Does that sit in contrast to what you're saying, or is it the same thing, or is it a different type of work?
cues.zh: 这和你之前说的观点相矛盾吗？还是说其实是一回事，又或者属于不同类型的工作？

cues.en: Well, I'll start by saying if you look at the history of Amazon, it lost money for probably 20 years.
cues.zh: 首先我要说的是，如果回顾亚马逊的发展史，它大概有20年的时间都在亏损。

cues.en: It was considered one of the worst investments until it wasn't.
cues.zh: 它曾被视为最糟糕的投资之一，直到后来情况发生了变化。

cues.en: They kept doubling down on what they believed in.
cues.zh: 他们始终坚持在自己坚信的事情上加倍投入。

cues.en: It wasn't working.
cues.zh: 那时的方法并不起作用。

cues.en: The audience showed it didn't work.
cues.zh: 市场反馈也表明它行不通。

cues.en: The model showed it didn't work, but they stuck to what they believed.
cues.zh: 业务模式显示它没有效果，但他们依然坚守自己的信念。

cues.en: And it changed the world.
cues.zh: 最终它改变了世界。

cues.en: So it's the same thing.
cues.zh: 所以其实是一回事。

cues.en: It's doubling down on what you believe in when all of the metrics are showing you it's not working.
cues.zh: 那就是在所有指标都显示方法无效时，依然坚持自己所相信的东西并加倍投入。

cues.en: That's the story of Amazon.
cues.zh: 这就是亚马逊的故事。

cues.en: Do you think people have different levels of their ability to, you know, if we take practices like meditation aside, it just seems that
cues.zh: 你认为人们在某种能力上存在差异吗？我的意思是，先不考虑冥想之类的练习，看起来

cues.en: through history, some people are better at cultivating that.
cues.zh: 在历史长河中，有些人比其他人更擅长培养这种能力。

cues.en: or listening to that internal voice than others.
cues.zh: 或者说更擅长倾听内心的声音。

cues.en: Obviously, I sit here and interview some of these great founders, and it appears that some people are just inherently more creative than others.
cues.zh: 显然，我坐在这里采访这些伟大的创始人，发现确实有些人天生就比其他人更有创造力。

cues.en: Some people are in the analytical part of their brain, and they need one plus one to be equal to all the time.
cues.zh: 有些人更偏向大脑的逻辑分析部分，他们总是需要一加一等于二这样的确定性。

cues.en: I'm wondering if there's other ways, if you think there is an inherent difference in creativity.
cues.zh: 我在想，如果创造力确实存在先天差异，是否还有其他途径？

cues.en: I think that creativity is beaten out of us over the course of our lives.
cues.zh: 我认为创造力是在我们的一生中被逐渐磨灭的。

cues.en: I think we go to school, we're told to repeat back what we're told.
cues.zh: 我们上学时，总是被要求复述别人告诉我们的内容。

cues.en: We're told to sit in a chair all day.
cues.zh: 我们还被要求一整天都坐在椅子上。

cues.en: Our spirits are broken by institutions.
cues.zh: 各种制度摧毁了我们的创造力。

cues.en: We're not taught to be free creative thinkers.
cues.zh: 我们从未被教导过如何成为自由且富有创造力的思考者。

cues.en: We're taught to follow rules.
cues.zh: 我们被教导要遵守规则。

cues.en: The rules are not there to help us.
cues.zh: 这些规则并非为了帮助我们。

cues.en: The rules are there to control us.
cues.zh: 这些规则是为了控制我们。

cues.en: I'm suggesting we break free and be free and express ourselves freely and that's our purpose here on
cues.zh: 我建议我们挣脱束缚，自由地表达自我，这正是我们身处此地的目的。

cues.en: the planet is to express ourselves freely that's why we're here what you're saying links to something we're talking about earlier which is at a very young age we're taught that the things
cues.zh: 在地球上，我们的目的就是自由表达自我，这就是我们存在的原因。你所说的与我们之前讨论的内容有关，那就是在很小的时候，我们就被教导说我们创造的东西

cues.en: we make are a means to a particular end and that end is promotions pay rises capital success job titles yes In the creative process,
cues.zh: 只是达成某种特定目标的手段，而那个目标就是晋升、加薪、资本积累、事业成功以及各种头衔。但在创造过程中，

cues.en: are you saying that it's never productive to talk about how we'll measure success and to try and optimize for that measurement?
cues.zh: 你是说，讨论如何衡量成功并试图为此优化根本没有任何意义吗？

cues.en: In the creative process, I tend not to think about those things.
cues.zh: 在创造过程中，我通常不会去考虑那些事情。

cues.en: I can't think of an example where we would want to use data.
cues.zh: 我想不出有任何情况是我们会想要使用数据的。

cues.en: I think it's much more about this internal feeling and then the feeling we have.
cues.zh: 我觉得这更多关乎一种内在的感觉，以及我们自身的感受。

cues.en: When you play it for someone, when you share it with someone, whether it lights someone up, you can tell when someone really resonates
cues.zh: 当你把作品展示给别人，或者与他人分享时，如果它能点燃某人的热情，你就能知道这个人是否真的被

cues.en: with something.
cues.zh: 某样东西打动了。

cues.en: Sometimes the numbers don't show, the numbers can't reflect that.
cues.zh: 有时候数据无法体现这一点，数字并不能反映实际情况。

cues.en: You know, you can have two things that are kind of on equal footing commercially, yet one of them lights you
cues.zh: 你知道，有些事物在商业层面或许处于同等地位，但其中一种会让你充满热情。

cues.en: up.
cues.zh: 开始。

cues.en: And the other one is, well, this gets a job done.
cues.zh: 而另一种则只是能完成工作而已。

cues.en: They're different.
cues.zh: 它们是不同的。

cues.en: And long-term, chances are, the one that lights you up is going to have more value to you and you'll be more willing
cues.zh: 从长远来看，那种能让你充满热情的事物往往会对你更有价值，你也更愿意

cues.en: to support that thing over time.
cues.zh: 长期支持它。

cues.en: In your book here, The Creative Act, A Way of Being, you talk about the things that block creativity.
cues.zh: 在你的著作《创造的行为：一种存在方式》中，你谈到了阻碍创造力的因素。

cues.en: Thoughts and habits not conducive to the work.
cues.zh: 那些不利于创造工作的想法和习惯。

cues.en: Believing you're not good enough.
cues.zh: 认为自己不够优秀。

cues.en: That's a big one.
cues.zh: 这是个很重要的因素。

cues.en: Someone at some point in time, you were singing and someone's like, ah, you can't sing.
cues.zh: 曾经在某个时候，你正在唱歌，却有人对你说，啊，你不会唱歌。

cues.en: When you're a kid and that gets lodged in you, singing is not something I can ever do, or you're a terrible cook, or you're
cues.zh: 小时候如果这种观念深植于心，就会觉得唱歌是我永远做不来的事，或者觉得自己厨艺很差，又或者觉得自己

cues.en: not smart enough.
cues.zh: 不够聪明。

cues.en: So often the gifts that we have are stifled and smothered.
cues.zh: 很多时候，我们与生俱来的天赋都会被压制、扼杀。

cues.en: We're all creative.
cues.zh: 我们所有人都具有创造力。

cues.en: We may not choose to embark on a creative, make creative choices, but that's,
cues.zh: 我们或许不会主动选择走创造性的道路、做出创造性的选择，但那其实是

cues.en: it's on us.
cues.zh: 取决于我们自己。

cues.en: We can, we just have bad information.
cues.zh: 我们是能够做到的，只是得到的信息有误。

cues.en: We're told we're not good enough and we believe it.
cues.zh: 别人告诉我们我们不够好，我们就信了。

cues.en: And it's not true.
cues.zh: 但那并不是事实。

cues.en: When people say that, oh, you know, Rick is a creative and Stephen is, they say Stephen is not a creative.
cues.zh: 当人们说‘里克很有创造力，而史蒂芬没有’的时候，

cues.en: What are they actually saying?
cues.zh: 他们到底想表达什么？

cues.en: What is that like in our culture to be a creative?
cues.zh: 在我们的文化里，成为有创造力的人意味着什么？

cues.en: How are like we misunderstanding the definition?
cues.zh: 我们究竟是如何误解这个定义的？

cues.en: See what I'm saying?
cues.zh: 明白我的意思了吗？

cues.en: Because we do, we go creative.
cues.zh: 正因如此，我们才会去发挥创造力。

cues.en: They do a little bit of art and music stuff, creative, not creative, Excel documents, creative.
cues.zh: 他们会做一些艺术和音乐相关的事情，有的有创造力，有的没有，还有Excel文档，也有创造性的。

cues.en: What are we actually saying there?
cues.zh: 我们实际上想表达的是什么？

cues.en: I think it's a way to,
cues.zh: 我觉得这是一种

cues.en: try to simplify the world.
cues.zh: 试图简化世界的方式。

cues.en: The world is complicated and I think all of us can do anything.
cues.zh: 世界很复杂，但我认为我们每个人都能做任何事。

cues.en: I'm not saying all of us could do everything to the best of our ability better than anyone else.
cues.zh: 我不是说我们所有人都能以比别人更好的水平做好所有事。

cues.en: That's a big part of it is the idea of competition.
cues.zh: 其中很重要的一个因素就是竞争的观念。

cues.en: Like if I want to play baseball, I know that I could get better at baseball.
cues.zh: 比如如果我想打棒球，我知道自己可以变得更擅长棒球。

cues.en: That doesn't mean I think I could get good enough to play on the Mets, but I know I could get better and I know I could train anything that
cues.zh: 这并不意味着我觉得自己能强到可以加入大都会队，但我知道我可以变得更好，也知道我可以训练任何技能。

cues.en: I'm interested in and get much better at it.
cues.zh: 我对它很感兴趣，而且水平也在不断提升。

cues.en: And as soon as we're not capable of playing for the Mets, we think it's not for us and we shut that off.
cues.zh: 一旦我们觉得自己没有能力为大都会队效力，就会认为这不适合自己，于是就此放弃。

cues.en: We're not doing a service to ourselves.
cues.zh: 这样对我们自己没有任何好处。

cues.en: We're not becoming our best selves or really living up to our full potential as humans.
cues.zh: 我们既无法成为最好的自己，也无法充分发挥作为人类的全部潜力。

cues.en: It feels like a natural human instinct to compare.
cues.zh: 比较似乎是一种天然的人类本能。

cues.en: in order to understand the value of anything i think we do it when we go to restaurants there's three steaks the expensive one's probably a bit bougie the cheap one's probably not
cues.zh: 为了了解任何事物的价值，我觉得我们会在去餐厅时这么做：那里有三块牛排，贵的那块可能比较高档，便宜的那块可能就不怎么样。

cues.en: good i'll go for the middle one seems like a way that humans take shortcuts but we do it with ourselves as well so i know that the thing i've made is good as if i look over at
cues.zh: 好吧，那我就选中间的那块。这似乎是人类常用的捷径，但我们对自己也会这么做，这样我就能确定自己做出来的东西是不错的，哪怕我只是看看

cues.en: your thing and mine is ranked better or mine is prettier or richer Are you saying for us
cues.zh: 你的东西和我的相比，谁的排名更高，或者谁的更漂亮、更高级。你是说对我们来说

cues.en: to get out of the business of comparison?
cues.zh: 应该停止比较吗？

cues.en: Yes, because I'm saying it's always apples and oranges.
cues.zh: 是的，因为我觉得这永远都是苹果和橙子的比较。

cues.en: If you were to ask who's better, Michael Jackson or Prince, I would say Michael Jackson's much better at being Michael Jackson.
cues.zh: 如果你问谁更出色，迈克尔·杰克逊还是普林斯，我会说迈克尔·杰克逊在扮演自己这个角色上要出色得多。

cues.en: And Prince is probably better at being Prince.
cues.zh: 而普林斯可能在扮演自己这个角色上更出色。

cues.en: But you can't compare what the two of them do.
cues.zh: 但这两个人做的事情是无法相提并论的。

cues.en: They do two different things.
cues.zh: 他们做的是两件完全不同的事情。

cues.en: Before you mentioned Kanye West and Drake.
cues.zh: 你之前提到了坎耶·韦斯特和德雷克。

cues.en: There's no competition there.
cues.zh: 他们之间不存在竞争关系。

cues.en: They do two totally different things.
cues.zh: 他们做的确实是两件截然不同的事情。

cues.en: What you get from each of them is totally different.
cues.zh: 从他们每个人那里得到的东西也完全不同。

cues.en: I wouldn't want from Drake what I get from Kanye, and I certainly wouldn't want from Kanye what I get from Drake.
cues.zh: 我不会从德雷克那里得到我从坎耶那里得到的东西，当然也不会从坎耶那里得到我从德雷克那里得到的东西。

cues.en: It's pointless.
cues.zh: 那样做毫无意义。

cues.en: Is either more creative?
cues.zh: 那两个人谁更有创造力呢？

cues.en: That's for you to decide.
cues.zh: 这得由你来说定。

cues.en: That's for you to decide.
cues.zh: 这还是得由你来说定。

cues.en: The whole idea of competition between artists, it's such a weird thing.
cues.zh: 艺术家之间互相竞争这种想法，实在是很奇怪。

cues.en: Again, it's back to who has a better diary entry.
cues.zh: 再说一次，又回到了谁的日记写得更好这个问题上。

cues.en: It's ridiculous.
cues.zh: 这太荒谬了。

cues.en: Feeling you don't have the energy it takes.
cues.zh: 感觉自己没有足够的精力。

cues.en: These are all things that are not conducive to the work.
cues.zh: 这些都是不利于工作的因素。

cues.en: Yeah, I have that one sometimes.
cues.zh: 是的，我有时也会这样。

cues.en: Feeling like I'm not up to it too much.
cues.zh: 感觉自己常常力不从心。

cues.en: I flew here yesterday from London.
cues.zh: 我昨天从伦敦飞到了这里。

cues.en: I'm tired.
cues.zh: 我好累。

cues.en: I'm a little jet lagged.
cues.zh: 我有点时差反应。

cues.en: I'm going to show up and talk to you.
cues.zh: 我会出现并和你们交谈的。

cues.en: Maybe it won't be good.
cues.zh: 也许效果不会很好。

cues.en: Maybe it's better to just lay down, relax, and recover.
cues.zh: 或许最好还是躺下来休息，恢复体力。

cues.en: But I'm here.
cues.zh: 但我在这里。

cues.en: I show up.
cues.zh: 我会准时出现。

cues.en: You've referred to yourself as a lazy workaholic.
cues.zh: 你曾称自己为懒惰的工作狂。

cues.en: It's true.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: What is a lazy workaholic?
cues.zh: 什么是懒惰的工作狂？

cues.en: Often, most days, I would rather not do any of the things that I'm scheduled to do.
cues.zh: 通常，大多数日子里，我都不想去做那些安排好的事情。

cues.en: And I schedule the things, and I show up, and I do what needs to get done.
cues.zh: 我会把事情安排好，然后出现，把该完成的工作做完。

cues.en: Do you ever settle with creative work?
cues.zh: 你会满足于创意工作吗？

cues.en: The deadline for the record label is approaching.
cues.zh: 唱片公司的截止日期快到了。

cues.en: The work is not yet done.
cues.zh: 工作还沒有完成。

cues.en: We'll finish here and we'll send it.
cues.zh: 我们在这里做完就发过去。

cues.en: I tend not to do that.
cues.zh: 我一般不会那样做。

cues.en: I tend not to work on deadlines until we're past the point.
cues.zh: 我通常不会在截止日期到来之前就开始工作。

cues.en: The first time we would ever establish a deadline is when we already know.
cues.zh: 我们第一次设定截止日期，是在已经确定结果的时候。

cues.en: We've cracked the code.
cues.zh: 我们已经破解了难题。

cues.en: We know what this is going to be.
cues.zh: 我们知道最终成果会是什么样子。

cues.en: We can see it.
cues.zh: 我们能够预见到它。

cues.en: It may not be completely finished.
cues.zh: 它可能还没有完全完成。

cues.en: But we have a good idea of what it is and how it's going to work.
cues.zh: 但我们对它的形态以及运作方式已经有比较清晰的认知。

cues.en: And it's maybe 90% done.
cues.zh: 大概已经有90%完成了。

cues.en: Then we might set a deadline for that last 10% of finishing it.
cues.zh: 这时我们才会为剩下的10%设定一个截止日期。

cues.en: And that last 10% probably won't make or break the project.
cues.zh: 而那最后的10%往往并不会决定整个项目的成败。

cues.en: Part of what you accept when you pursue the creative process you've described, where it's really about like, do I like it?
cues.zh: 在追求你所说的那种创作过程时，需要接受的一点就是，重点其实在于——我喜欢它吗？

cues.en: Do we like it?
cues.zh: 我们喜欢它吗？

cues.en: You will create things that are at some points just absolute legendary and unlike anything else that exists.
cues.zh: 你创造出的作品，有时会变得极其传奇，完全不同于世间任何其他存在。

cues.en: They are not the same.
cues.zh: 它们是不一样的。

cues.en: But part of the risk you take is you'll make things that other people just don't like.
cues.zh: 但你承担的风险之一，就是可能会做出别人根本不喜欢的东西。

cues.en: That's all there is in this process is you have an idea, you build it.
cues.zh: 整个过程就是先有个想法，然后去把它实现出来。

cues.en: You may learn along the way that the idea was maybe not the best idea and it turns left and you make, I'm starting out to make this blue statue and
cues.zh: 在过程中你可能会发现，原来的想法或许并非最佳选择，于是方向会改变，比如我一开始打算制作这座蓝色雕像，

cues.en: it turns out to be this red painting.
cues.zh: 结果却变成了一幅红色画作。

cues.en: You don't know that going in, but you discover it through the process and it could take a long time.
cues.zh: 一开始你并不知道，但会在过程中逐渐发现，而且这个过程可能需要很长时间。

cues.en: Other times you'll think I'm going to make this blue thing.
cues.zh: 有时候你会觉得我要制作那个蓝色的东西。

cues.en: You make it in five minutes.
cues.zh: 五分钟之内你就做完了。

cues.en: There it is done.
cues.zh: 看，已经做好了。

cues.en: And, and we can't, you can't calculate that.
cues.zh: 而且，这是无法预测的，根本算不出来。

cues.en: You can't anticipate what's going to happen.
cues.zh: 你不可能预知接下来会发生什么。

cues.en: But if I wasn't doing this experiment here, I would never get to the better thing.
cues.zh: 但要是我没有在这里做这个实验，就永远无法找到更好的方法。

cues.en: It happens all the time.
cues.zh: 这种事情随时都会发生。

cues.en: And then sometimes you build it.
cues.zh: 然后有时候你会去构建它。

cues.en: and it doesn't work for 20 years, and then it becomes Amazon.
cues.zh: 它可能20年都不起作用，之后才会发展成亚马逊那样。

cues.en: I've thought a lot recently about how time horizons change the work that you do.
cues.zh: 最近我一直在思考时间视野是如何改变我们所做工作的。

cues.en: And that's kind of also what I'm hearing there, because in that example you gave of this blue statue thing, if you were under a time horizon, you wouldn't have the space for that exploration
cues.zh: 我在那里也听到了类似的观点，因为在你举的那个蓝色雕像的例子中，如果受时间视野的限制，就根本没有空间去进行你描述的那种探索。

cues.en: you've described.
cues.zh: 你刚才已经描述过了。

cues.en: And actually in all of our lives, we, I think, apply time horizons.
cues.zh: 实际上，在我们每个人的生活中，我想都会运用时间视野。

cues.en: We say, this part of my career is going to be five years.
cues.zh: 我们会说，我职业生涯的这一阶段将持续五年。

cues.en: And in those five years, I want to achieve these things.
cues.zh: 在这五年里，我想要实现这些目标。

cues.en: How do you think about setting personal time horizons, but also like creative time horizons?
cues.zh: 你觉得该如何设定个人的时间视野，同时也要设定创造性的时间视野呢？

cues.en: One of the things I talk about in the book is that there are different phases of creativity.
cues.zh: 我在书中提到的一点是，创造力存在不同的阶段。

cues.en: The first phase is the seed phase.
cues.zh: 第一阶段是种子阶段。

cues.en: Then is the experimentation phase.
cues.zh: 接着是实验阶段。

cues.en: Then is the crafting phase.
cues.zh: 然后是打造阶段。

cues.en: And then is the finishing, completion, editorial phase.
cues.zh: 最后是完成、定稿以及编辑阶段。

cues.en: And you can't set a timeline early in that process.
cues.zh: 在流程的早期是无法确定时间表的。

cues.en: In the seed phase...
cues.zh: 在种子阶段……

cues.en: You have to try a lot of things and it's going to take as long as it takes.
cues.zh: 你必须尝试很多方法，所需时间也会随情况而定。

cues.en: And in the experimental phase, which is where you're taking the seeds and seeing what they want to be, that takes time.
cues.zh: 在实验阶段，也就是让这些种子展现其发展可能性的阶段，这同样需要时间。

cues.en: And then in the crafting phase, the third phase, it still takes time because now you have the seed, you see what it wants to be, you've given it time to gestate, you
cues.zh: 到了第三阶段的打造阶段，依然需要时间，因为此时你已经有了种子，看到了它的潜在形态，也给了它足够的时间成长，

cues.en: see how it grows.
cues.zh: 观察它的变化。

cues.en: And now in the crafting phase, third phase, you start trimming it and making it the way you see it.
cues.zh: 在第三阶段的打造阶段，你开始对其进行修剪，使其变成你期望的样子。

cues.en: All of that has to happen before there's any idea of a timeline.
cues.zh: 所有这些都必须完成之后，才能考虑时间表的问题。

cues.en: Because until that time, you don't really know what you're making.
cues.zh: 因为在那之前，你其实并不知道自己正在创造什么。

cues.en: It's a dream.
cues.zh: 那只是一个梦想。

cues.en: But once you've gone through these three phases, and you have this thing in front of you, it may not be finished, but you see what it is.
cues.zh: 但一旦你经历了这三个阶段，眼前出现了这个东西，它可能还尚未完成，但你已经看清了它的模样。

cues.en: You see it, and it's good.
cues.zh: 你看到了它，而且它很不错。

cues.en: You're excited about it.
cues.zh: 你会为此感到兴奋。

cues.en: When I say it's good, I mean it's good to me.
cues.zh: 当我说它不错时，指的是它对我来说不错。

cues.en: That's it.
cues.zh: 就是这样。

cues.en: That's where it ends.
cues.zh: 到此为止了。

cues.en: It's good to me.
cues.zh: 它对我来说不错。

cues.en: I like it enough that I'm willing to show it to you.
cues.zh: 我足够喜欢它，所以愿意展示给你看。

cues.en: If I like it enough that I'm willing to show it to you, I like it enough to show it to everybody.
cues.zh: 如果我足够喜欢它，愿意展示给你看，那就意味着我足够喜欢它，愿意展示给所有人看。

cues.en: People will hear this as creative advice.
cues.zh: 人们会把这当作关于创造力的建议来听。

cues.en: I was hearing it as life advice.
cues.zh: 我当时把它当作人生建议来听。

cues.en: I was hearing the seed phase of my life, the experimentation phase of my life, the crafting phase.
cues.zh: 我把它视为我人生中的种子期、实验期以及创作期。

cues.en: It's the same.
cues.zh: 其实是一样的。

cues.en: It's all the same.
cues.zh: 全都是一样的。

cues.en: And that's why the creative act started with this idea of how to make things.
cues.zh: 正因如此，创造行为最初就是从如何创造事物的想法开始的。

cues.en: And it turned, what I realized through writing the book is, it's how to be in the world.
cues.zh: 通过写这本书我意识到，其实创造就是如何活在世间。

cues.en: That you either live your life to allow these things to happen, or you don't.
cues.zh: 要么让这些事情发生，要么就不让它们发生。

cues.en: And if you live your life to allow these things to happen, then you're an artist.
cues.zh: 如果你让这些事情发生，那你就是一名艺术家。

cues.en: Even if you're a businessman or if you're a chef or if you're a mother, you're living your life as an artist.
cues.zh: 即便你是商人、厨师或是母亲，你也是在以艺术家的姿态生活。

cues.en: You're embodying it and it's coming from you.
cues.zh: 你正在将这种特质体现出来，而且它源自你自己。

cues.en: And it's, I want to say it's who you are.
cues.zh: 我想说，它就是你的本质。

cues.en: It's not who you are, but it's who you are in that moment.
cues.zh: 它并非你的本质，而是你在那一刻的自我。

cues.en: I'm showing you this beautiful thing as a reflection of how I see the world today.
cues.zh: 我向大家展示这件美好的事物，正是为了体现我如今看待世界的方式。

cues.en: Now, tomorrow, I may see the world differently.
cues.zh: 不过明天，我看待世界的方式可能会发生变化。

cues.en: That's fine.
cues.zh: 那也没关系。

cues.en: But when I share it with you, this is the best it can be in this moment.
cues.zh: 但当我把它分享给你们时，这就是此刻它能呈现的最佳状态。

cues.en: The reason I was asking this question about the, you know, sometimes the world might not like what you give it is because...
cues.zh: 我之所以会提出这个问题，也就是关于有时候世界可能不会喜欢你给出的东西，原因在于……

cues.en: because of this word failure, which you talk about in the book as well, and how to deal with failure.
cues.zh: 就是那个‘失败’这个词，你在书中也提到过它，以及该如何应对失败。

cues.en: I guess a lot of the reason why people won't take the risk to listen to themselves, to what they love, is because of the word risk.
cues.zh: 我想，很多人不敢冒险去倾听自己、去追求自己热爱的东西，很大程度上也是因为‘风险’这个词的缘故。

cues.en: And with that comes, I might lose money, I might lose friends.
cues.zh: 随之而来的担忧就是，我可能会赔钱，也可能会失去朋友。

cues.en: If I quit this job and pursue that violin hobby and go to Peru and violin up in Peru, I'm going to lose friends, people are going to think I'm strange.
cues.zh: 如果我辞掉这份工作去发展小提琴爱好，还去秘鲁继续练琴，我就会失去朋友，别人也会觉得我很奇怪。

cues.en: So I'll conform.
cues.zh: 所以我就选择随波逐流。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: And I'm saying you have to do all of those things, lose the friends, take the risk.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，你必须接受所有这些情况，失去朋友，也要敢于冒险。

cues.en: And I'm also saying, I'm not saying that 100% if you go move to Peru and
cues.zh: 我还要说，我不是说如果你真的搬到秘鲁去当小提琴手，就一定能成功。

cues.en: be the violinist, it's going to work.
cues.zh: 并且你或许在这么做的同时还需要一份正式工作来支付账单。

cues.en: And you may want to have an actual job to pay the bills while you're doing that.
cues.zh: 那也没关系。

cues.en: That's okay.
cues.zh: 认为所有事情都必须是同一件事，这种想法是不对的。

cues.en: The idea that it all has to be one thing.
cues.zh: 我必须做自己梦想的事，而且它还必须是我的职业。

cues.en: I have to do my dream thing and it has to be my profession.
cues.zh: 它还得是我的爱好、我的热爱、我的职业，以及我养活自己的方式。

cues.en: It has to be my hobby, my love, my profession, the way I support myself.
cues.zh: 其实并不一定非得如此。

cues.en: It doesn't have to be.
cues.zh: 当我开始创作音乐时，我原以为自己会有一份正经工作，同时把音乐当作爱好来做。

cues.en: When I started making music, I thought I was going to have a real job and I'd make music and it would be my hobby.
cues.zh: 我会一直做这件事下去。

cues.en: I would do it forever.
cues.zh: 我会永远做这件事。

cues.en: I would do exactly what I was doing, but I thought I would have a real job to support myself to do these things that I want to do.
cues.zh: 幸运的是，事情并没有因为我做什么而改变，它自然而然就发展成了另一回事。

cues.en: Luckily, I was able to, it turned into its own thing by nothing that I did.
cues.zh: 最终它变成了一种独立的职业。

cues.en: Had no expectation that it could be a profession.
cues.zh: 我完全没想过这能成为一种职业。

cues.en: I had no, it couldn't be.
cues.zh: 我根本不认为它能行。

cues.en: It was a ridiculous idea.
cues.zh: 那是个荒谬的想法。

cues.en: I did it because I loved it.
cues.zh: 我做这件事是因为热爱它。

cues.en: And while I was going to school and while I was probably going to go to law school and I would have a regular job, day job, and I would do
cues.zh: 当时我在上学，可能还会去读法学院，同时会有一份常规的工作，而我会

cues.en: music as the love of my life.
cues.zh: 把音乐当作一生的热爱来从事。

cues.en: That's what I would do.
cues.zh: 那就是我原本会做的事。

cues.en: Luckily, I didn't have to do that.
cues.zh: 幸运的是，我不必那样做。

cues.en: But that's what would have happened.
cues.zh: 但本来就会是那样。

cues.en: A lot of people at that age are told to follow their passion, find their purpose, which sounds like this, you know, because the word passion is a singular word.
cues.zh: 很多同龄人都会被告知要追随自己的热情、找到人生目标，听起来就是，你知道的，因为‘热情’是个单数词。

cues.en: And also the word find means I have to go out there and actively pursue the thing.
cues.zh: 而且‘找到’这个词也意味着我必须主动去追求它。

cues.en: A lot of people listening now would say, you know, I've been told to find my passion.
cues.zh: 现在很多正在听的人会说，你知道，我也曾被要求去找到自己的热情。

cues.en: And when they look at their job in the factory or wherever it might be, whatever they're doing, they go, okay, this isn't it yet, but I will get there.
cues.zh: 当他们看着自己在工厂或其它地方的工作，无论正在做什么，他们都会想，好吧，现在还不是时候，但我一定会做到目标的。

cues.en: At some point later.
cues.zh: 在以后的某个时候。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: And I will jump.
cues.zh: 然后我就会行动起来。

cues.en: So you're saying don't jump necessarily.
cues.zh: 所以你是说不一定非得立刻行动？

cues.en: There are realities of life that you have to deal with.
cues.zh: 生活中有一些现实问题是需要去面对的。

cues.en: I'm not saying ignore the fact that you have to pay rent or say, I'm happy living in my parents' house until it
cues.zh: 我不是说可以忽视要交房租的事实，也不是说在事情解决之前就一直住在父母家里就没事。

cues.en: works.
cues.zh: 等一切顺利了再说。

cues.en: That's fine.
cues.zh: 那也没关系。

cues.en: I'm saying there are realities of life that have to be dealt with.
cues.zh: 我的意思是生活中有一些现实问题必须去处理。

cues.en: Don't put the pressure of that on your art because then you won't make the best decisions.
cues.zh: 不要把这种压力施加到你的艺术创作上，否则你就无法做出最正确的决定。

cues.en: You'll make short-term decisions.
cues.zh: 那样你只会做出短视的决定。

cues.en: based on real world issues that you have to deal with in that moment that won't support the long-term benefit
cues.zh: 基于当下必须处理的现实问题，而这些问题并不会带来长远的益处。

cues.en: of the work you're doing, the real work you're doing.
cues.zh: 你正在做的那些工作，真正有价值的工作。

cues.en: I'm sure you've sat there in those moments where you're trying to persuade an artist to follow themselves and what they...
cues.zh: 我敢肯定你肯定有过这样的经历：试图说服一位艺术家坚持自我，遵循他们自己的想法……

cues.en: No?
cues.zh: 没有吗？

cues.en: I don't try to persuade anyone of anything.
cues.zh: 我不会试图说服任何人做任何事。

cues.en: Oh, really?
cues.zh: 哦，真的吗？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不是。

cues.en: I wouldn't use that word.
cues.zh: 我不会用那个词。

cues.en: I wouldn't use the word persuade.
cues.zh: 我不会用‘说服’这个词。

cues.en: What word would you use?
cues.zh: 你会用哪个词呢？

cues.en: We talk about it.
cues.zh: 我们会讨论这个话题。

cues.en: I ask what are your...
cues.zh: 我会问你的……是什么。

cues.en: What do you hope to accomplish?
cues.zh: 你希望达成什么目标？

cues.en: And then I'd support that process.
cues.zh: 然后我会支持这个过程。

cues.en: Can we role play?
cues.zh: 我们可以角色扮演吗？

cues.en: I pretend I'm an artist who wants to write an album.
cues.zh: 我假装自己是一名想要创作专辑的艺术家。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: So I am actually learning to DJ.
cues.zh: 实际上我正在学习当DJ。

cues.en: I've been learning for like four years.
cues.zh: 我已经学了大概四年了。

cues.en: What would you say to me?
cues.zh: 你会对我说什么？

cues.en: So I could come to you and say, Rick, I want to make an album.
cues.zh: 这样我就可以去找你，对你说：里克，我想制作一张专辑。

cues.en: What would the first questions be to me?
cues.zh: 你首先会问我哪些问题？

cues.en: Play me the, of all the things you've made, play me your favorites.
cues.zh: 在你创作的所有作品中，播放一下你最喜欢的吧。

cues.en: Let's talk about it.
cues.zh: 我们来谈谈这件事吧。

cues.en: I would listen to it and then we would talk about it.
cues.zh: 我会先听一遍，然后我们再讨论它。

cues.en: So I play you, let's say it's a house song.
cues.zh: 那我给你放一首歌吧，就当是主题曲吧。

cues.en: I play it.
cues.zh: 我放歌了。

cues.en: I said, this is my favorite.
cues.zh: 我说，这是我最喜欢的。

cues.en: I would tell you whatever I think about it, honestly.
cues.zh: 我会诚实地告诉你我对它的真实看法。

cues.en: Honestly.
cues.zh: 说实话。

cues.en: even if you thought it was terrible.
cues.zh: 哪怕你觉得它很糟糕。

cues.en: Yeah, I probably wouldn't say it in an unpleasant way, but I would probably ask more questions around it.
cues.zh: 嗯，我大概不会用刻薄的方式说，但我会多问一些相关问题。

cues.en: Ask, you know, explain to me what it is that you like about it.
cues.zh: 问问看，比如解释一下你喜欢它的哪些地方。

cues.en: How did you get to that?
cues.zh: 你是怎么想到这个的？

cues.en: What equipment did you use?
cues.zh: 你用了什么设备？

cues.en: Was it fun making it?
cues.zh: 制作它的时候有趣吗？

cues.en: Was it a good experience?
cues.zh: 这是一次不错的体验吗？

cues.en: Have you played it for other people?
cues.zh: 你给其他人玩过这个吗？

cues.en: What's it like?
cues.zh: 那感觉怎么样？

cues.en: What's the experience like?
cues.zh: 整体的体验如何？

cues.en: What's the feeling you get when you're making it?
cues.zh: 在创作的时候你会有什么感受？

cues.en: What's the feeling you get when you play it for a friend?
cues.zh: 给朋友玩的时候你又有什么感受？

cues.en: Have you ever played it in a club?
cues.zh: 你曾在俱乐部里表演过它吗？

cues.en: What's that like?
cues.zh: 那是什么样的体验？

cues.en: I would listen to what you say, and then we would talk about it.
cues.zh: 我会先听你说的，然后我们再一起讨论。

cues.en: Often an artist will come to me.
cues.zh: 通常会有艺术家来找我。

cues.en: They'll tell me exactly what they want to do and then say, I have no idea what I want to do.
cues.zh: 他们会明确告诉我自己想做什么，却又说不知道自己想做什么。

cues.en: Can you help me?
cues.zh: 你能帮我吗？

cues.en: It's like they can't, they can't hear themselves.
cues.zh: 就好像他们做不到，根本听不见自己的声音。

cues.en: There's a, we, we all have this barrier between it's a little bit how therapy works.
cues.zh: 我们所有人之间都存在这样一道障碍，这和心理治疗的方式有点类似。

cues.en: If you go to see a therapist, you might talk.
cues.zh: 如果你去见心理治疗师，你们可能会交谈。

cues.en: They might not say anything, but through the talking, you start understanding.
cues.zh: 他们可能什么都不说，但通过交谈，你就能逐渐理解。

cues.en: What you believe, what you think, what's going on in your life.
cues.zh: 你的信念、你的想法，以及你生活中的种种状况。

cues.en: You might have epiphanies just because someone's listening.
cues.zh: 仅仅因为有人倾听，你就可能会顿悟。

cues.en: Most people are not used to being heard, really heard, deeply heard.
cues.zh: 大多数人并不习惯被真正倾听，被深入地倾听。

cues.en: Often you'll say something to someone and they're thinking about what they're going to say next.
cues.zh: 很多时候你跟别人说话时，他们心里正想着接下来要说什么。

cues.en: They're not really hearing what you're saying.
cues.zh: 他们其实并没有真正听进你在说什么。

cues.en: And I find if you really are there and listen to what someone's saying,
cues.zh: 我发现，如果你真的全神贯注地倾听别人说的话，

cues.en: They tell you what they want to do, and then my job is to just help remove the roadblocks that they're putting in the way of
cues.zh: 他们就会告诉你自己想做什么，而我的职责就是帮助他们消除那些阻碍他们

cues.en: themselves to get there.
cues.zh: 实现目标的障碍。

cues.en: And when they say what they want to do, but then ask you what they should do, is that a lack of sort of self-trust?
cues.zh: 当他们说出了自己想做的事情，却又来问你应该怎么做时，这是不是缺乏自我信任的表现？

cues.en: Yes, but that lack of self-trust is what is the condition of the world.
cues.zh: 没错，而这种自我信任的缺失正是当今世界的现状。

cues.en: That's how we're indoctrinated.
cues.zh: 我们就是在这种环境下被灌输观念的。

cues.en: Most people don't trust themselves.
cues.zh: 大多数人都不信任自己。

cues.en: And it's a fine line because there are the few people who might seem to really trust themselves and you think, oh, they're egomaniacs.
cues.zh: 这其实很微妙，因为总有一些人看似真的非常自信，但你可能会觉得他们是自大狂。

cues.en: Usually when someone really comes off as wildly egotistical, it's usually hiding some.
cues.zh: 通常那些表现得极度自负的人，往往是在掩饰某些东西。

cues.en: Insecurities, really, it's like a mask.
cues.zh: 其实是内心的不安，就像一层面具罢了。

cues.en: So that's dealing with someone who's insecure and dealing with someone who's overconfident.
cues.zh: 所以这就涉及到如何应对内心不安的人，以及如何应对过度自信的人。

cues.en: It's often two sides of the same coin.
cues.zh: 这往往是同一枚硬币的两面。

cues.en: And we're really looking for this middle place of reality.
cues.zh: 我们真正要寻找的，就是这种现实的中间状态。

cues.en: It's like not what you're afraid of about yourself or what other people are going to think, but where
cues.zh: 关键不在于你害怕自己如何，或者别人会怎么想，而在于

cues.en: are you really on this?
cues.zh: 你真正处于什么位置。

cues.en: I often describe it as tasting food.
cues.zh: 我常常把它形容成品尝食物的过程。

cues.en: Like if I gave you two pieces of pizza and say, taste the two pieces of pizza, tell me which one you like better.
cues.zh: 比如我给你两块披萨，让你尝一尝，然后告诉我哪一块你更喜欢。

cues.en: It's not a hard question.
cues.zh: 这并不是个难的问题。

cues.en: You'll probably say, I like this one much better than this.
cues.zh: 你很可能会说，我明显更喜欢这一块。

cues.en: And when I ask you which tastes better, you wouldn't say, well, I think this guy's going to like this pizza better.
cues.zh: 而当我问你哪一块味道更好时，你不会说‘我觉得这个人会更喜欢这块披萨’。

cues.en: You would say, this one tastes better to me.
cues.zh: 你会说，这一块对我来说味道更好。

cues.en: That's the goal is getting to that.
cues.zh: 我们的目标就是达到这种状态。

cues.en: This one tastes better to me.
cues.zh: 这一块对我来说味道更好。

cues.en: Simple.
cues.zh: 很简单。

cues.en: We don't believe.
cues.zh: 我们并不认为，

cues.en: That it can be as simple as it is.
cues.zh: 事情能简单到这种程度。

cues.en: And it is simple.
cues.zh: 但实际上它真的很简单。

cues.en: If you were to bet on an artist being one of these great artists that you've worked with because they have a set of characteristics
cues.zh: 如果你要赌某个艺术家能成为你曾共事过的那些伟大艺术家之一，那是因为他们具备某些特定的特质，

cues.en: or a perspective or a humility that is conducive with what you've seen results in exceptional work.
cues.zh: 或是某种视角、某种谦逊的态度，而这些恰恰能带来出色的作品。

cues.en: What are those like similar attributes?
cues.zh: 那些类似的特质究竟是什么？

cues.en: As someone that does a lot of investing in entrepreneurs, I was wondering if there were similarities even there.
cues.zh: 作为经常投资创业者的人，我在想即便在创业领域是否也存在类似的共性。

cues.en: I'm sure there are.
cues.zh: 我肯定存在。

cues.en: Because some of it sounded the same.
cues.zh: 因为有些地方听起来很相似。

cues.en: I'm sure there are.
cues.zh: 我肯定存在。

cues.en: Um, I asked a friend of mine who is a venture capital guy about when he's picking things
cues.zh: 嗯，我曾问过一位从事风险投资的友人，在他挑选投资对象时，

cues.en: to invest in, is it the premise of the business or is it the founder?
cues.zh: 是看项目的本身，还是看创始人？

cues.en: And he said, it's always the founder.
cues.zh: 他说，永远是看创始人。

cues.en: It doesn't matter what the business is.
cues.zh: 项目本身如何并不重要。

cues.en: He said, if I believe in the person, I'll back them.
cues.zh: 他说，只要我相信这个人，我就会支持他。

cues.en: And I suppose it's, it would be the same with artists.
cues.zh: 我想对于艺术家来说也是同样的道理。

cues.en: It's like, it's.
cues.zh: 就是……

cues.en: It's the artists, not like, well, they wrote a great song.
cues.zh: 关键在于艺术家本人，而不是说他们写了一首很棒的歌。

cues.en: The great song is more like the great product.
cues.zh: 一首出色的歌更像是出色的产品。

cues.en: It's like, maybe they could do that again.
cues.zh: 也许他们还能再做到那样。

cues.en: But if you see that the way that they see music, the way that they innovate in the things that they make, that's
cues.zh: 但如果你看到他们看待音乐的方式，以及他们在创作中创新的方式，那可是

cues.en: a good sign.
cues.zh: 一个好迹象。

cues.en: Tell you a story.
cues.zh: 让我给你们讲个故事。

cues.en: Band The Strokes.
cues.zh: The Strokes乐队。

cues.en: I produced their new album, just came out maybe a month ago.
cues.zh: 我为他们的新专辑担任制作人，那张专辑大概一个月前刚发行。

cues.en: And they had asked me to produce an album for them, maybe.
cues.zh: 他们曾请求我为他们制作一张专辑，大概是在……

cues.en: I want to say 15 years ago.
cues.zh: 我想说的是15年前。

cues.en: And I listened to the demos and I didn't hear it.
cues.zh: 我听了那些演示版本，但没听出那种感觉。

cues.en: I didn't, I didn't, I'm not saying it couldn't be good.
cues.zh: 我没有，我不是说它不可能很好。

cues.en: I just didn't see the way in for me.
cues.zh: 我只是看不出自己该从哪入手。

cues.en: It's like, I don't think I should do this.
cues.zh: 就是，我觉得自己不该做这件事。

cues.en: I don't, I don't feel it.

cues.en: It's almost a bit of a trade I made.
cues.zh: 这几乎算是一种我主动做出的选择。

cues.en: I accepted it, which meant that at cocktail parties, people were impressed by me.
cues.zh: 我接受了它，这样一来在鸡尾酒会上，人们就会对我刮目相看。

cues.en: And so, you know, we traded something for something else and now we're boxed in.
cues.zh: 所以，你知道，我们用一样东西换来了另一样东西，结果现在反而被困住了。

cues.en: And now a lot, you know, I hear a lot from our listeners on this show, like they feel stuck.
cues.zh: 现在，我经常听到本节目的听众说，他们感觉自己陷入了困境。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: We're free.
cues.zh: 我们是自由的。

cues.en: We're free.
cues.zh: 我们是自由的。

cues.en: We just have to choose to take advantage of this human gift of freedom and We can start
cues.zh: 我们只需要选择好好利用这份人类与生俱来的自由，然后就可以开始了。

cues.en: over.
cues.zh: 结束。

cues.en: I remember the one close friend who tried to commit suicide and luckily lived.
cues.zh: 我记得有个密友曾试图自杀，所幸活了下来。

cues.en: I went to visit him in the hospital.
cues.zh: 我去医院看望了他。

cues.en: He was laying in a hospital bed and he was seemingly catatonic.
cues.zh: 他躺在病床上，看起来处于木僵状态。

cues.en: He hadn't spoke since this happened.
cues.zh: 自从那件事发生后，他就再没说过话。

cues.en: And I was standing in the hallway and there were a series of his friends coming to see him.
cues.zh: 我站在走廊里，看到他的一群朋友陆续前来探望。

cues.en: Everybody would go into the room one at a time.
cues.zh: 每个人都轮流进到房间里去。

cues.en: And I listened to the two people who went in before me and they were crying and they were acting as if
cues.zh: 我听到了在我之前进去的两人的对话，他们一直在哭，表现得好像

cues.en: he had died.
cues.zh: 他已经死了似的。

cues.en: Now he's laying there, he's in fetal position.
cues.zh: 此刻他正蜷缩在那里，呈胎儿姿势。

cues.en: He's not saying a word.
cues.zh: 他一句话也不说。

cues.en: And I'm just thinking this, this is really weird.
cues.zh: 我就想着，这真的太奇怪了。

cues.en: This is, it's really, the whole scene is weird.
cues.zh: 整个场面真的非常奇怪。

cues.en: Never seen anything like it before.
cues.zh: 我以前从未见过这样的情形。

cues.en: And my first thought was the people who are going in there and talking to him, they have no idea how to act.
cues.zh: 我首先想到的是，那些进去和他交谈的人根本不知道该怎么做。

cues.en: None of us do because this is an unusual situation.
cues.zh: 我们所有人都不清楚，因为这确实是个不寻常的情况。

cues.en: Unless you've been in it, which I hadn't been before, you'd have no idea what to do.
cues.zh: 除非你有过类似经历，而我之前没有，否则根本不知道该采取什么行动。

cues.en: But I knew from listening, this is not the best.
cues.zh: 但通过倾听我就知道，现在这样处理并不好。

cues.en: What they're doing is not the best situation.
cues.zh: 他们目前的做法并不是最佳选择。

cues.en: There's a better way.
cues.zh: 还有更好的办法。

cues.en: And I was the next one in and I went in and I looked down and I said, again, I don't know where this
cues.zh: 接下来轮到我进去，我走进去后低头说道，我不知道这话是从哪儿冒出来的，但它就是出现了。

cues.en: came from, but it came.
cues.zh: 我说，你现在可能很难看出来，但你正处于最佳状态。

cues.en: I said, this may be hard for you to see right now, but you're in the sweet spot.
cues.zh: 我记得自己说了这话，而他看着我的眼神，就好像我疯了一样。

cues.en: And I remember saying that and he looked at me and he looked at me like I was insane.
cues.zh: 我也记得他那样看着我。

cues.en: But it was the first time anyone, the first thing he reacted to was that.
cues.zh: 不过那是第一次有人出现这种情况，他第一反应就是那样。

cues.en: And I said, you just hit the reset button.
cues.zh: 我说，你只要按下重置按钮就行了。

cues.en: I said, all of the things that you hate to do, that you feel obligated to do, that you feel committed to do,
cues.zh: 我说，那些你讨厌做、觉得有义务做、觉得必须去做的事情，

cues.en: that made you want to not be here anymore.
cues.zh: 正是这些让你不想再待在这里。

cues.en: You just hit the reset button.
cues.zh: 你只要按下重置按钮就行了。

cues.en: You never have to do any of those things again.
cues.zh: 你再也不必做那些事了。

cues.en: And now you can do anything you want.
cues.zh: 现在你可以做任何你想做的事。

cues.en: You're free to start.
cues.zh: 你可以自由地开始了。

cues.en: All of those old ideas, none of those obligations are hanging over your head.
cues.zh: 那些旧观念、那些束缚都不再压在你的头上。

cues.en: And we ended up having a really nice conversation and he got up and he got dressed and he was like himself.
cues.zh: 最后我们进行了一次非常愉快的交谈，他起身穿好衣服，又变回了原来的自己。

cues.en: It was an amazing experience.
cues.zh: 那是一次令人惊叹的经历。

cues.en: But that's how boxed in we feel.
cues.zh: 但我们就是有这种被束缚的感觉。

cues.en: But it's all just a story.
cues.zh: 但那不过是个故事罢了。

cues.en: It's not true.
cues.zh: 那不是真的。

cues.en: We are free.
cues.zh: 我们是自由的。

cues.en: Is there a step one in that direction for people that want to hit the reset button?
cues.zh: 对于那些想要重置人生的人来说，有没有第一步可走？

cues.en: Is there a first step?
cues.zh: 有第一步吗？

cues.en: Well, I would try to see what are the things in your life that really you want to change and then think about what's the cleanest
cues.zh: 我会试着找出你生活中真正想要改变的事情，然后再思考改变它们的最简洁方式。

cues.en: way to change them.
cues.zh: 离开一份工作，结束一段关系。

cues.en: Leaving a job, leaving a relationship.
cues.zh: 你知道，这些事情会发生，是因为我们怀着良好的意愿做出承诺。

cues.en: You know, the reason these things happen is we make commitments with good intentions.
cues.zh: 而当难以履行承诺时，人就会开始感到被困住了。

cues.en: And then when it's hard to keep the commitment is where it starts feeling boxed in.
cues.zh: 不过，我认为做出承诺并遵守承诺都是好事。

cues.en: Now, I think commitments are a good thing both to make and to keep.
cues.zh: 话虽如此，有时它也会变得关乎生死。

cues.en: That said, there can be a point where it becomes life and death.
cues.zh: 也就是说，有时候它确实会变得至关重要。

cues.en: It's like this commitment that I made was a mistake or something changed.
cues.zh: 我感觉自己当初做出的那个承诺是个错误，或者有些事情发生了变化。

cues.en: Maybe the person that I married became an alcoholic.
cues.zh: 也许我娶的那个人变成了酒鬼。

cues.en: And it's really hard living with an alcoholic.
cues.zh: 和酒鬼一起生活真的非常艰难。

cues.en: And it's not fun.
cues.zh: 而且一点乐趣都没有。

cues.en: This is not what we signed up for.
cues.zh: 这根本不是我们当初期望的生活。

cues.en: And I can do everything I can to help this person, but maybe nothing works.
cues.zh: 我会尽自己所能去帮助这个人，但也许什么办法都不起作用。

cues.en: And at some point, it's okay to hit the reset button and say, you know what?
cues.zh: 在某个时候，按下重置按钮，说‘你知道吗？’也是可以的。

cues.en: you're not doing any favors.
cues.zh: 你这样做根本帮不上对方的忙。

cues.en: If you're locked in a situation, I have a lot of friends who are in relationships and maybe the relationship has gone south,
cues.zh: 如果陷入某种状况，我有很多朋友正处于感情关系中，而这段关系可能已经变糟了，

cues.en: but they stay in it because both sides of the couple feel like this is the life we signed up for.
cues.zh: 但他们仍然选择维持，因为双方都觉得这就是自己当初承诺要过的生活。

cues.en: And in reality, you're not doing any favors for the person being unhappy in a relationship.
cues.zh: 但实际上，你对在感情中不开心的人并没有起到任何帮助作用。

cues.en: It's the nature of love is it's a two-way street.
cues.zh: 爱情的本质就是双向的。

cues.en: Or the same I can say if someone is in love with someone and the other person, unrequited love, the person's not in love
cues.zh: 或者用同样的话来说，如果有人爱上了另一个人，而对方没有同样的感情，也就是单恋的情况，那这个人其实并没有真正恋爱。

cues.en: with them.
cues.zh: 和他们在一起。

cues.en: There's no really such thing because the nature of love is, it's like a negative and a positive magnet
cues.zh: 其实根本不存在这种事，因为恋爱的本质就像正负磁铁一样，

cues.en: pulling towards each other.
cues.zh: 会互相吸引。

cues.en: You can't have one side of the magnet in love.
cues.zh: 磁铁不可能只有一面处于恋爱状态，

cues.en: It doesn't work.
cues.zh: 那是行不通的。

cues.en: And it's just a fantasy of what, you know, it's, it's a beautiful fantasy of what you think, like as an optimist, it could be so beautiful, but
cues.zh: 那只不过是你作为乐观主义者所想象的一种美好幻想罢了，虽然听起来很美好，但

cues.en: if it's not there, it's best for everyone involved.
cues.zh: 如果那种感情不存在，对所有相关的人来说都是最好的。

cues.en: Sometimes I have some friends who feel like, well, I don't want to break up with them because it'll, it'll, um, it'll destroy them.
cues.zh: 有时候我会遇到一些朋友，他们觉得不想和对方分手，因为那样会毁了对方。

cues.en: It's not true.
cues.zh: 那不是真的。

cues.en: It's better for everyone involved.
cues.zh: 对所有相关的人而言，分开反而是更好的选择。

cues.en: If it's not working to find the new, beautiful life.
cues.zh: 如果这段关系无法继续，那就去寻找新的、美好的生活吧。

cues.en: You can do that.
cues.zh: 你可以做到这一点。

cues.en: It's okay.
cues.zh: 没关系的。

cues.en: I imagine as well there's some people who have lots of small misalignments.
cues.zh: 我想也有一些人存在很多细微的偏差。

cues.en: None of them are huge issues on their own, but now they have a life full of a hundred small misaligned things.
cues.zh: 这些偏差单独来看都不是什么大问题，但累积起来就会让他们的生活中充满无数细微的偏差。

cues.en: Could be anything.
cues.zh: 原因可能是任何事情。

cues.en: And so their life feels really fundamentally misaligned, but it's actually just maybe they struggled with honesty across many little areas of their life.
cues.zh: 因此他们的整个人生会给人一种彻底失衡的感觉，但实际上可能只是他们在生活的诸多小方面缺乏坦诚。

cues.en: And maybe those can be worked on, and maybe it can be fixed, but in either case, don't let it just linger.
cues.zh: 这些问题或许可以解决，也许能够得到改善，但无论如何都不要让它们一直存在。

cues.en: You know, repair them.
cues.zh: 你知道的，把它们修复掉吧。

cues.en: It's hard conversations though, Rick.
cues.zh: 不过这确实是些艰难的对话，里克。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: A lot of people aren't good at that, you know, people pleases.
cues.zh: 很多人不擅长做这件事，也就是那些喜欢讨好别人的人。

cues.en: And there's a through line here with creativity generally, I think, this idea of like people pleasing the difficult conversation.
cues.zh: 我认为这与创造力本身也有共通之处，也就是那种在艰难对话中喜欢讨好别人的心态。

cues.en: And I've obviously seen from some of the things you've mentioned through this conversation that you'd be willing to tell people like, this isn't for me.
cues.zh: 从我们这次谈话中你提到的一些内容来看，显然你愿意告诉别人，这东西并不适合我。

cues.en: I imagine you're offered a lot of money a lot of the time as well.
cues.zh: 我想很多时候你也会收到很多钱的报价吧。

cues.en: How do you sort of pass through that if you're offered a ton of money to do something, but at some level it's not aligned with your principles or values?
cues.zh: 如果有人出大价钱让你做某件事，而这件事在某种程度上与你的原则或价值观相悖，你要如何应对呢？

cues.en: I want to make good things.
cues.zh: 我想创造出优秀的作品。

cues.en: Like I want to make something good.
cues.zh: 我就想做出点好东西来。

cues.en: Have you turned down large numbers in terms of money or other incentives because you didn't feel something was going to
cues.zh: 你是否因为觉得事情不会有进展，而拒绝过大量金钱或其他激励措施？

cues.en: be good or was aligned?
cues.zh: 要优秀，还是要保持一致？

cues.en: Yeah, I'm sure I have.
cues.zh: 是的，我确定我有。

cues.en: I can't think of examples, but I'm sure I have.
cues.zh: 我想不起来具体的例子了，但我确定我曾经有过。

cues.en: I don't think about the stuff.
cues.zh: 我不会去思考那些事情。

cues.en: I think about the things I do.
cues.zh: 我会思考自己所做的事情。

cues.en: I don't think about things I don't do, you know?
cues.zh: 我一般不会去想那些自己不会做的事情，你懂的吧？

cues.en: Does it matter to you, the money part of it?
cues.zh: 钱这方面对你来说重要吗？

cues.en: I want to be in success.
cues.zh: 我渴望获得成功。

cues.en: I want to participate in the success.
cues.zh: 我想参与到这份成功之中。

cues.en: I think that's right.
cues.zh: 我觉得那样没错。

cues.en: That feels right to me.
cues.zh: 我觉着那样很对。

cues.en: I never make a decision for a financial reason.
cues.zh: 我从来不会因为财务原因做决定。

cues.en: That said, if we make something successful, that's valuable.
cues.zh: 话虽如此，如果我们把某件事做成功了，那是很宝贵的。

cues.en: And in your own life, and we're talking there about mental health, through your early 30s, you had a depressive episode yourself.
cues.zh: 至于你自己的生活，我们这里谈到的是心理健康问题，在你三十出头的时候，你自己也经历过抑郁发作。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Was there a causal factor?
cues.zh: 有导致它的因素吗？

cues.en: And how important was that in shaping how you think generally about the world and the art and the creativity?
cues.zh: 那在塑造你整体看待世界、艺术以及创造力的方式上，它有多重要？

cues.en: Because I know I've heard you say on Newsday that it changed you permanently.
cues.zh: 因为我记得我在《新闻日报》上听你说过，那件事永久地改变了你。

cues.en: It did.
cues.zh: 确实如此。

cues.en: Take me into that part of your life.
cues.zh: 带我走进你生命中的那段时光吧。

cues.en: You're 33 years old, my age.
cues.zh: 你33岁，和我年纪一样。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: What happened?
cues.zh: 发生了什么事？

cues.en: What happened was I had been an only child.
cues.zh: 事情是这样的，我一直是独生子女。

cues.en: My parents really loved me, really cared about me, always supportive.
cues.zh: 我的父母非常爱我，十分关心我，一直给予支持。

cues.en: I went to school.
cues.zh: 我去上学了。

cues.en: I started making music as a hobby.
cues.zh: 我开始把做音乐当作爱好。

cues.en: It ended up taking on a life of its own and becoming a business and had great success for all those years.
cues.zh: 后来它逐渐有了自己的发展，变成了一项事业，并且这些年来一直都非常成功。

cues.en: And then at 33, for the first time, it got called into question.
cues.zh: 到了33岁的时候，它第一次遭到了质疑。

cues.en: I had a business relationship with a big company.
cues.zh: 我和一家大公司有业务往来。

cues.en: The person who I was in relationship with was one of the, probably the top person in the whole music industry, well-loved,
cues.zh: 与我有过合作的人，大概是整个音乐行业中最重要的人物之一，深受大家喜爱，

cues.en: beautiful person, one of my mentors.
cues.zh: 是个非常出色的人，也是我的导师之一。

cues.en: He got politically forced out and a new person was put in who I didn't have a relationship with.
cues.zh: 他因为政治原因被逼离开，接着来了一个我和他没有合作关系的新人。

cues.en: And that person called me and said, I read your, I read our agreement because he had adopted the agreement that I had with my mentor.
cues.zh: 那个人给我打电话说，我看了你的协议，其实他用的就是我当初和导师签订的那个协议。

cues.en: He's like, I don't like it.
cues.zh: 他说，我不喜欢这个协议。

cues.en: When you come back to California, we should talk about it.
cues.zh: 等你回到加利福尼亚后，我们得好好谈一谈。

cues.en: That was it.
cues.zh: 就这些内容。

cues.en: That was the whole conversation.
cues.zh: 整个对话就只有这些。

cues.en: Now for me, I didn't, I didn't know because I had so much success for so long.
cues.zh: 对我来说，我之前并不知道，因为这么长时间我一直都很成功。

cues.en: I never, I never had to deal with any instability in my life in that way.
cues.zh: 我从来没遇到过生活里这种不稳定的状况。

cues.en: I felt like the rug had been pulled out from under me.
cues.zh: 我感觉自己仿佛被突然抽走了立足之地。

cues.en: And I had started having panic attacks and couldn't sleep and got really sick.
cues.zh: 后来我开始出现恐慌发作，无法入睡，身体也变得很糟糕。

cues.en: And again, for almost anyone else, the exact same scenario would have been, okay, we'll deal with it when I get there.
cues.zh: 对几乎所有其他人来说，同样的情况出现时，他们大概只会说，等到了那儿再处理吧。

cues.en: No problem.
cues.zh: 没问题。

cues.en: And move on.
cues.zh: 然后继续前进就行。

cues.en: But I didn't have the ability to deal with it because I never had to deal with anything like that.
cues.zh: 但我没有能力去处理它，因为我从来没遇到过类似的情况。

cues.en: I didn't have the musculature to deal with that issue.
cues.zh: 我没有足够的精力去应对那个问题。

cues.en: And it felt like the rug was pulled out.
cues.zh: 感觉就像脚下的地板被突然抽走了。

cues.en: I didn't know what to do and sunk.
cues.zh: 我不知道该做什么，只能陷入绝望。

cues.en: And then it ended up going on for years, even after the problem was solved.
cues.zh: 之后这种情况持续了好几年，甚至在那个问题解决之后依然如此。

cues.en: I ended up leaving the company, starting a relationship with a new company.
cues.zh: 最终我离开了那家公司，开始在另一家公司工作。

cues.en: Everything was fine.
cues.zh: 一切都很正常。

cues.en: But some, it's like, it was like a, it was like I was a balloon that got burst in that moment.
cues.zh: 但对某些人而言，那简直就像我当时突然被戳破的气球一样。

cues.en: And I'm still not the same person as I was before.
cues.zh: 现在的我已不再是原来的那个人了。

cues.en: Now, maybe now I'm more rooted in reality, which probably sounds funny after a lot of the things I've been saying.
cues.zh: 现在，也许我比以前更脚踏实地了，考虑到我之前说过那么多话，这听起来可能有点好笑。

cues.en: Before that, I would say I never questioned anything.
cues.zh: 在那之前，我可以说自己从未质疑过任何事情。

cues.en: It was just like everything was always rolling in this one direction.
cues.zh: 一切似乎总是朝着同一个方向发展。

cues.en: And that was the first time that it was questioned.
cues.zh: 而那也是第一次有人对这种状况提出质疑。
