cues.en: And I remember after all this debate, I went and read your opinion on alcohol.
cues.zh: 记得经过一番思考后，我去读了您关于酒精的观点。

cues.en: And it actually allowed me, it gave myself permission to drink, which I know sounds exactly the opposite of what you're saying.
cues.zh: 那实际上让我获得了喝酒的许可，虽然这听起来和您说的完全相反。

cues.en: But you had said it was really only a sin or bad if you do it in excess.
cues.zh: 但您说过，只有过量饮酒才是罪过或坏事。

cues.en: So I finally allowed myself to drink.
cues.zh: 所以最终我允许自己喝酒了。

cues.en: Yeah, I didn't like to do it except in excess.
cues.zh: 是的，除非过量，否则我并不想喝酒。

cues.en: Yeah, well, I soon later found out that that is pretty nice on occasion.
cues.zh: 嗯，后来我才发现，偶尔喝一点其实还挺不错的。

cues.en: not a recommendation, but I found your opinion on that.
cues.zh: 这不算推荐，只是我想听听你对此的看法。

cues.en: And this was after about a year and a half of, honestly, I was suffering a lot.
cues.zh: 这是在大约一年半之后的事了，说实话，那段时间我过得非常痛苦。

cues.en: So I was in my head.
cues.zh: 当时我满脑子都是负面想法。

cues.en: I was anxious.
cues.zh: 我感到十分焦虑。

cues.en: I couldn't be myself.
cues.zh: 我无法做回真实的自己。

cues.en: I felt like I was disassociating in environments, but actually I took, I drank alcohol and it brought me into the present for the first time in a very long time.
cues.zh: 我觉得自己在各种场合都会产生疏离感，但实际上我喝了酒，这让我在很长一段时间后第一次回到了当下。

cues.en: And I think oddly enough, that was.
cues.zh: 说来奇怪，那件事居然是这样。

cues.en: a part of healing, which sounds completely counterproductive and not intuitive at all, but it helped me oddly enough.
cues.zh: 它成了康复过程的一部分，虽然听起来完全适得其反且不合常理，但奇怪的是它确实帮到了我。

cues.en: It's like training wheels.
cues.zh: 就像辅助轮一样。

cues.en: To experience, you know, like a social environment physically, like you're actually there to experience happiness for the first time in
cues.zh: 让我能够真正身处社交场合，亲身体验快乐，就像很久以来第一次那样。

cues.en: a very long time.
cues.zh: 在很长一段时间之后。

cues.en: I did it with a close friend of mine, but I don't know what that, if that means anything, if there's any significance to that or, you know, I don't want to be recommending alcohol.
cues.zh: 我是和一位很要好的朋友一起做的，但我不确定那意味着什么，也不知道那是否有任何意义，或者，你知道的，我并不想推荐饮酒。

cues.en: The significance fundamentally is that things are complicated.
cues.zh: 其根本意义在于事情本来就很复杂。

cues.en: Like lots of teenagers now don't drink at all.
cues.zh: 比如现在很多青少年根本不喝酒。

cues.en: So you might say, well, that's a good thing because alcohol, all things considered, is problematic.
cues.zh: 所以你可能会说，那当然是好事，因为总体而言酒精确实存在问题。

cues.en: But if you're not partying because you have no friends and you're in your basement, miserable and depressed, that's
cues.zh: 但如果你因为没有朋友而独自待在地下室，感到痛苦和沮丧，那其实

cues.en: not an improvement.
cues.zh: 并不是什么进步。

cues.en: And so I suppose to some degree, whether or not something is good depends on your starting point.
cues.zh: 所以我想在某种程度上，某件事是否好取决于你的出发点。

cues.en: You know, like I can understand, for example, why so many young men admire Andrew Tate.
cues.zh: 你知道，比如我能理解为什么有这么多年轻男性崇拜安德鲁·泰特。

cues.en: At least Andrew Tate has all the positive aspects of a successful narcissist.
cues.zh: 至少安德鲁·泰特具备一个成功的自恋者所具备的所有积极特质。

cues.en: It beats the hell out of being depressed and anxious.
cues.zh: 这总比陷入抑郁和焦虑要好得多。

cues.en: Now, is that a stellar goal?
cues.zh: 那么，这算是个出色的目标吗？

cues.en: No, but it's an improvement over isolated misery.
cues.zh: 不算，但总比孤立无援的痛苦要好一些。

cues.en: You know, you see this in female mate choices.
cues.zh: 你知道，这在女性择偶行为中也很常见。

cues.en: There's a strong proclivity in women to...
cues.zh: 女性有一种很强的倾向……

cues.en: be enamored of bad boys.
cues.zh: 喜欢那些坏男孩。

cues.en: And there's a variety of reasons for that.
cues.zh: 造成这种现象的原因有很多。

cues.en: But one reason is, well, they're a hell of a lot more interesting than martyred, miserable, depressed, anxious, self-conscious, low
cues.zh: 但其中一个原因就是，他们比那些饱受折磨、痛苦不堪、抑郁、焦虑、缺乏自信、自尊心低下的

cues.en: self-esteem, non-starters.
cues.zh: 毫无吸引力的人有趣得多。

cues.en: So now, is that an optimal choice?
cues.zh: 那么，这算是最佳选择吗？

cues.en: No.
cues.zh: 不是。

cues.en: But comparatively, that's the attraction of the shadow figure fundamentally.
cues.zh: 但从根本上说，这正是那种阴暗形象的吸引力所在。

cues.en: What did Nietzsche say about morality?
cues.zh: 尼采对道德有什么看法？

cues.en: Most morality is cowardice.
cues.zh: 大多数道德行为都是懦弱的表现。

cues.en: What did he mean by that?
cues.zh: 他这么说是什么意思？

cues.en: Well, he didn't mean that morality was cowardice.
cues.zh: 嗯，他并不是说道德就是懦弱。

cues.en: He said most morality is cowardice.
cues.zh: 他是说大多数道德行为其实都是懦弱的表现。

cues.en: And what he meant by that was people find themselves too timid to do anything.
cues.zh: 他的意思是人们往往胆小到不敢采取任何行动。

cues.en: And so instead of admitting their lack of courage to themselves, they put a moral gloss on it and say that the reason they're timorous is because they're good.
cues.zh: 所以他们不承认自己缺乏勇气，反而给这种行为披上道德的外衣，声称自己胆小是因为品德高尚。

cues.en: That's a form of moral hypocrisy.
cues.zh: 这就是一种道德虚伪的表现。

cues.en: You know, there were kids in my high school, for example, who never drank.
cues.zh: 比如我高中时就有些学生从来不喝酒。

cues.en: You know, they were good kids, but they weren't good.
cues.zh: 他们看起来是好孩子，但实际上并非如此。

cues.en: They're just cowards.
cues.zh: 他们只是懦夫罢了。

cues.en: That wasn't helpful.
cues.zh: 那样做并没有什么帮助。

cues.en: Now, my friends, my delinquent friends in junior high and high school, a lot of them became alcoholics.
cues.zh: 而我那些初中和高中时爱犯错的朋友，很多人后来都成了酒鬼。

cues.en: So their lack of cowardice on the exploration front also caused them a tremendous amount of misery.
cues.zh: 所以他们在探索新事物时缺乏懦弱，反而给自己带来了极大的痛苦。

cues.en: Look, there's actually a literature on this.
cues.zh: 其实关于这个话题已经有不少相关研究文献了。

cues.en: So imagine you took adolescents on a distribution of rule breaking.
cues.zh: 那么试想，如果你让青少年去体验不同程度的违规行为会怎样。

cues.en: Okay.
cues.zh: 好的。

cues.en: There's kids who never break any rules on one end, and there's kids who break them all the time on the other end.
cues.zh: 一类孩子从不会违反任何规则，而另一类孩子则总是违反规则。

cues.en: And then there's the kids in the middle who experiment with rule-breaking in adolescents.
cues.zh: 再就是处于中间的那些青少年，他们会尝试各种违规行为。

cues.en: Well, the ones who never break rules are at much higher risk for depression, anxiety, and dependent personality disorder later in life.
cues.zh: 那些从不违反规则的孩子，日后患抑郁症、焦虑症以及依赖型人格障碍的风险要高得多。

cues.en: They're too inhibited.
cues.zh: 他们太过拘谨了。

cues.en: And the ones who break rules all the time, well, they end up in prison.
cues.zh: 而那些总是违反规则的孩子，最终往往会进监狱。

cues.en: So you want to have that.
cues.zh: 所以你希望孩子处于哪种状态呢？

cues.en: I'm not saying that you should be in the middle exactly.
cues.zh: 我并不是说孩子必须恰好处于中间状态。

cues.en: I'm saying that there's an optimal mode of being that allows you to explore, even in ways that could potentially be
cues.zh: 我的意思是，存在一种最佳的状态，能让孩子们在探索的过程中，即便采用可能

cues.en: destructive.
cues.zh: 具有破坏性的方式，

cues.en: And that that's the best pathway to facilitate development.
cues.zh: 这也是促进其成长的最佳途径。

cues.en: It's like 12 rules.
cues.zh: 它就像12条规则一样。

cues.en: It's the order in chaos.
cues.zh: 它是混乱中的秩序。

cues.en: It's walking the line between what's familiar and known versus exploring something else.
cues.zh: 它是在熟悉已知的事物与探索其他事物之间寻找平衡。

cues.en: Yeah, because you don't want to make the error of presuming that a totalitarian order is equivalent to morality.
cues.zh: 没错，因为你不能犯错，以为极权秩序就等同于道德。

cues.en: It's funny, what you said was actually exactly the conclusion that I had came to, which was I was assigning a false sense of morality to myself because I was sober.
cues.zh: 有趣的是，你说的其实正是我得出的结论，那就是因为我保持清醒，就给自己赋予了错误的道德感。

cues.en: even though I actually, it just made me feel good about myself because I thought that I was holier than thou because I wasn't drinking.
cues.zh: 尽管实际上，这只会让我自我感觉良好，因为我觉得自己比别人更圣洁，毕竟我没有喝酒。

cues.en: And I was denying myself that because other people would say that, like people that cared about me, but I wouldn't actually accept it.
cues.zh: 而我却否认这一点，因为那些关心我的人会这么说，但我自己并不愿意接受。

cues.en: And it was out of cowardice.
cues.zh: 那是出于胆怯。

cues.en: It's interesting how alcohol affects everybody differently because for me, it puts me to sleep.
cues.zh: 酒精对每个人的影响都不一样，这很有趣，因为对我来说，它会让我入睡。

cues.en: I'll have two drinks and instantly I'm just like, all right, I'm tired.
cues.zh: 我喝两杯之后，马上就会觉得累了。

cues.en: This isn't fun.
cues.zh: 这样并不好玩。

cues.en: I'm not enjoying myself.
cues.zh: 我并没有享受其中。

cues.en: For some people, it's an accelerant.
cues.zh: 对某些人来说，它能起到加速作用。

cues.en: No, it's, yeah.
cues.zh: 不，就是那样。

cues.en: We tested people in the lab in Montreal.
cues.zh: 我们在蒙特利尔的实验室里对受试者进行了测试。

cues.en: You give them three drinks in 20 minutes, so a pretty decent dose.
cues.zh: 我们在20分钟内让他们喝三杯，剂量相当可观。

cues.en: Their heart rate would go up 40 beats per minute.
cues.zh: 他们的心率会每分钟上升40次。

cues.en: It was just like a shot of cocaine.
cues.zh: 效果简直就像注射了可卡因一样。

cues.en: And those were often people who had a history of familial alcoholism.
cues.zh: 而且这些受试者往往有家族性酗酒史。

cues.en: So they had a genetic predisposition to be alcoholic, but they were getting a psychomotor stimulant kick.
cues.zh: 也就是说他们有成为酗酒者的遗传倾向，同时又因这种精神运动兴奋剂而兴奋。

cues.en: And it looks like that was opiate mediated.
cues.zh: 看起来这是由阿片类物质介导的。

cues.en: So for some people, when they drink, they produce a lot of beta endorphin, which is an opiate.
cues.zh: 所以对某些人而言，饮酒后会分泌大量β内啡肽，而β内啡肽属于阿片类物质。

cues.en: It's in the opiate family.
cues.zh: 它属于阿片类家族。

cues.en: And so there's...
cues.zh: 因此存在……

cues.en: endless benefit to that.
cues.zh: 这能带来无尽的好处。

cues.en: I had a friend in Montreal, an old guy, Frank Irvin.
cues.zh: 我在蒙特利尔有个朋友，是个老头，叫弗兰克·欧文。

cues.en: He was a cool old guy.
cues.zh: 他是个很酷的老头。

cues.en: He looked like Ernest Hemingway.
cues.zh: 他长得像欧内斯特·海明威。

cues.en: I liked Frank a lot.
cues.zh: 我非常喜欢弗兰克。

cues.en: He had a monkey farm on St.
cues.zh: 他在圣基茨岛上有个猴子养殖场，

cues.en: Kitts, Vervet Monkeys.
cues.zh: 养的是绿猴。

cues.en: And him and his wife, Roberta Palmer, who was also very cool, they ran
cues.zh: 他和他的妻子罗伯塔·帕尔默也都很酷，他们经营了

cues.en: an alcohol lab for years.
cues.zh: 一家酒精研究实验室好几年。

cues.en: They gave these fervent monkeys free access to rum and coke, and 5% of them would drink Tacoma on first exposure.
cues.zh: 他们让这些聪明的猴子自由饮用朗姆酒加可乐，结果有5%的猴子在第一次接触时就会喝塔科马酒。

cues.en: It was funny.
cues.zh: 真是有趣。

cues.en: They had videos of that, and it's like a frat party.
cues.zh: 他们有相关的视频，看起来就像兄弟会派对一样。

cues.en: It's very funny to watch these drunk monkeys, but 95% of them wouldn't drink Tacoma, right?
cues.zh: 看这些喝醉的家伙真是好笑，但95%的人都不会喝塔科马酒，对吧？

cues.en: They'd have a bit and stop, but 5% of them would.
cues.zh: 他们喝一点就会停下来，但有5%的人会继续喝。

cues.en: It was like.
cues.zh: 就好像……

cues.en: Where have you been all my life?
cues.zh: 我这一辈子你都去哪儿了？

cues.en: Like Barney Gumbel on The Simpsons, you know?
cues.zh: 就像《辛普森一家》里的巴尼·甘贝尔，你知道的吧？

cues.en: So alcohol is a great drug for some people.
cues.zh: 所以酒精对某些人来说确实是很好的药物。

cues.en: It wasn't for you.
cues.zh: 但对你来说不是。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: It's just a natural disposition to either being accelerated while you're taking alcohol or being, I guess, slowed down.
cues.zh: 这其实是一种天生的倾向，要么在饮酒时反应变快，要么，我想，反应变慢。

cues.en: Well, if you're very fortunate, let's say, and you really want to become an alcoholic, it would be good to be susceptible to the anxiety reduction element and the psychomotor stimulant
cues.zh: 嗯，如果你非常幸运，而且真的想变成酒鬼，那么对缓解焦虑的作用、促进心理运动的作用以及阿片类作用都敏感会比较好。

cues.en: element and the opiate element.
cues.zh: 还有那些其他作用。

cues.en: And then, you know, hooray.
cues.zh: 那样一来，嘿，太棒了。

cues.en: It's a very good drug, except it makes you stupid.
cues.zh: 这药效果很好，只是会让人变笨。

cues.en: That's also the part of the problem with being hedonistically oriented.
cues.zh: 这也是追求享乐主义所带来的问题之一。

cues.en: It's short-term gratification.
cues.zh: 那就是追求短期的满足感。

cues.en: It's like, that's fine, but...
cues.zh: 嗯，那样也行，但是……

cues.en: What do you pay for it?
cues.zh: 你得为此付出什么代价？

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: That was one of the reasons too why I completely stopped drinking is because the more successful I got, the bigger the price I
cues.zh: 这也是我彻底戒酒的原因之一，因为我的事业越成功，我就要支付的代价就越高。

cues.en: had to pay.
cues.zh: 不得不付款。

cues.en: Like taking half a day off became so valuable that I thought to myself, do I want to pass that up for two drinks?
cues.zh: 那我还不如不喝那两杯酒呢。

cues.en: Would I rather just not have the two drinks?
cues.zh: 嗯，另一件让我决定戒酒的事是，当我正在写第一本书的时候，我根本无法做到。

cues.en: Well, that was another thing that also convinced me to stop drinking is when I was working on my first book, I couldn't.
cues.zh: 首先，宿醉状态下工作在情感上要求实在太高了。

cues.en: First of all, it was too emotionally demanding to work on when I was hungover.
cues.zh: 再说，宿醉时工作对情绪的消耗也太大。

cues.en: Like I just couldn't handle it.
cues.zh: 我简直应付不来啊。

cues.en: It was just too much because, you know, reading about sadistic Auschwitz guards is rather disturbing at the best of times.
cues.zh: 那真的太难承受了，因为，你知道，即便在平常情况下，阅读关于奥斯威辛残忍看守人的描述也已经够令人不安的了。

cues.en: And if you're royally hungover, it's much worse.
cues.zh: 要是宿醉得厉害，情况会更糟。

cues.en: And also I couldn't edit because I couldn't think clearly.
cues.zh: 而且我也没法剪辑，因为思维无法清晰。

cues.en: And, you know, one of the things, so here's something to consider.
cues.zh: 你知道，有一点值得思考，

cues.en: In the biblical stories of transformation, Abraham, the story of Abraham is a good example of that.
cues.zh: 在圣经中的蜕变故事里，亚伯拉罕的故事就是很好的例子。

cues.en: So Abraham.
cues.zh: 所以亚伯拉罕。

cues.en: Abraham leaves the confines of his family.
cues.zh: 亚伯拉罕离开了家庭的庇护。

cues.en: He's from a wealthy family.
cues.zh: 他出身于一个富裕的家庭。

cues.en: He leaves the comfort in the confines of his family.
cues.zh: 他放弃了家庭带来的安逸生活。

cues.en: He goes out into the world.
cues.zh: 他走向了外面的世界。

cues.en: God comes to him as the spirit of adventure.
cues.zh: 上帝以冒险之灵的形象出现在他面前。

cues.en: And then Abraham goes through a series of transformations of personality.
cues.zh: 随后亚伯拉罕经历了一系列性格上的转变。

cues.en: His name is actually Abram, to begin with, A-B-R-A-M.
cues.zh: 他最初的姓名其实是亚伯兰，A-B-R-A-M。

cues.en: He's renamed about two-thirds of the way through the story.
cues.zh: 在故事进行到大约三分之二的位置时，他的名字被改了。

cues.en: And the reason for that is that his identity transforms so radically that it's as if he's a new person.
cues.zh: 之所以如此，是因为他的身份发生了极其彻底的改变，简直就像变成了另一个人。

cues.en: Okay, so what does he do?
cues.zh: 那么他到底做了什么？

cues.en: Well, he starts aiming up.
cues.zh: 他开始把目光投向更高处。

cues.en: And then his personality transforms.
cues.zh: 接着他的性格也发生了变化。

cues.en: He has to make a sacrifice.
cues.zh: 他必须做出牺牲。

cues.en: So he builds an altar and he makes a sacrifice.
cues.zh: 于是他筑起一座祭坛并献上祭品。

cues.en: Well, what's the sacrifice?
cues.zh: 那么这个祭品是什么呢？

cues.en: Well, you just said what the sacrifice is.
cues.zh: 你刚才不就说了祭品是什么吗。

cues.en: You jumped up a rung in terms of the field of opportunity and responsibility that was in front of you.
cues.zh: 你在面前的机遇与责任层面上升了一个层级。

cues.en: And you thought, oh, my time's too valuable to waste half a day.
cues.zh: 你心想，哦，我的时间太宝贵了，可不能浪费半天时间。

cues.en: Well, that also happened to me in graduate school.
cues.zh: 嗯，我在读研究生时也遇到过这种情况。

cues.en: It's like, no, I can't afford this anymore.
cues.zh: 就是那种，不行了，我再也负担不起了的感觉。

cues.en: And it's partly, it's not even I couldn't afford it.
cues.zh: 其实也不完全是负担不起，

cues.zh: 如此一来，人类就能在世代之间延续下去，而其中的核心显然就是男女之间

cues.en: women.
cues.zh: 的关系。

cues.en: Are there ways of approximating that?
cues.zh: 有办法近似实现那个状态吗？

cues.en: Well, obviously, but.
cues.zh: 嗯，显然有，但是……

cues.en: There are approximations.
cues.zh: 是有一些近似的方法的。

cues.en: And that doesn't mean, obviously, there are some people who have better friendships than their marriage, but that's irrelevant with regards to the main point because
cues.zh: 当然，这并不意味着就有人们的友谊比婚姻更牢固，但这一点与核心话题无关，因为

cues.en: we're talking about something that's an ideal.
cues.zh: 我们讨论的是一种理想状态。

cues.en: Everybody falls short of the ideal.
cues.zh: 每个人都不可能完全达到那种理想状态。

cues.en: But part of the reason you can't maintain sanity isn't in your head.
cues.zh: 但你无法保持心智正常的部分原因并不出在你的头脑里。

cues.en: Like, here's a definition of sanity.
cues.zh: 比如说，这是心智正常的定义：

cues.en: You're well enough socialized so other people can tell you when you're an idiot and you'll listen.
cues.zh: 你的社交能力足够好，能让别人指出你犯傻的时候，而你也会愿意倾听。

cues.en: So why is that a good solution?
cues.zh: 那为什么这会是个好解决办法呢？

cues.en: Well, there's a lot of other people.
cues.zh: 因为还有很多人在周围。

cues.en: And if they're giving you signals all the time, all you have to do is listen.
cues.zh: 如果他们一直给你发出信号，你只要认真倾听就行了。

cues.en: So that's a good deal for you.
cues.zh: 这对你来说真是很划算的买卖。

cues.en: You might think, well, that's, you know, sanity's in my head.
cues.zh: 你可能会想，嗯，我的头脑里可是有理智的。

cues.en: It's like, what
cues.zh: 那就是，什么？

cues.en: makes you think you can regulate yourself?
cues.zh: 是什么让你觉得自己能够自我约束？

cues.en: You're pretty goddamn complicated, you know?
cues.zh: 你知道吗，你其实相当复杂啊。

cues.en: So we regulate ourselves socially.
cues.zh: 所以我们会通过社交来约束自己。

cues.en: That's why we talk to each other.
cues.zh: 这就是我们彼此交流的原因。

cues.en: It's vital.
cues.zh: 这非常重要。

cues.en: That's so interesting.
cues.zh: 那真是太有趣了。

cues.en: I feel like, once again, what you're saying, I feel like I'm like struck with my...
cues.zh: 我再次觉得，你所说的话让我有种……

cues.en: pride a little bit.
cues.zh: 有点自豪的感觉。

cues.en: Like I feel like I can regulate myself.
cues.zh: 就好像我觉得自己能够自我约束一样。

cues.en: I can always aim up or try to do what is right and think, well, I guess I'm still basing my decision-making because a heuristic
cues.zh: 我总能努力向上看，尝试做正确的事，同时心想，我想我的决策依然是在依靠某种启发式方法。

cues.en: I use a lot of the time when I'm trying to decide what to do between like a moral conundrum is like, what would the optimal person in this situation do?
cues.zh: 每当我面临道德困境、不知道该怎么做时，我常常会问自己，处于这种状况下的最理想的人会怎么做？

cues.en: And completely remove myself from this situation.
cues.zh: 然后完全将自己从那种情境中抽离出来。

cues.en: And then I do that.
cues.zh: 之后我就会这么做。

cues.en: But I guess that's also relating.
cues.zh: 不过我想这也算是有关联的吧。

cues.en: Well, that's right.
cues.zh: 嗯，没错。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: That's a good observation.
cues.zh: 观察得很到位。

cues.en: What you've done to some degree is you've constructed an idealized representation of another, or
cues.zh: 你在某种程度上构建了另一个人的理想化形象，或者说，

cues.en: a human being for that matter.
cues.zh: 其实也是对人类的理想化形象。

cues.en: That's like the son of man in the Christian conception.
cues.zh: 这就好比基督教概念里的‘人子’。

cues.en: That's a good way of thinking about it.
cues.zh: 用这种方式来思考确实不错。

cues.en: So what you're doing...
cues.zh: 所以你正在做的……

cues.en: when you do that is no different from what, say, evangelical Christians do when they ask themselves, what would Jesus do?
cues.zh: 你这么做和那些福音派基督徒问自己‘耶稣会怎么做’的做法没什么不同。

cues.en: It's exactly the same thing.
cues.zh: 完全是一回事。

cues.en: And it's pulled from real people.
cues.zh: 这些内容取自真实人物。

cues.en: It's just certain components about them.
cues.zh: 只是选取了他们身上的某些特质。

cues.en: So they're still technically impressing upon me.
cues.zh: 所以从技术层面来讲，他们仍在给我留下深刻印象。

cues.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
cues.zh: 是的，是的，是的。

cues.en: You're essentially fabricating.
cues.zh: 你本质上是在编造。

cues.en: Out of whole cloth, something approximating a classic religious orientation.
cues.zh: 凭空创造出某种类似传统宗教观念的东西。

cues.en: What would someone who is ideal do in this situation?
cues.zh: 在这种情况下，一个理想的人会怎么做？

cues.en: Well, see, if you delved into that, this is where the religious investigation would take place.
cues.zh: 嗯，你看，如果你深入探究这个问题，宗教层面的分析就会从这里开始。

cues.en: It's like, okay, who is this ideal that you're calling upon?
cues.zh: 就好比在问，你所依赖的这个理想人物究竟是谁？

cues.en: What's the characterization of that ideal?
cues.zh: 那个理想的特征是什么？

cues.en: You could write that all down.
cues.zh: 你可以把这一切都记下来。

cues.en: You'd see what your ideal is.
cues.zh: 这样你就能看清自己的理想是什么了。

cues.en: And then you'd see that it has...
cues.zh: 然后你就会发现它具有……

cues.en: And that it approximates the figure of the hero in mythology, insofar as it has any utility to you.
cues.zh: 而且就其对你的实用价值而言，它与神话中的英雄形象颇为相似。

cues.en: I told my friend this, and he said, that is the start of religion, or that is God to people.
cues.zh: 我把这番话告诉了我的朋友，他说那就是宗教的起点，或者说对人们而言那就是上帝。

cues.en: Yeah, well, that's the intermediary figure in some ways.
cues.zh: 没错，从某些方面来看，那确实是一个中介性的存在。

cues.en: There's the transcendent ultimate unity, let's say, but that's ineffable.
cues.zh: 比如说还有那种超越性的终极统一，但那是无法用语言描述的。

cues.en: It's difficult to establish a relationship with.
cues.zh: 很难与它建立联系。

cues.en: There's some intermediary figure.
cues.zh: 存在某种中介性的存在。

cues.en: That's the role that Christ plays in Christianity, right?
cues.zh: 在基督教里，基督扮演的正是这样的角色，对吧？

cues.en: That's God brought down to earth.
cues.zh: 那就是降临人间的上帝。

cues.en: Why is Christ an ideal?
cues.zh: 为什么基督堪称理想人物？

cues.en: Because he welcomes the catastrophe of fate, right?
cues.zh: 因为他能接纳命运带来的灾难，对吧？

cues.en: And so there's no ideal person who doesn't do that.
cues.zh: 所以不存在不这样做的理想之人。

cues.en: I mean, James Bond does that.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，詹姆斯·邦德也是这样做的。

cues.en: Like, well, seriously, like anybody that attracts your admiration is going to have that welcoming attitude towards
cues.zh: 说真的，任何能赢得你钦佩的人，都会对

cues.en: even the difficulties of existence.
cues.zh: 甚至生存中的种种困难也持接纳态度。

cues.en: That's going to be a stellar part of their character.
cues.zh: 这会成为他们性格中极为出色的一部分。

cues.en: Otherwise, you wouldn't admire them.
cues.zh: 否则你就不会钦佩他们了。

cues.en: You admire people who can maintain themselves across a catastrophe, right?
cues.zh: 人们钦佩的是那些能在灾难中依然保持自我的人，对吧？

cues.en: So the most admirable person is the person who can maintain themselves the best across the worst possible catastrophe.
cues.zh: 所以最值得钦佩的人，就是在最糟糕的灾难中仍能最好地保持自我的人。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: And so that'll be lurking at the back of the ideal.
cues.zh: 而这也会潜藏在理想的背后。

cues.en: So welcoming suffering and welcoming the catastrophe reminds me of Man's Search for Meaning, which for me was one of the most important books I've ever
cues.zh: 如此接纳苦难与接受灾难，让我想起了《人性的尊严》，对我来说那是我有生以来读过最重要的书籍之一

cues.en: read.
cues.zh: 请开始阅读。

cues.en: And he also quoted...
cues.zh: 他还引用了……

cues.en: a man who has a why can bear almost any how, right?
cues.zh: 有一个明确目标的人，几乎可以承受任何实现方式，对吧？

cues.en: Which is what you quoted earlier, which is really interesting.
cues.zh: 这正是你之前引用的内容，实在很有意思。

cues.en: Are there any other books or authors where if you were to tell the viewers right now, if they started listening to them or reading them, that would make
cues.zh: 还有没有其他书籍或作者，要是现在就告诉观众去阅读或聆听他们的作品，会很有帮助的？

cues.en: one of the biggest impacts that they can possibly- Well, that's a good one.
cues.zh: 他们可能带来的最重大的影响之一——嗯，这确实是个很好的点。

cues.en: Modern Man's Search for a Soul, that's Jung's book.
cues.zh: 《现代人的灵魂追寻》，那是荣格写的书。

cues.en: That's a very good book.
cues.zh: 那是一本非常好的书。

cues.en: The Gulag Archipelago is like Viktor Frankl on steroids, but it's a voyage,
cues.zh: 《古拉格群岛》就像是强化版的维克多·弗兰克尔作品，但这是一段旅程。

cues.en: that book.
cues.zh: 那本书。

cues.en: Frankl's book has the advantage of being pretty accessible.
cues.zh: 弗兰克尔的这本书有个优点，就是相当容易理解。

cues.en: It's accessible, but it's profound.
cues.zh: 这本书虽然通俗易懂，但内涵十分深刻。

cues.en: It's relatively short.
cues.zh: 篇幅相对较短。

cues.en: So that's a pretty good deal.
cues.zh: 那可真是相当划算了。

cues.en: Notes from Underground, anything Dostoevsky wrote.
cues.zh: 《地下笔记》，还有陀思妥耶夫斯基写的任何作品。

cues.en: Beyond Good and Evil, although that's a rough one.
cues.zh: 《善恶的彼岸》，不过那本比较难读。

cues.en: That's hard on people, that book.
cues.zh: 那本书对读者来说确实很有冲击力。

cues.en: But Viktor Frankl's book is singular in some ways in the popular literature because of
cues.zh: 不过维克多·弗兰克尔的这本书在通俗文学中独树一帜，原因在于

cues.en: its combination of depth and accessibility.
cues.zh: 它兼具深度与通俗性。

cues.en: I read Crime and Punishment because of you.
cues.zh: 是因为你，我才去读《罪与罚》的。

cues.en: And I had never, this was the first book I've ever read of that type.
cues.zh: 而我以前从未读过这类书，那是我第一次读这类作品。

cues.en: That was so deep.
cues.zh: 那本书实在太有深度了。

cues.en: And it's interesting because now it reminds me of the conversation we had earlier where the emotions that they can bring out in the reader are so gut
cues.zh: 有趣的是，它让我想起我们早先的对话，书中能唤起读者的情感实在是非常强烈。

cues.en: -wrenching.
cues.zh: 极其令人揪心。

cues.en: And it's like pain, but it's positive and negative at the exact same time.
cues.zh: 它就像痛苦，但同时又兼具积极与消极的意味。

cues.en: That's right.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: And just like classical music, great classical music.
cues.zh: 就像古典音乐，尤其是那些优秀的古典音乐。

cues.en: But it was a whole different set of emotions I feel like I hadn't experienced before.
cues.zh: 但我感受到的是一套完全不同的情感，是我以前从未体验过的。

cues.en: And I found that interesting because I guess overall, there was a lot of meaning in the book and it brought about a different experience of life I hadn't previously experienced.
cues.zh: 我觉得这很有趣，因为总体而言，这本书蕴含着丰富的意义，让我获得了此前从未有过的全新生活体验。

cues.en: But at the same time, it was the contending of the positive and negative emotions.
cues.zh: 但与此同时，其中也存在着积极与消极情感的交织。

cues.en: And also, I mean, the way that Dostoevsky can write is so descriptive and accurate.
cues.zh: 而且，陀思妥耶夫斯基的写作方式极为生动且精准。

cues.en: Well, it's also a great adventure story, a great thriller, a great crime novel.
cues.zh: 它同时也是一部精彩的冒险故事、出色的惊悚作品以及优秀的犯罪小说。

cues.en: It's an amazing book.
cues.zh: 这是一本非常了不起的书。

cues.en: What are your thoughts on Eckhart Tolle?
cues.zh: 你对埃克哈特·托尔有什么看法？

cues.en: I don't know enough about him really to...
cues.zh: 实际上我对他的了解还不够多，所以……

cues.en: to comment in depth.
cues.zh: 进行深入评论。

cues.en: I mean, Eckhart Tolle is part of that 1960s humanist movement, essentially.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，埃克哈特·托尔本质上属于20世纪60年代的人文主义运动。

cues.en: And fundamentally, the humanists were wrong.
cues.zh: 而从根本上说，那些人文主义者是错的。

cues.en: And so that would go along with, say, conceptions like self-actualization.
cues.zh: 这也和自我实现之类的观念相契合。

cues.en: That would be Abraham Maslow.
cues.zh: 那就是亚伯拉罕·马斯洛提出的概念。

cues.en: And what did Carl Rogers describe it as?
cues.zh: 那卡尔·罗杰斯又是如何描述它的呢？

cues.en: Something like the fully functional person, the person whose actions are commensurate with their utterances, who's transparent to themselves and others, who
cues.zh: 大致就是指那种功能完备的人，其行为与言语一致，对自己和他人都保持坦诚的人。

cues.en: communicates in a manner that's striving to bring themselves and other people upward.
cues.zh: 这样的人会以一种努力提升自己和他人境界的方式与他人交流。

cues.en: But it's all within a humanist framework.
cues.zh: 但这一切都仍在人文主义的框架之内。

cues.en: And in the final analysis, that's...
cues.zh: 归根结底，那就是……

cues.en: It's weak.
cues.zh: 它很脆弱。

cues.en: It can't withstand ideological assault with any degree of resistance.
cues.zh: 它根本无法抵抗任何形式的意识形态冲击。

cues.en: I found Eckhart Tolle to be...
cues.zh: 我觉得埃克哈特·托尔的作品……

cues.en: I mean, his two books were also some of the most important books I've ever read.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，他的那两本书也是我读过的重要著作之一。

cues.en: A New Earth and The Power of Now.
cues.zh: 《新地球》和《活在当下》。

cues.en: Both of those made tremendous differences.
cues.zh: 这两本书都带来了巨大的改变。

cues.en: A lot of it has to do...
cues.zh: 其中很多内容都与……

cues.en: The fundamental...
cues.zh: 最根本的……

cues.en: The idea of those books is very similar to what a lot of different philosophers say.
cues.zh: 那些书所传达的理念与许多不同哲学家的观点非常相似。

cues.en: A lot of philosophers, when you boil it down, like I'm sure you know that the fundamentals are pretty much the same.
cues.zh: 归根结底，很多哲学家的观点其实都差不多，我相信你也知道这一点。

cues.en: It's just the abstractions from it differ.
cues.zh: 只是他们从中抽象出的内容有所不同。

cues.en: I feel like if you've, I'm sure you've observed that, but I think those two books were some of the most important things for me, at least to use as tools to alleviate.
cues.zh: 我觉得如果你留意过的话就会发现，至少对我来说，那两本书是非常重要的，可以当作缓解压力的工具。

cues.en: I learned a lot from the humans when like Rogers and Naslo, for example, when I read them when I was, I don't know, something approximately, how old are you?
cues.zh: 比如罗杰斯和纳斯洛这类人物，我在阅读他们的作品时学到了很多东西，当时我大概……你多大了？

cues.en: So a little, how old are you?
cues.zh: 那再小一点，你多大了？

cues.en: I read them when I was a little younger than you and they had, I learned a lot from Rogers and from Naslo.
cues.zh: 我在比你稍年轻的时候读过那些书，从罗杰斯和纳斯洛那里我学到了很多东西。

cues.en: So the effect that a book has on you depends to some non-trivial degree on where you happen to be standing when you encounter the book.
cues.zh: 一本书对你产生的影响，在很大程度上取决于你遇到这本书时的处境。

cues.en: And if the person who's writing the book knows much more than you do about something at that moment, well, then the book can be very enlightening.
cues.zh: 如果写这本书的人在某个方面比你懂得更多，那么这本书就会带来极大的启发。

cues.en: And lots of books, like I learned a lot from Freud.
cues.zh: 还有很多书，比如我从弗洛伊德那里也学到了很多。

cues.en: I think Freud was fundamentally wrong in his insistence that...
cues.zh: 我认为弗洛伊德坚持认为……这一观点从根本上是错误的。

cues.en: It was the hedonic element that drove life itself.
cues.zh: 是享乐元素驱动着生命本身。

cues.en: He used the sexual impulse as a stand-in for hedonic orientation.
cues.zh: 他用性冲动来代表享乐倾向。

cues.en: I just don't think that's true, but I still learned a lot from reading Freud.
cues.zh: 我觉得那并不正确，但即便如此，我读弗洛伊德的书还是学到了很多。

cues.en: Lots of thinkers can be...
cues.zh: 很多思想家……

cues.en: wrong in some ways and right in others.
cues.zh: 在某些方面可能犯错，而在其他方面则是对的。

cues.en: And, you know, a discriminating reader pulls out the wheat, leaves the chaff behind.
cues.zh: 而且，你知道的，一个有眼光的读者能够挑选出精华，抛弃糟粕。

cues.en: I learned a lot from Ernest Becker's book, The Denial of Death, which is sort of the ultimate extension of the Freudian view.
cues.zh: 我从欧内斯特·贝克尔的《死亡的否定》这本书中学到了很多，它可以说是弗洛伊德观点的进一步延伸。

cues.en: It's a brilliant book.
cues.zh: 这是一本非常出色的书。

cues.en: It's wrong, but it's brilliant.
cues.zh: 虽然有误，但确实很出色。

cues.en: And there's much in it that's correct.
cues.zh: 而且书中有很多内容是正确的。

cues.en: Fundamentally, it's wrong because Becker believed that the heroic orientation in life was also a form of defense
cues.zh: 从根本上说它是错的，因为贝克尔认为人生中的英雄主义取向也是一种防御方式，

cues.en: against death anxiety.
cues.zh: 用来抵御对死亡的焦虑。

cues.en: It's just, that's not.
cues.zh: 其实并非如此。

cues.en: It's a good theory.
cues.zh: 这是个不错的理论。

cues.en: It's an interesting theory.
cues.zh: 这是个有趣的理论。

cues.en: Sometimes it's true, but fundamentally it's true.
cues.zh: 有时候它是正确的，但从根本上讲并不对。

cues.en: You wrote in your book about growing up and living a very poor life, at least financially speaking, and
cues.zh: 你在书中写过自己成长过程中生活十分贫困，至少在经济方面如此，而且

cues.en: that you were an assistant professor supporting a family, and your wife Tammy had no green card, so she couldn't work, and you have a funny story about selling a neighbor a

cues.zh: 乔丹，非常感谢你来到本节目，这对我来说意义重大。

cues.en: It really means a lot.
cues.zh: 我真的非常感激。

cues.en: Really appreciate it.
cues.zh: 谢谢大家收看。

cues.en: Thank you guys for watching.
cues.zh: 请关注彼得森学院，链接在下方。

cues.en: Check out Peterson Academy.
cues.zh: 谢谢。

cues.en: It'll be linked down below.
cues.zh: 谢谢。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 再见。

cues.en: Till next time.
cues.zh: 下次再见。

cues.en: Thank you guys.
cues.zh: 谢谢大家。

material.title: 冰咖啡时刻 · 迈克·罗谈职业选择
material.subtitle: The Iced Coffee Hour · Mike Rowe： How To Make $10,000 Per Month In 90 Days - No Degree Required! · 英文自动字幕

cues.en: People say to me, Mike Will, are you ever going to run out of Dirty Jobs?
cues.zh: 人们总问我，迈克·威尔，你的‘脏活’节目什么时候会没活儿可拍？

cues.en: And I say, not this season.
cues.zh: 而我总是回答，这个季节不会。

cues.en: I know you love that, America.
cues.zh: 我知道你们很喜欢这个节目，美国观众们。

cues.en: The great dirty secret of Dirty Jobs, we probably featured 45 multimillionaires on that show.
cues.zh: 《脏活》节目有个不为人知的秘密，我们曾在节目中介绍过45位千万富翁。

cues.en: You would have never known it because they were covering the s**t or something worse.
cues.zh: 你们根本不会察觉，因为他们都在处理那些糟糕至极的事情，甚至更恶劣的状况。

cues.en: You became famous showing America the jobs that we all depend on.
cues.zh: 你通过向美国展示我们所有人都依赖的工作而走红。

cues.en: Why did we stop respecting these jobs?
cues.zh: 为什么我们不再尊重这些工作了呢？

cues.en: I think the fault has to do with our tendency to resent that which we rely upon.
cues.zh: 我觉得问题出在我们总会对自己所依赖的事物心生怨恨。

cues.en: What about the fact that for every five tradespeople who retire, two replace them?
cues.zh: 那每有五名技工退休，就有两人接替他们这件事又怎么说？

cues.en: I don't have to be an economist to tell you that.
cues.zh: 我不需要是经济学家就能告诉你们这一点。

cues.en: That's not sustainable.
cues.zh: 这种状况是难以持续的。

cues.en: There are seven million able-bodied men right now who are not only not working, They're not looking for work.
cues.zh: 目前有七百万身体健康的男性不仅没有工作，甚至也不在找工作。

cues.en: That's never happened in our country, not in peacetime.
cues.zh: 我们国家从来没发生过这种事，和平时期更是绝无仅有。

cues.en: Anyway, 7 million men.
cues.zh: 不管怎样，就是700万男人。

cues.en: What do you think happened?
cues.zh: 你觉得到底发生了什么？

cues.en: Mike Rowe, thank you so much for coming on the Iced Coffee Hour.
cues.zh: 迈克·罗，非常感谢您能来到《冰咖啡时刻》。

cues.en: Well, you're welcome.
cues.zh: 不用客气。

cues.en: But did I really come on your hour or did you come to the place where I record?
cues.zh: 不过真的是我来参加您的节目，还是您来到了我录制节目的地方？

cues.en: Yeah, we came to San Francisco just for you.
cues.zh: 没错，我们专程为了您来到了旧金山。

cues.en: We were so excited for this.
cues.zh: 我们对这次见面感到无比兴奋。

cues.en: Then let me officially thank you for doing that.
cues.zh: 那我就正式感谢您所做的一切。

cues.en: I know it's a pain in the ass to travel these days, especially into San Francisco, where half the runways are closed for no good reason.
cues.zh: 我知道现在出行很麻烦，尤其是去旧金山，那里有一半的跑道毫无理由就关闭了。

cues.en: Well, for me, this is big because I've been a huge fan of you and Dirty Jobs.
cues.zh: 对我来说这意义重大，因为我一直是您以及《肮脏的工作》节目的忠实粉丝。

cues.en: I grew up watching Dirty Jobs.
cues.zh: 我是在看《肮脏的工作》节目长大的。

cues.en: And in fact, you inspired this.
cues.zh: 事实上，正是你激励了我这么做。

cues.en: I kept it up briefly on my channel.
cues.zh: 我在自己的频道上短暂地继续做了这些内容。

cues.en: It's called Undercover Millionaire.
cues.zh: 那个频道叫《卧底百万富翁》。

cues.en: What I did is I worked these jobs that you would have no idea made a whole bunch of money.
cues.zh: 我所做的就是从事那些你根本想不到能赚很多钱的工作。

cues.en: Window washing.
cues.zh: 洗窗户。

cues.en: This kid made a thousand dollars a day.
cues.zh: 有个小伙子每天能赚一千美元。

cues.en: Car washing.
cues.zh: 洗汽车。

cues.en: This kid made five hundred dollars a day.
cues.zh: 有个小伙子每天能赚五百美元。

cues.en: Dog walking.
cues.zh: 遛狗。

cues.en: and running a dog business that was making $1,500 a day.
cues.zh: 还有经营狗狗相关业务，每天能赚1500美元。

cues.en: And so I found these jobs that were making a whole bunch of money.
cues.zh: 所以我找到了这些能赚大钱的工作。

cues.en: And then from doing that, people would reach out to me.
cues.zh: 之后，就有人主动联系我了。

cues.en: Incredible businesses.
cues.zh: 真是了不起的企业。

cues.en: And you were the inspiration for that.
cues.zh: 而您正是这一切的灵感来源。

cues.en: Well, wow.
cues.zh: 哇，太棒了。

cues.en: Thank you.
cues.zh: 谢谢您。

cues.en: You know, that was a big part of the thesis of the show that didn't get talked about enough.
cues.zh: 您知道，这其实是该节目论点中非常重要却很少被提及的部分。

cues.en: It was the underpinning of entrepreneurship.
cues.zh: 它是创业精神的基石。

cues.en: Like, first and foremost, it was a TV show, right?
cues.zh: 首先，这毕竟是一档电视节目，对吧？

cues.en: Like, it had to have some entertainment spectacle to it.
cues.zh: 它总得有一些娱乐性的看点。

cues.en: So there was always an exploding toilet or some misadventure and animal husbandry or, you know, some crazy thing that would get you to watch.
cues.zh: 所以总会有马桶爆炸、各种意外状况、畜牧相关的内容，或是其他一些疯狂的情节来吸引观众。

cues.en: But if you really paid attention, as you obviously did over time, you know, we did 350 of those things and you would almost always find
cues.zh: 但如果您真的仔细观看，就像您后来所做的那样，要知道我们一共做了350集这样的内容，您几乎总能发现

cues.en: in every episode, not in every segment, but in every episode, you would find a buried love letter to entrepreneurship.
cues.zh: 在每一集中，虽然不是每个片段，但每一集里都藏着写给创业精神的一封隐秘情书。

cues.en: And you would find a rumination on the dignity of work.
cues.zh: 同时也能看到对工作尊严的思考。

cues.en: And you would find humor that often exists on job sites, but doesn't get baked into a lot of popular portrayals
cues.zh: 你还会发现工作现场常常存在的那种幽默感，只不过在很多流行的作品里并没有被展现出来。

cues.en: of work.
cues.zh: 工作。

cues.en: The great dirty secret of dirty jobs, which nobody really believes to this day, but you will because you watch for all these reasons.
cues.zh: 那些脏活累活背后那个鲜为人知的秘密，至今都没人真正相信，但因为你看了这些内容，你就会相信了。

cues.en: We probably featured 40 to 45 multimillionaires on that show.
cues.zh: 在那档节目中，我们大概请到了40到45位千万富翁出场。

cues.en: You would have never known it because they were covered in shit or something worse.
cues.zh: 你根本看不出来，因为他们浑身都是污秽，甚至状况更糟。

cues.en: What's the job that made the most money that would shock people?
cues.zh: 有什么高薪工作会让人感到震惊呢？

cues.en: The answer will be one of the segments that was really about entrepreneurship.
cues.zh: 答案会出自那个真正探讨创业主题的环节。

cues.en: Again, it's the story nobody tells, but the business of mastering a trade and taking the
cues.zh: 这又是没人愿意讲的故事，也就是掌握一门手艺并从事

cues.en: reverse commute, right?
cues.zh: 反向通勤的工作，对吧？

cues.en: In other words, seeing where everybody else is going and totally taking your passion and your dreams and setting them off to
cues.zh: 换句话说，就是看着其他人都往哪个方向走，而完全凭着自己的热情和梦想，选择朝完全不同的方向前进。

cues.en: the side and saying, no, I'm going in the other direction.
cues.zh: 不去随大流，而是说，不，我要往另一个方向走。

cues.en: I'm going to find the opportunity.
cues.zh: 我要去寻找机会。

cues.en: I'm going to get great at it.
cues.zh: 我会把它练得非常出色。

cues.en: And then I'm going to find a way to love it.
cues.zh: 然后我会找到办法去爱上它。

cues.en: You know, the answer to your question is probably less Swanson comes to mind.
cues.zh: 你知道，对你问题的答案可能是斯旺森出现的次数会变少。

cues.en: He was a guy in Wisconsin who I met in the pilots, like in the very, very, very early days.
cues.zh: 他是威斯康星州的人，我在项目初期就认识了他。

cues.en: He put me in his honey wagon.
cues.zh: 他让我上了他的运蜜车。

cues.en: This is outside of Madison.
cues.zh: 那是在麦迪逊郊外。

cues.en: And, and we went to clean out a pumping station.
cues.zh: 然后，我们去了一个泵站清理工作。

cues.en: on the side of the road which you would never recognize as a thing it's just a it looks like a concrete bunker you probably drove past
cues.zh: 就在路边，你根本看不出那是什么地方，看上去就像一个混凝土掩体，你可能开车从旁边经过过。

cues.en: a couple on your way in but when you go in They go down four or five stories sometimes.
cues.zh: 进去的时候会有一对夫妇在，但一旦进去，楼梯会向下延伸四五层。

cues.en: And that's where all the crap accumulates in a given zip code.
cues.zh: 在那个邮编范围内，所有的垃圾都会堆积在那里。

cues.en: And it's just an unspeakable level of hell at a glance, right?
cues.zh: 光是看一眼就能知道，那简直就是难以形容的地狱景象，对吧？

cues.en: It's like 104 degrees, crazy hot in Wisconsin.
cues.zh: 威斯康星州的温度有104华氏度，热得离谱。

cues.en: We were standing up to our nipples in the filthiest of the filth, knocking cholesterol off the walls, talking.
cues.zh: 我们站在极其肮脏的环境里，脏得几乎没过乳头，一边清理墙上的胆固醇，一边交谈。

cues.en: That's really what Dirty Jobs was.
cues.zh: 《肮脏的工作》其实就是这样的节目。

cues.en: It was an interview.
cues.zh: 那其实是一次访谈。

cues.en: It was a talk show in a sewer, you know, nine out of 10 times.
cues.zh: 十有八九，那就像在下水道里举办的脱口秀。

cues.en: Unless at one point it was just so hot and so miserable.
cues.zh: 除非有时候天气实在太热，环境也实在太恶劣。

cues.en: And there was really nothing to do except what I did, which was look at him and say, how did you wind up here, man?
cues.zh: 那时除了我做的那样——看着他问‘你是怎么走到这一步的，伙计？’，真的没什么别的可做的。

cues.en: Like, what happened to you?
cues.zh: 也就是，你到底发生了什么事？

cues.en: And his answer was, he was a guidance counselor for years.
cues.zh: 他的回答是，他当了多年指导顾问。

cues.en: And then he had a practice, like a psychiatric practice.
cues.zh: 之后他开了家诊所，算是心理科诊所。

cues.en: And then he turned 50 or so.
cues.zh: 大概到了50岁左右的时候，

cues.en: And he just went in another direction.
cues.zh: 他就选择了另一条路。

cues.en: And I said, but why?
cues.zh: 我就问，可为什么呢？

cues.en: You know, I mean, remember, we're literally covered in crap, like working in the most inhospitable environment you can imagine.
cues.zh: 你知道，我的意思是，回想一下，我们当时简直浑身都是污垢，工作的环境也是你能想象到的最恶劣的。

cues.en: And without missing a beat, he said, I got tired of dealing with other people's shit.
cues.zh: 他立刻回答说，我受够了处理别人的烂摊子。

cues.en: And, you know, it was one of those unscripted moments.
cues.zh: 那真是个即兴的瞬间。

cues.en: And you start thinking, so wait a minute, turns out he owns three or four honey wagons.
cues.zh: 你开始想，等等，原来他还有三四辆运蜜车。

cues.en: Turns out he's got, you know, a dozen people working for him.
cues.zh: 原来他有十几个人为他工作。

cues.en: Turns out he's got a summer house.
cues.zh: 原来他还有栋避暑别墅。

cues.en: Turns out he's got a margarita machine by his built-in swimming pool.
cues.zh: 原来他在自家室内游泳池旁还有一台玛格丽塔酒机。

cues.en: Turns out he's living a pretty great life.
cues.zh: 原来他的生活相当不错。

cues.en: Anyway, sorry for the rant, but that's the answer are men and women like that who actually used
cues.zh: 不管怎样，抱歉说了这么多，答案就是那些像他这样的男女，他们确实

cues.en: a dirty job.
cues.zh: 从事过脏活累活。

cues.en: to build a going concern.
cues.zh: 以此打造出一番事业。

cues.en: What makes a trade higher or lower earning?
cues.zh: 是什么让某种职业的收入更高或更低？

cues.en: Is it the obstacle to enter the trade?
cues.zh: 这是进入该行业面临的障碍吗？

cues.en: Is it how dirty a trade is?
cues.zh: 是这个行业有多脏吗？

cues.en: Is it just like how many- Or is it the operator?
cues.zh: 只是和人数有关——还是和操作人员有关？

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: How many people want to get into it?
cues.zh: 有多少人想从事这个行业？

cues.en: What determines the pay of a trade?
cues.zh: 是什么决定了一个行业的薪资？

cues.en: So many things.
cues.zh: 很多因素都会影响。

cues.en: The time in the century to which you're referring.
cues.zh: 你说的那个世纪里的时间。

cues.en: the day of the week, the state that we happen to be in.
cues.zh: 一周中的哪一天，以及我们所在的州。

cues.en: Was it union?
cues.zh: 是工会制度导致的吗？

cues.en: Was it non-union?
cues.zh: 是非工会制度导致的吗？

cues.en: I mean, there's a long, long list.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，相关因素多得数不清。

cues.en: Like my foundation has helped train hundreds of welders.
cues.zh: 我的基金会已经帮助培训了数百名焊工。

cues.en: Some of them are making $300,000 a year right now.
cues.zh: 他们当中有些人现在的年收入高达30万美元。

cues.en: Others are making $58,000 a year.
cues.zh: 还有些人的年收入是5.8万美元。

cues.en: The thing about the trades, and I think it's probably true of everything else too, is you can't paint with too broad a brush.
cues.zh: 从事技术工种有个特点，我觉得其他行业可能也是如此，那就是不能用过于宽泛的方式处理问题。

cues.en: Actually, you can, but you shouldn't.
cues.zh: 其实也可以，但不应该这么做。

cues.en: I was just in Plano, Texas, and touring a data center.
cues.zh: 我刚去过德克萨斯州的普莱诺，参观了一座数据中心。

cues.en: I met three electricians, all making north of $240,000 a year, 240 to 280.
cues.zh: 我遇到了三名电工，他们每年的收入都在24万美元以上，具体在24万到28万之间。

cues.en: Electricians, no college.
cues.zh: 这些电工都没有上过大学。

cues.en: Two of them were former submarine guys out of the Navy, and the other just went through.
cues.zh: 其中两人曾是海军潜艇船员，另一人则是通过常规的技术学校培训毕业的。

cues.en: the typical trade school process.
cues.zh: 没有负债。

cues.en: No debt.
cues.zh: 最令人惊讶的是，这三人都在之前的18个月内被其他公司挖走了三次。

cues.en: And the craziest part of the stat is they were all poached three times in the prior 18 months.
cues.zh: 而这个数据最令人惊讶的地方在于，他们在之前的18个月内竟然都被挖角过三次。

cues.en: Now, what's true in Plano right now with data centers might not be true in Boise, might not be true in Tallahassee.
cues.zh: 现在，普莱诺的数据中心行业状况或许适用于当地，但在博伊西或塔拉哈西可能就不适用了。

cues.en: I don't know.
cues.zh: 我不知道。

cues.en: But what I can tell you is the...
cues.zh: 但我可以告诉你们的是……

cues.en: The entire economy is flipped with regard to job security and with regard to the definition of a good
cues.zh: 整个经济在就业保障以及‘好工作’的定义方面都发生了变化。

cues.en: job.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 确实如此。

cues.en: Now, a lot of people believe that the jobs market is weak and the average American can't pay a thousand dollar emergency.
cues.zh: 很多人认为就业市场疲软，普通美国人无力承担一千美元的紧急开支。

cues.en: From your perspective, what's the reality on this?
cues.zh: 从您的角度来看，实际情况是怎样的？

cues.en: I think that's probably true, but I don't spend a lot of time.
cues.zh: 我觉得这可能是真的，但我不会花太多时间去

cues.en: agonizing over the plate of the average American.
cues.zh: 为普通美国人的生活困境苦恼。

cues.en: And I know that sounds kind of crappy, but I'm not running for office, right?
cues.zh: 我知道这么说听起来有点糟糕，但我又不是在参选，对吧？

cues.en: I'm not even running for a renewal on a show.
cues.zh: 我甚至都不是在争取节目续约。

cues.en: You know what I would do?
cues.zh: 你知道我会怎么做吗？

cues.en: I would refer you to a terrific book.
cues.zh: 我会推荐你一本非常棒的书。

cues.en: I bet your viewers would dig it.
cues.zh: 我敢肯定你的观众会很喜欢它。

cues.en: It's by a guy called Todd Rose.
cues.zh: 这本书的作者是托德·罗斯。

cues.en: He runs a think tank up in Boston.
cues.zh: 他在波士顿经营一家智库。

cues.en: He's written three amazing books.
cues.zh: 他已经写了三本很出色的书。

cues.en: The first is called The End of Average.
cues.zh: 第一本的书名是《平均值的终结》。

cues.en: And it goes to your question, right?
cues.zh: 这正好回应了你的问题，对吧？

cues.en: It goes to this idea.
cues.zh: 它探讨的是这样一个观点：

cues.en: that we have it in our heads that there is this state that most people
cues.zh: 我们总觉得存在一种大多数人都

cues.en: fit in.
cues.zh: 能够适应的状态。

cues.en: That's the average state.
cues.zh: 那就是所谓的平均状态。

cues.en: It could be average intelligence.
cues.zh: 可能是普通智力而已。

cues.en: It could be average height.
cues.zh: 可能是普通身高罢了。

cues.en: It could be so many different things.
cues.zh: 可能是很多不同的因素。

cues.en: But what Todd basically argues is that it's all nonsense.
cues.zh: 但托德基本上认为这一切都是无稽之谈。

cues.en: It's all rooted in a fallacy.
cues.zh: 这一切都源于一个错误观念。

cues.en: And he gives lots of examples, like the Air Force spent a fortune trying to build a cockpit in their fighter jets that

cues.zh: 七个月前，我和这位总统以及另外35位掌管着当前国家运作的CEO们一起在匹兹堡参加了那场能源会议。

cues.zh: 我希望看到制造业重新焕发生机。

cues.zh: 我希望看到所有这些工作岗位都恢复起来。

cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: Yep.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: to go through the course.
cues.zh: 让你能够完成这个课程。

cues.zh: 它将会改变我们对证书、要求、培训以及金钱的认知。

cues.zh: 我不会重新考虑的。

cues.zh: 那是七年前，那时这个职业变得非常流行。

cues.zh: 现在软件工程师已经供过于求，而人工智能似乎也在很大程度上分流了这一领域的需求。

cues.zh: 他就站在那里。

cues.zh: 我看着那一幕，心里想着：天哪。

cues.zh: 他在唱你的歌呢。

cues.en: And I'm like, no, actually it's not.
cues.zh: 我回答说：不，其实不是。

cues.en: It's not, I've never meant to suggest that what's plaguing the country.
cues.zh: 真的不是，我从来没想过要把困扰这个国家的问题归咎于哲学家太多。

cues.en: are too many philosophers.

cues.en: That's not the way to think about it.
cues.zh: 我们需要的是更多能够保持冷静、理解

cues.en: mechanics of fabricating steel.

cues.en: uh, logic and reasoning and Aristotle and Nietzsche and Descartes and Kant.
cues.zh: 呃，逻辑与推理，还有亚里士多德、尼采、笛卡尔和康德。

cues.en: And like, why does it have to be one or the other?
cues.zh: 为什么非得二选一呢？

cues.en: You know, that, that I think that's what I meant by, I think we're going to have to reimagine education because we're like
cues.zh: 你知道，我想说的就是，我们得重新思考教育体系，因为我们现在

cues.zh: 被困在两种观念的牢笼里，要么这个太多，要么那个太少。

cues.zh: 所以我们必须摒弃其中一些东西。

cues.zh: 为什么我们还在谈论失业率，好像它真的很重要似的？

cues.zh: 你知道，那个尼克·埃伯斯塔德，就是写《没有工作的人》那本书的那位，他很有说服力地指出，很难

cues.zh: 找到比失业人数更没有意义的统计数据了。

cues.zh: 那是大萧条时期留下的产物。

cues.zh: 因为在那个年代...

cues.zh: 如果有1200万人失业，你依然可以创造就业岗位，那些人也会去接受。

cues.en: Is it safe to buy and drive salvage cars?
cues.zh: 购买并驾驶事故车安全吗？

cues.en: Uh, can be.
cues.zh: 呃，有可能安全。

cues.en: The crazy thing I've learned by doing this, there are so many corners you can cut.
cues.zh: 通过做这件事我发现，其实有很多可以省钱的办法。

cues.en: So when you buy a salvaged title car, you could get a car better than factory.
cues.zh: 所以当你购买一辆事故车时，甚至可能得到一辆比原厂车还好的车。

cues.en: You get a car that somebody cut a gazillion corners on that is absolutely not safe to drive.
cues.zh: 你买到的其实是有人为节省成本而大打折扣的车，开起来根本不安全。

cues.en: Absolutely not.
cues.zh: 绝对不行。

cues.en: How do you know?
cues.zh: 你怎么知道的？

cues.en: Because I'm on Facebook marketplace and I'm like, well, that's a really good deal.
cues.zh: 因为我会在脸书市场上看车，当时觉得那价格实在很划算。

cues.en: And then I see salvage.
cues.zh: 然后我才看到上面写着是事故车。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 对。

cues.en: But it looks awesome and it's half the price.
cues.zh: 但它看起来很棒，价格还只有正常车的一半。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 没错。

cues.en: I mean, if I'm just looking to.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，如果我只是想……

cues.en: mob around in the city.
cues.zh: 在城里随便转转的话。

cues.en: Like that, that's cool.
cues.zh: 那样的话，倒也挺不错。

cues.en: For sure.
cues.zh: 当然了。

cues.en: Yeah.
cues.zh: 是的。

cues.en: I mean, I think, I think that's why salvage cars are so cheap is because there's that unknown.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，我觉得残值车之所以这么便宜，就是因为存在那些未知因素。

cues.en: There's that risk.
cues.zh: 也就是有那种风险。

cues.en: I think the big thing with a salvage title car is if you can find photos of the accident, right?
cues.zh: 我认为，对于带有残值车证的汽车来说，关键在于能否找到事故的照片，对吧？

cues.en: If you can find what happened and then also when did it happen?
cues.zh: 如果能知道发生了什么，还能知道是何时发生的？

cues.en: If you're buying a car and the accident happened three months ago and it just got repaired, you have no idea.
cues.zh: 如果你要买一辆车，而事故是在三个月前发生的，而且车才刚修好，那你根本无从知晓情况。

cues.en: Whereas like my 430 Scud.
cues.zh: 而我那辆430 Scud就是如此。

cues.en: That was a salvage.
cues.zh: 那也是辆残值车。

cues.en: This was a salvage.
cues.zh: 这辆也是残值车。

cues.en: This event was a roadster.
cues.zh: 这辆车是跑车款。

cues.en: Now, those cars, the accident had happened four, five, six years ago.
cues.zh: 至于那些车，事故发生在四五六年前了。

cues.en: You could see it on the Carfax.
cues.zh: 在Carfax上就能看到相关信息。

cues.en: Let's say, for example, it had 10,000 miles on it, and now the car has 17,000 miles on it.
cues.zh: 比如说，这辆车原本的里程数是10,000英里，现在则变成了17,000英里。

cues.en: You know, there's that history, right?
cues.zh: 你知道的，上面会有相关的历史记录，对吧？

cues.en: You can look back.
cues.zh: 可以回溯查看。

cues.en: You can see, like, oh, this car has been driven a lot.
cues.zh: 就能看出，哦，这辆车已经被开了很多公里了。

cues.en: It happened a number of years ago.
cues.zh: 那件事是多年前发生的。

cues.en: Here's photos of the accident.
cues.zh: 这是事故的照片。

cues.en: So it's really a case-by-case basis, and there's never a guarantee.
cues.zh: 所以真的得逐案处理，根本没法保证什么。

cues.en: Obviously an inspection, right?
cues.zh: 显然需要进行检查，对吧？

cues.en: You can get a PPI, somebody who knows what to look for.
cues.zh: 可以找懂行的人来做车辆状况检查。

cues.en: You know, frame damage is obviously the most important thing that you're looking for.
cues.zh: 你知道的，车架损坏显然是最需要重点检查的。

cues.en: Not always easy to know for sure, but that's why they're cheap, you know?
cues.zh: 虽然并不总是能确定，但正因如此这类检查才价格便宜，你懂的吧？

cues.zh: 而且它的价值暴涨了。

cues.zh: 你当时以多少钱卖的Countach，为什么卖？

cues.en: So I sold the Countach for $565,000.
cues.zh: 我以565,000美元卖掉了那辆Countach。

cues.en: I bought that car for $450, $475, somewhere in there.
cues.zh: 我当初买它的价格大概在450美元到475美元左右。

cues.en: So, you know, I probably pocketed around $100,000, drove it across the country, filmed a lot of cool videos.
cues.zh: 所以，我大概赚了10万美元左右，开着它跑遍了全国，还拍了很多很酷的视频。

cues.en: But the main reason I sold it, though, is it was incredible to look at.
cues.zh: 不过我卖它的最主要原因，还是因为它看起来太棒了。

cues.en: It was just the coolest car.
cues.zh: 那真的是最酷的车。

cues.en: It was triple white, big old wing.
cues.zh: 它是三色白色搭配，还有巨大的尾翼。

cues.en: I mean, every single Lamborghini that exists now looks the way it does because of the Countach.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，现在市面上所有的兰博基尼，都是因为Countach才变成现在这个样子的。

cues.en: But it was very hard to use.
cues.zh: 不过它实际驾驶起来非常困难。

cues.en: It was very hard to drive.
cues.zh: 开这辆车非常困难。

cues.en: I didn't want to drive it in extreme heat because kind of what happened to the Gallardo.
cues.zh: 我不想在极端高温下驾驶它，毕竟加利亚多就出现过那种情况。

cues.en: I felt like that might happen to the Countach.
cues.zh: 我觉得康塔奇也可能遭遇同样的问题。

cues.en: Didn't want to drive it in the wintertime.
cues.zh: 我也不想在冬天驾驶它。

cues.en: Didn't want to drive it in the snow.
cues.zh: 更不想在雪地里开它。

cues.en: It was an investment grade car.
cues.zh: 这是一辆具备投资价值的汽车。

cues.en: So I felt like, you know, the spring and the fall, I could drive it.
cues.zh: 所以我觉得，春天和秋天应该可以驾驶它。

cues.en: And then even when I did drive it, you know, I wasn't going to take it on a road trip.
cues.zh: 即便真的开了，我也不会带它去长途旅行。

cues.en: I had all this money tied up in it.
cues.zh: 我所有的钱都投入在这辆车上了。

cues.en: And it just felt like, you know, YouTube is not only my business, but it's also my passion.
cues.zh: 而且我觉得，YouTube不仅是我的事业，也是我的爱好。

cues.en: And being able to take that money and do other things.
cues.zh: 能把那些钱用来做其他事情，

cues.en: felt like the better option.
cues.zh: 似乎是更好的选择。

cues.en: I also had a Koenigsegg at the time and I had payments and I wanted to finish the Batcave.
cues.zh: 那段时间我也有辆科尼赛克，还要还车贷，同时还想把蝙蝠洞项目做完。

cues.en: And so I actually sold the Countach for 565.
cues.zh: 于是我最终以565的价格卖掉了那辆Countach。

cues.en: I took 300,000-ish of that and I finished the Batcave, which I think is the coolest thing in this entire house.
cues.zh: 我拿出了大约30万，用它完成了蝙蝠洞项目，我觉得这是这整栋房子里最酷的东西。

cues.en: Things that I'm known for.
cues.zh: 这些也是我出名的原因。

cues.en: I mean, the videos did amazing on it.
cues.zh: 我的意思是，相关视频的播放效果非常好。

cues.en: Like there was a fantastic ROI, you know, and it's something I really wanted to finish.
cues.zh: 回报率极高，这是我真心想完成的项目。

cues.en: It's enhanced the value of this house.
cues.zh: 它提升了这栋房子的价值。

cues.en: significantly.
cues.zh: 提升幅度相当大。

cues.en: And then I took the rest of the money and I was able to kind of give me some room to make Koenigsegg payments while also investing in
cues.zh: 剩下的钱让我有了一定的余力，既能继续偿还科尼赛克的车贷，又能用于

cues.en: the channel, other projects, et cetera, et cetera.
cues.zh: 频道运营、其他项目等等。

cues.zh: 那辆车现在的价值是多少？

cues.en: You know, it's crazy.
cues.zh: 你知道，高得离谱。

cues.zh: Countach的售价确实上涨了，但涨幅没有Mercy那么大。

cues.en: They've not gone up like the 2RS we were talking about.
cues.zh: 它们的价格也没有我们之前谈过的2RS那么高。

cues.zh: 458系列的售价同样没有出现大幅上涨。

cues.en: My car was a nice car, but it wasn't the car, right?
cues.zh: 我的车本来也挺不错的，但它算不上最顶级的车型，对吧？

cues.zh: Countach是最好搞清楚的车型之一，因为它的生产时间大概从1974年持续到1991年左右。

cues.en: So, and there's so many different iterations.
cues.zh: 而且它的版本非常多。

cues.zh: 有燃油喷射版的，也有化油器版的，还有加装侧裙的款式。

cues.en: Like there's just so many different factors and like the carbureted round body, like 1985 cars are the cars to have.
cues.zh: 影响因素实在太多了，像那种1985年款的圆形车身车型才是值得拥有的。

cues.en: And they're worth way more than my car, which was an 87 Quattro valve.
cues.zh: 而且它们的价值远远高于我的车，我的车是1987年的Quattro valve款。

cues.en: Yeah, my car's probably, I'm guessing around $650, $700 is what it would be worth now.
cues.zh: 没错，我估计我的车现在大概值650到700美元左右。

cues.zh: 那要怎么判断是直接用现金买车还是选择贷款购车呢？

cues.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我觉得关键因素在于我银行账户里有多少钱，对吧？

cues.zh: 这在很大程度上取决于车型本身，对吧？

cues.en: you know, something like the M4, I think I paid 65 for that car.
cues.zh: 像M4这种车，我记得当时买它花了65万。

cues.en: Sometimes it's just easier to not finance a car.
cues.zh: 有时候不选择贷款买车反而更简单。

cues.zh: 直接汇款、拿到车辆所有权证、完成注册，然后继续过自己的生活，这样不是更简单吗？

cues.en: Whereas other times it's like, you know, like the Temerario, that car's financed, right?
cues.zh: 不过有时候也会像Temerario那辆车那样，是需要贷款购买的，对吧？

cues.zh: 剩下的25万我会用来投资其他项目。

cues.zh: 所以说，很多事情其实都取决于时机。

cues.zh: 拥有这么多超级跑车要花多少成本？

cues.zh: 比如保险、燃油和保养费用。

cues.zh: 简直不可思议。

cues.zh: 保险费用其实不算高。

cues.en: It really isn't.
cues.zh: 真的不算高。

cues.en: That's not bad at all.
cues.zh: 这其实还不错。

cues.zh: 还有那辆Strato，同样有贷款。

cues.zh: 我们不是问过他谁最不擅长理财吗？

cues.zh: 他就是，呃，斯特拉德曼。

cues.en: I'm like, dude, throwing stones from a glass house.
cues.zh: 我说，伙计，这简直就是住在玻璃房子里还扔石头的人。
